document.content:
Commitment sprint: regional capacity checkpoint

HelixWorks is targeting a 12-month extension plus a stepped capacity uplift across EU and APAC. Primary asks: predictable reserved EU capacity, APAC burst for Black Friday-like spikes, and private key management for logs. SE will run benchmarks; AE to deliver updated quote and term sheet.
Meeting header: 2025-11-28 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Ethan Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Alvarez (Redwood SE), Jordan Blake (HelixWorks Head of ML), Priya Suresh (Infra Lead), Tom Warren (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto): HelixWorks wants to lock pricing for 12 months, add eu capacity and an apac burst lane; wants KMS + VPC controls; legal to review by mid-December.

Topics: capacity uplift, region onboarding, contract extension, security / KMS, benchmarks.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll just run through current usage, proposed uplift and timeline. Jordan, do you want to kick with where you are on usage this quarter?
[00:20] Jordan: Yeah sure, so right now we're averaging about 1.8 million tokens a day on the hosted API, peaks hitting around 4.2M on heavy retrieval windows. Our EU traffic is growing — about 28% month over month — so the latency is starting to matter. We're seeing p95 climb into the 380 to 420ms range for some of our longer contexts.
[00:45] Maya: ok, and that's with your current prefix cache settings? Is KV cache enabled for most routes?
[00:52] Jordan: We have some prefix cache, yeah — but it's spotty; a lot of the longer conversations don't hit the cache. And for EU specifically we get the cross-region hop to us-west which adds 60 to 90ms sometimes.
[01:10] Ethan: Got it. Priya, from infra side, what's your ask for regional nodes? Are you looking for reserved capacity in eu-west or a hybrid reserved + burst?
[01:25] Priya: Hybrid. We need predictable baseline for inference — think 2x of our current p50 throughput in EU — plus an APAC burst pool we can consume on demand for campaigns. Ideally reserved eu-west nodes with a burst policy to fallback to hosted or to apac when needed.
[01:45] Tom: Quick procurement note — if there's a one-time setup or private hosting fee that needs capital approval, we need to understand that by the 10th of December. Otherwise we can't commit to invoices before January.
[02:00] Ethan: Makes sense. On the commercial side we can propose a 12-month extension with a stepped reserve: baseline reserved in eu-west, and a negotiated burst pool in ap-southeast. We can show pricing with and without an early payment discount.
[02:20] Jordan: Also we need KMS integration. We can't have keys with you; actually we need customer-managed keys for any logs or model payloads stored.
[02:30] Maya: to clarify, you're asking for customer-managed KMS for the control plane logs / audit trail, or for token encryption at rest?
[02:40] Jordan: Both ideally. At minimum KMS for audit logs and for S3 dumps; tokenization data should be treated as sensitive.
[02:50] Ethan: Understood. We support CMK via our KMS integration for Private and Dedicated customers, though for Hosted there are constraints. I'll flag that — Maya can add detail on the VPC and key flow.
[03:05] Maya: Yeah, for Dedicated we can offer a VPC peering setup and customer-managed CMK. We do need to run an onboarding checklist though — network CIDR, egress rules, and certs. Some customers also ask for HSM-backed keys; that needs a special ops ticket.
[03:25] Priya: HSM would be preferred but we can start with CMK. What's the audit retention window for logs if we enable that?
[03:33] Ethan: Default is 90 days in the console, longer retention is an add-on. We can include extended retention in the quote.
[03:40] Jordan: On benchmarking, we want a reproducible harness. We'll provide a sample prompt set (about 3k prompts) that represent real sessions, avg context 1,800 tokens, 95th percentile target under 300ms for EU.
[03:57] Maya: Ok we'll run the harness in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1. Couple of caveats: cold starts on quantized checkpoints can add ~50-120ms depending on the model, and if KV cache isn't primed you'd see higher tails. Also some of our kernel paths differ on older GPUs which can change throughput.
[04:20] Jordan: Understood. We can do a warm-up priming stage. We just need the numbers and the raw logs.
[04:30] Ethan: Good. Tom, about procurement dates — you mentioned needing sign-off by the 10th — is that for purchase order or for terms?
[04:38] Tom: PO. We need commercial terms by the 3rd so we can get legal review and issue the PO on the 10th. If we miss that, budget moves to next quarter.
[04:48] Ethan: We'll get the commercial by the 3rd then.
[04:52] [05:00] Speaker 3 (crosstalk): um just to highlight, we should also include a failover policy — if the EU pool is saturated, route to the lowest-cost compatible variant, is that something Redwood supports?
[05:15] Maya: Yes, smart routing is configurable — you can set policies: latency-first, cost-first, or capacity-fallback. In practice we often do latency-first with a cost cap. The fallback can go to a smaller quantized variant or to hosted fallback.
[05:30] Jordan: Any impact to model quality when falling back to quantized variants? We can't have hallucinations increase during bursts.
[05:39] Maya: There is a small delta — usually in edge-case token generation. Our Optimize recommendations can set thresholds and quality hooks; we can monitor a prompt subset and auto-fail back if quality regresses.
[05:55] Priya: Also, what about data residency — EU logs must stay in eu-west. If we send logs to your console, can they be partitioned per region?
[06:06] Ethan: Yep — for Dedicated we can keep logs and metrics in region. For Hosted we typically centralize but we can enable regional retention for an enterprise contract. We'll note that in the doc.
[06:20] Tom: Legal will want SOC2 and ISO evidence. Do you have a SOC2 report we can share?
[06:27] Ethan: Yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation; I'll attach the latest reports.
[06:33] Jordan: One more technical: we run a lot of long-context gen with KV cache; one of the earlier transcripts had Redwood's docs referencing KV cache behavior — sometimes transcribed as K-V cash in our notes — hah. When you run the benchmark include both primed and unprimed cache runs.
[06:50] Maya: absolutely. We'll run cold start, warm primed cache, and sustained throughput. Also include a run that simulates your 10-second burst pattern.
[07:02] Ethan: On pricing we can show three options: (A) 12-month term with reserved EU nodes + APAC burst (B) 24-month with larger discount (C) 12-month with a credit-backed burst pool. Any preference?
[07:18] Priya: Option A to start, provision for a mid-term review after 90 days. We may lock in (B) if the numbers look good post-benchmark.
[07:28] Tom: Option A is easiest to approve from finance if the up-front isn't too large. We need net-30 terms ideally.
[07:35] Ethan: We can do net-30 for enterprise contracts. We'll include the payment terms in the quote.
[07:42] Jordan: For the benchmark data, can you give raw token-level logs? We'll scrub as needed but need detail for our telemetry team.
[07:50] Maya: Yes, we can provide structured logs with request/response times and token counts. We'll need an ingestion location; we can put an S3 bucket behind your KMS if you prefer.
[08:02] Jordan: Good, we'll confirm bucket details.
[08:08] [08:30] Ethan: Ok recap — items: AE to send commercial with Option A pricing and extended retention add-on, SE to run benchmark in EU+APAC using the HelixWorks prompt set and return results, customer to share prompts and procurement timeline. Any other blockers?
[08:45] Priya: One small thing — can we get an ops contact for the VPC handshake? We need someone to test peering flows in a staging window.
[08:54] Maya: I'll be primary for handshake, and I'll include ops-eng (infra-oncall) in the ticket.
[09:02] Tom: Legal will ping Ethan for a standard enterprise SOW; they usually want indemnity language clarified.
[09:09] Ethan: We'll push the SOW draft with the quote.
[09:14] Jordan: timeline — can we aim to have benchmarks done and a go/no-go decision by Dec 12th? That's when our engineering sprint planning lands.
[09:22] Ethan: Dec 12th is doable if we get the prompts and the PO timeline holds. We'll put the dates in the action items.
[09:30] Priya: Awesome. A few handwritten notes: extended retention, CMK, baseline 2x p50 in eu, APAC burst pool 3x peak for campaigns.
[09:45] Maya: Noted. I'll include the configuration matrix in the benchmark ticket.
[09:51] Ethan: Anything else before we close?
[09:55] Jordan: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[10:00] Ethan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the quote and ticket links. Meeting end.

Post-meeting references: deck link (shared) - https://app.redwood.example/sales/decks/hlx-q4-commitment.pdf; benchmark runbook (to be attached); SOC2 report link: sas-2025-soc2.pdf (attached).

document.content:
CelestiaGrid partner intro + integration framing

Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-28 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Rohan (CelestiaGrid Head of Cloud), Priya (CelestiaGrid Lead Platform Eng), Sam (CelestiaGrid VP Partnerships)
Links shared: partner-onboarding.pdf (Redwood), quick-bench-template.xlsx (SE), celestiagrid-network-diagram-v1.png (customer)

Summary: Quick partner intro between Redwood Inference and CelestiaGrid to scope initial integration patterns (hosted onramp vs private VPC offering), discuss latency/cost tradeoffs, and identify next steps for a pilot. High-level security posture checked (SOC2, SSO, KMS) and initial perf benchmarking plan agreed.

00:00 Maya Ortiz: uh okay everyone we can maybe start, um thanks for joining — i'm maya ortiz from redwood inference, i'm the account lead on partnerships.
00:10 Rohan Iyer: hey maya, thanks. sam, priya on this end. short agenda is fine for us — we want to understand how you see integration with a channel partner like celestiagrid.
00:22 Maya Ortiz: perfect. daniel will jump in on the technical bits — daniel do you want to give a 5 min run through of the runtime and where partners plug in?
00:30 Daniel Wu: yeah, sure. hi everyone, daniel wu, solutions eng. so at a high level redwood's serving runtime is a gpu-optimized engine, supports streaming, function-calls, embeddings, rerank — common stuff. for partners we have three patterns: 1) hosted api where celestiagrid could resell or route, 2) dedicated pools for reserved capacity, and 3) private deployment — vpc or on-prem. each has slightly different integration surface.
00:53 Priya Menon: when you say private deployment, is that private control plane or do you ship a package we host?
01:01 Daniel Wu: good q. both options exist — private control plane where you manage the network and keys, or an on-prem package that we provide images for. most partners start with private vpc peering or private link for low latency.
01:15 Sam Carter: and from partnership layer — interested in how billing and quotas are visible. we usually need tenant separation and partner-level reporting.
01:24 Maya Ortiz: we expose usage and token-level cost breakdowns in the console; for reseller partners we can provide partner-aggregated reporting and per-tenant dashboards. the marketplace/reseller contract can include pass-through billing or invoiced resale.
01:36 Rohan Iyer: great. i'm curious about the perf characteristics — what latency can we expect for a 2k token chat request? and how will that change with batching?
01:45 Daniel Wu: so latency depends on model family, sequence length, and quantization. rough ballpark: a 2k token generation on a modern 80GB-class GPU with optimized kernels can be mid-100s ms to low seconds depending on decode strategy. continuous batching reduces cost but increases tail latency; we have autoscaling and burst capacity to keep p95s within targets.
02:08 Priya Menon: can we pin models? sometimes our customers need model versioning and pinned rollouts for compliance.
02:15 Daniel Wu: yes, pinning by model version is first-class. rollouts support canary and A/B, and there's automatic fallback to lighter quantized variants if a node is saturated. note: fallback changes output distribution so we flag regressions in the optimize/quality monitor.
02:34 Maya Ortiz: quick note on security — redwood supports SSO/SAML, RBAC, SOC2 attestation, and KMS integration. audit logs are retained per enterprise plan; we can discuss retention windows in the MOU.
02:45 Sam Carter: that's helpful — compliance is a big check for our customers in regulated finance.
02:51 Rohan Iyer: network topology question: are you open to direct vpc peering or would you prefer private link? our infra team prefers peering for lower jitter.
03:01 Daniel Wu: both supported; peering is lower latency but needs routing setup. private link simplifies support and cross-account routing. either way we do NAT/external egress minimization and endpoint whitelisting.
03:16 Priya Menon: any gotchas on MTU or tcp tune for kv cache traffic? we run heavy kv cache reads for long-context chat.
03:25 Daniel Wu: KV cache is internal to the runtime; if you host the runtime on your infra the KV traffic is local. for hosted/reseller we use a prefix cache and edge-layer to minimize cross-region fetches — but yes, we should validate MTU and path MTU because mishandled fragmentation can spike latency.
03:42 Maya Ortiz: i'd like to pause and make sure we surface success criteria — sam/rohan what would a successful pilot look like in 8 weeks?
03:52 Sam Carter: success for us: validated latency under 500 ms p95 on a 512-token gen workload for our east-coast customers, cost per 1k tokens estimate within 20% of your hosted benchmark, and a documented network/topology pattern.
04:08 Rohan Iyer: and we need an SLO doc we can show to enterprise prospects — e.g., targeted p95 and failover behavior across regions.
04:15 Maya Ortiz: ok noted. daniel — is the bench template you mentioned earlier something we can run on celestiagrid infra?
04:23 Daniel Wu: yes, we have quick-bench-template.xlsx — it lists model configs, sequence lengths, tokenization settings. we can run it with a small client harness we share. proposed approach: run baseline on 1 GPU instance, then on a 4-node cluster to observe scaling and batching impact.
04:41 Priya Menon: timeline wise we can provision a pilot cluster in one of our edge regions in ~2 weeks if we get the config.
04:49 Maya Ortiz: perfect — we will send config by Tue.
05:00 [timestamp skipped ahead]
08:12 Rohan Iyer: question on data residency — some customers require EU-only residency plus separate audit logs. how do you solve for region isolation?
08:22 Daniel Wu: region isolation is supported: hosted can provide region-restricted endpoints, dedicated pools can be provisioned in eu-west, and private on-prem removes cloud residency concerns. audit log retention can be set per tenant in dedicated/private plans.
08:40 Priya Menon: do you have HSM integration for keys?
08:44 Maya Ortiz: yes — KMS/HSM integrations are available for enterprise and private deployments. we can surface a list of supported KMS providers.
08:53 Sam Carter: any existing partners doing similar reseller integrations so we can see a reference flow?
09:00 Maya Ortiz: we have a few — i'll share anonymized diagrams and a short partner case study.
09:05 Priya Menon: are there known model compatibility quirks with certain GPUs (like older A100 variants or patched drivers)? we've seen issues with kernel mismatches.
09:14 Daniel Wu: yeah, that's real — driver/kernel combo matters. our runtime auto-selects kernels but older drivers cause fallbacks increasing latency. in pilot we'll run a quick driver/stack check.
09:28 Rohan Iyer: on the topic of pricing — can you give a sense of reserved vs burst pricing? our customers vary.
09:35 Maya Ortiz: reserved capacity is contracted monthly with committed throughput, giving a discount vs hosted on-demand. burst capacity allows short-term usage above commit at a premium. for partners we can structure revenue share and pass-through or resell arrangements.
09:49 Rohan Iyer: revenue share details later but good to know pricing flex.
09:53 [15:00 marker - mid call technical dive]
15:02 Daniel Wu: diving deeper: batching strategy — we deploy continuous batching with dynamic batching windows tuned to maintain latency SLOs. for throughput-heavy workloads we recommend batching size tuned to traffic patterns; for chat low-latency workloads we keep small micro-batches and use prefixed KV caching.
15:26 Priya Menon: do you support prefix caching where we pre-warm user sessions?
15:30 Daniel Wu: yes we support prefix and kv caching; we can pre-warm popular prefixes. the caching semantics are configurable per-tenant.
15:40 Rohan Iyer: any automated fallback policies if a model variant becomes unhealthy? we need graceful degradation not complete outage.
15:46 Daniel Wu: built-in fallbacks to quantized or smaller family models, plus region fallback. the console flags quality regressions and can trigger rollback.
16:00 Priya Menon: regarding logs — what do you send back in audit logs? we need obfuscated PII; logs should show request metadata not raw content.
16:09 Maya Ortiz: default logs include request id, model, tokens, latency, error codes. content redaction is supported and we can integrate protocols to scrub or not store payloads depending on plan.
16:22 Sam Carter: ok that answers our compliance stack.
16:28 [crosstalk briefly]
20:30 Maya Ortiz: let's talk pilot scope. recommended minimal pilot: one east-coast region cluster (4 GPUs), run bench for 512 and 2k token profiles, latency and cost capture, and a simple end-to-end flow with your customer identity layer. does that sound realistic?
20:44 Priya Menon: yes, sounds good. we will need a runbook for ops and escalation.
20:50 Daniel Wu: we'll include runbook and monitoring hooks; we can send datadog/grafana dashboards or provide metrics via our console's tracing hooks.
21:01 Rohan Iyer: how invasive is the integration? do we need to modify our networking heavily?
21:07 Daniel Wu: minimal for private link; heavier for peering (routing changes). we avoid opening public NAT paths by setting up dedicated endpoints.
21:17 Sam Carter: for a channel agreement — what's typically the timeline from pilot to go-live? 3 months?
21:24 Maya Ortiz: typical is 8-12 weeks from pilot start to initial go-live, depending on integrations, compliance checks, and contract. some go faster.
21:33 Priya Menon: any suggestion for benchmarks we should run to prove capacity planning?
21:38 Daniel Wu: run steady-state throughput tests at 60-80% target utilization, ramp tests, and sustained long-context sessions to exercise KV evaporation. quick-bench-template includes these scenarios.
21:52 Rohan Iyer: can you run a small smoke test against our infra next week? we can share a bastion and credentials with limited scope.
21:59 Daniel Wu: yes — we'll need an infra contact and an isolation VPC; priya?
22:05 Priya Menon: i'll coordinate.
22:10 Maya Ortiz: i'll put that in the next steps.
22:20 [longer silence as notes are taken]
30:05 Sam Carter: question on risk: what happens if a model update causes quality regressions for our customers mid-rollout — what's your rollback process?
30:16 Daniel Wu: we have auto rollback triggers tied to quality monitors; canary percent and automated rollback if eval metrics drop. we also keep previous versions deployable so rollback is typically minutes.
30:30 Priya Menon: and change logging for audits?
30:33 Maya Ortiz: every rollout is recorded with metadata and release notes, and enterprise customers can require approval gates.
30:40 Rohan Iyer: any pre-existing OCI or helm charts for on-prem?
30:45 Daniel Wu: yes, we provide helm charts and k8s manifests for private installs. we'll share the repo access in the follow-up.
30:55 Priya Menon: driver matrix please.
31:00 Daniel Wu: yep will include driver/kernel matrix in the tech pack.
35:12 Maya Ortiz: (recap) ok action items: daniel builds perf test plan, maya sends MOU and partner docs, priya shares infra diagram. timeline target — kick pilot first week of june, run 2-4 week bench, then sync.
35:34 Rohan Iyer: sounds good. any red flags from you folks at redwood?
35:40 Daniel Wu: the main thing is ensuring the pilot gpu shapes match our performance assumptions and the driver stack is compatible. once that's validated all else is integration work.
35:52 Sam Carter: we'll prioritize verifying driver/stack and give you a point of contact.
36:00 Maya Ortiz: for the partner commercial model, we propose a simple revenue share for the first 6 months and then a committed reserved capacity conversation — i'll include options in the MOU.
36:12 Rohan Iyer: ok that's fine.
36:16 Priya Menon: one final tech nuance — we have a multi-tenant overlay in celestiagrid that enforces network isolation. will that complicate key exchange?
36:26 Daniel Wu: we can integrate KMS per tenant or use a partner key-wrap flow; we'll detail options.
36:35 Maya Ortiz: great. any other questions?
36:40 [pause]
40:02 Sam Carter: none from me. looking forward to the technical deep dive.
40:10 Maya Ortiz: next steps again: send MOU + tech pack (Maya), perf plan (Daniel), infra diag (Priya). schedule deep dive for week of Jun 7.
40:25 Rohan Iyer: we'll aim to have infra ready by Jun 2.
40:31 Priya Menon: agreed.
40:35 Maya Ortiz: okay i'll follow up with calendar invite and share the bench template and runbook links.
40:42 Daniel Wu: i'll prep the perf harness and a checklist for driver validations.
40:50 Sam Carter: thanks everyone.
40:54 Maya Ortiz: thanks — we'll close out here.

Action items (as captured in chat): Daniel Wu: perf test plan; Maya Ortiz: partner MOU + pricing; Priya Menon: infra diagram; Maya to send follow-up invite and links.

End of transcript.

document.content:
Neptune Retail - Tokenflow orientation and hosting discussion

Intro discovery focused on p95 latency targets for streaming recommendations, expected concurrency, token/sec profiling with sample payloads, and hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs. Identified security requirements (SSO, KMS, audit logs) and agreed to run a short token/sec benchmark and a sample streaming test. Next steps: benchmark results, security pack, and pricing sketch.
Ethan Ross: run token/sec and streaming trial with Neptune's 2 sample scenarios using 8k context prompt by 2026-03-03
Samira Velez: share SOC2 report, SSO/SAML integration guide, and audit-log retention options by 2026-02-27
Maya Chen: prepare hosted vs dedicated cost comparison with burst capacity assumptions by 2026-03-05
Jonah Ortiz: provide sample traffic pattern (qps, typical session length, tokens per session) and sample prompts by 2026-02-28
Redwood to run token/sec benchmark with Neptune sample payload and share results (Ethan) - target 2026-03-03
Send SOC2 + security whitepaper and KMS integration notes (Samira) - target 2026-02-27
Follow-up pricing sketch for hosted vs dedicated with committed capacity scenarios (Maya) - target 2026-03-05
Schedule 1-hour deep dive on private deployment network topology if needed (Lisa to confirm)
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25 16:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Samira (Redwood CSM), Lisa (Neptune CTO), Jonah (Neptune SRE), Priya (Neptune ML) ...

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. quick agenda — understand your production p95 goals, concurrency, streaming behavior and whether hosted or dedicated/private is a better fit.
[00:15] Lisa Park: Thanks Maya, yeah we want to see if Redwood can hit our p95 under streaming recommendations. Right now our internal service sits around 120 ms p95 for small-ish prompts but when we go to 8k context and multi-turn recommender streaming it jumps.
[00:33] Ethan Ross: got it. can you give ballpark concurrency? are you expecting steady 100 concurrent streams or bursts to 2k?
[00:41] Jonah Ortiz: Typical desktop interactive is like 30-50 concurrent during peak, mobile maybe another 50, but we have flash sale events where we see spikes to maybe 1,500 concurrent for a few minutes.
[00:57] Priya Kapoor: and session length: average session is 3-5 turns, tokens per turn 80-250, but our recommender sometimes generates 600-1,200 tokens in a follow-up. so tokens/sec matters a lot.
[01:15] Maya Chen: ok so two modes: steady low-mid concurrency with sporadic high-burst traffic. With Redwood hosted you get elastic capacity but cost rises during those spikes; Dedicated gives reserved pools and more predictable latency, Private/VPC gives you network control.
[01:34] Lisa Park: Our compliance team will want SSO and KMS integration, plus audit logs retained for 365 days. Is that supported across all modes?
[01:44] Samira Velez: yes, SSO/SAML and audit logs are available. KMS integration is supported in Private and Dedicated; hosted supports customer-managed keys via our KMS partner integration but there are some caveats around key rotation timelines — we can share docs.
[01:59] Jonah Ortiz: another question - what p95 can we expect for streaming token-by-token? We need under 300 ms p95 for per-token latency for our interactive flows, otherwise UX degrades.
[02:12] Ethan Ross: streaming per-token p95 is influenced by model variant, batch window, and whether you use KV cache warm paths. With a medium sized model and continuous batching tuned for low-latency, we've seen 150-250 ms per-token p95 on dedicated pools for 2k token contexts. On hosted it depends on noisy neighbors and routing config; we usually set a latency SLO route for premium customers.
[02:38] Lisa Park: can you explain noisy neighbor mitigation?
[02:41] Ethan Ross: sure — we do isolation via reserved slots and request coalescing, and route by policy. dedicated capacity gives you private GPU pools; hosted has routing tiers and preemptible capacity for cheaper routes but premium routing pins to non-preemptible hardware. sometimes the transcriber misses a term — we call it prefix/KV cache but you might see it as K-V cash in notes.
[03:02] Jonah Ortiz: haha noted. for our bursts, we really worry about cold-starts causing p95 spikes. how do you avoid long tail when scaling from zero-to-1500?
[03:11] Oliver Wang (Redwood): two levers — warm pool (we keep a small standing pool depending on your burst profile) and fast fallback to a lower-cost model family that has compatible outputs. also autoscaling thresholds and a low-latency reserve for verified customers.
[03:29] Maya Chen: and on economics — we recommend pairing caching with a committed capacity plan for Dedicated to reduce unit cost. Redwood Optimize will run suggestions for quantization and batching to hit your cost target while respecting quality.
[03:43] Lisa Park: curious about quantization quality. Priya, do you run evals?
[03:47] Priya Kapoor: yeah we have a small eval harness, we'll want to run Redwood's quantized weights against our test prompts.
[03:52] Maya Chen: perfect — that can be part of the POC.
[03:55] [04:00] Ethan Ross: can I get more details on the two sample scenarios you mentioned in the signup? one is a 6k context recommendation stream, the other is a 2k context conversational assistant used concurrently by mobile and web.
[04:12] Lisa Park: yes — scenario A is batch-like recommender that still streams results (clients expect partials early) — bursty during launches; scenario B is long-running conversational threads with 4-6 turns and mid sized token outputs.
[04:27] Ethan Ross: sounds good. for benchmarking i'd like both sample prompts and a traffic generator with the session distribution — that helps us reproduce tokens/sec and warm/cold patterns.
[04:39] Jonah Ortiz: we can provide a small k6 script and a csv of prompt types. also we'll include percentile distributions for tokens per response.
[04:47] [05:00] Maya Chen: great. on the token/sec numbers — Priya, what throughput do you need?
[05:06] Priya Kapoor: we target about 7k tokens/sec sustained during flash sales across the whole fleet, and peaks maybe 30k tokens/sec for ~2 minutes.
[05:17] Ethan Ross: ok, that's helpful. rough math: with a quantized medium model on Dedicated optimized kernels, a single GPU can do roughly 4-8k tokens/sec depending on prompt shape and sequence length. So sustained 7k could be one or two GPUs with batching, but peaks to 30k would need a burst pool or autoscale across several nodes.
[05:39] Lisa Park: can you show cost difference? we care about predictable invoices.
[05:43] Maya Chen: we will sketch hosted per-token + burst surcharge vs Dedicated reserved capacity pricing and an example with 6-month commit. we'll model burst headroom and warm pools in both.
[05:56] Jonah Ortiz: another aspect — we run in eu-west primarily; do you support region pinning and multi-region failover?
[06:04] Ethan Ross: yes — region routing is supported. we can pin workloads to eu-west for data residency and do multi-region failover with optional cross-region cache replication. there are tradeoffs for failover cold-starts.
[06:18] Lisa Park: security — retention of logs, who has access, can we do RBAC mapping to our Okta groups?
[06:25] Samira Velez: absolutely, SSO with Okta + SCIM + RBAC mapping is supported. audit logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM. retention windows and export cadence are configurable.
[06:39] [06:45] Jonah Ortiz: the SRE team will need a runbook for failovers — do you have sample runbooks?
[06:50] Samira Velez: yes we'll share runbooks and a playbook for invoking failover and model fallback.
[06:57] Ethan Ross: back to perf — I want to call out two knobs: batch window and KV cache reuse. If you have repeated prompts or similar prefix data, cache reuse massively reduces per-token cost and latency. For streaming long outputs, we tune small micro-batches to keep per-token latency low.
[07:20] Priya Kapoor: our recommender often uses a 4k prefix that's reused heavily; that sounds promising.
[07:26] Ethan Ross: then prefix caching should help — we'll validate with your sample set.
[07:30] [07:35] Lisa Park: any SLA for p95 latency?
[07:38] Maya Chen: for Dedicated we can offer SLA-backed latency targets at commit tiers; hosted has standard uptime SLA but tiered latency SLOs for premium accounts. we'll propose an SLA that maps to your 300 ms per-token p95 ask for streaming.
[07:52] Jonah Ortiz: good. about fallback models — do outputs remain functionally equivalent? we can't have recomms that change meaningfully in the middle of a session.
[08:02] Ethan Ross: fallback models are chosen to be architecture-compatible and tested; Quality monitoring flags regressions and we can auto-fallback to previous model versions if score drift detected. we'll include regression tolerance thresholds in the rollout plan.
[08:17] [08:30] Maya Chen: Are there any blockers on procurement or legal?
[08:33] Lisa Park: procurement wants initial 3 month pilot with an exit clause and an NDA addendum for data handling. Legal asked about subprocessor list.
[08:42] Samira Velez: we can provide subprocessor list and a pilot contract template, plus the security pack.
[08:48] Jonah Ortiz: for the POC run — we prefer a short 2-week benchmark with two phases: functional correctness and throughput latency profiling.
[08:56] Ethan Ross: that aligns with our standard flow — phase 1 correctness and evals on quantized models, phase 2 stress tests for tokens/sec and burst scaling.
[09:06] [09:10] Maya Chen: ok i'm going to summarize next steps — Ethan will run benchmarks, Samira will send security docs, Maya will send pricing sketch. Jonah will provide traffic generator. Anything else?
[09:21] Lisa Park: can we get an example of your warm-pool sizing logic?
[09:25] Oliver Wang (Redwood): yes — we'll sketch a warm pool sizing recommendation based on peak percentiles and cold-start SLA you want.
[09:34] Priya Kapoor: and we'll run Redwood's quantized model on our eval set during the POC.
[09:40] [09:45] Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kickoff.
[09:50] Lisa Park: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.

Notes and imperfect bits: occasional transcription mislabels, some technical terms are abbreviated. timestamps approximate.

document.content:
Data ejection & request retention console review - HarborTech Logistics

Walkthrough of Redwood Console request-storage toggles, selective telemetry ejection, PII redaction rules, and policy-driven retention. Customer cares about minimal retained request data, SOC2/KMS, and ability to redact / egress logs to their S3 for audits.
Meeting header: 2026-12-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 47 min | Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Kwan (Redwood Product), Maya Chen (HarborTech CISO), Ethan Park (Platform Eng), Ravi Malhotra (PM), Priya Singh (Legal)

Summary section (auto): quick demo of console toggles for request retention and redaction, discuss legal/ residency, confirm pilot scope and next steps.

00:00 Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, afternoon, morning depending on where you are. quick intros?
00:07 Maya Chen: Maya Chen, CISO at HarborTech. We've got a tight bar for PII retention and need to see redaction end-to-end.
00:12 Ethan Park: Ethan, platform engineering. I'll be the person integrating and running tests.
00:16 Ravi Malhotra: Ravi, product, focus on latency and cost tradeoffs.
00:20 Priya Singh: Priya, legal - here for compliance constraints, data residency notes.
00:24 Lena Ortiz: Great, from Redwood I'm Lena, AE; Samir will do the product deep dive and demo; Jules is on product to answer policy questions.
00:33 Samir Patel: Hi all. We'll show Console toggles: route-level storage, selective ejection, regex redaction, KMS settings, and how Optimize recommends less-retentive configs. This is a working demo so you may see some UI lag.
00:47 Maya Chen: Perfect. high-level ask: we cannot store full request text beyond 7 days for European shipments and some US customers. need to redact account numbers and PII before it lands in logs. Also want proof of deletion for audits.
01:05 Samir Patel: Totally reasonable. Walkthrough: first, request-storage at route level. you can set retention policy per route: none, ephemeral, 7d, 30d, or custom. we'll show ephemeral and selective ejection where we drop full request bodies but keep metadata tokens for billing.
01:25 Samir Patel: (screen share) Console > Apps > HarborTech-pilot > Routes. here's our sample webhook route. Notice the toggle 'Request Storage' — off = store nothing, ephemeral = store for the duration of request processing only, On with retention = full stored logs.
01:42 Ethan Park: Is 'ephemeral' zero copies on disk or just short-lived temp? we need to ensure it never persists to S3.
01:48 Samir Patel: Good question. ephemeral means no long-term object store. The runtime uses in-memory buffers and KV caches for processing, those are not written to durable object storage. We also offer an option 'eject-to-customer-s3' which you control. If it's off, nothing is exported.
02:10 Maya Chen: And encryption? we require customer-managed keys for anything that touches our data.
02:15 Samir Patel: We support KMS integration. Under Settings > Keys you can attach a KMS alias. For hosted, Redwood encrypts at rest with our keys by default, but for Private/Dedicated you can mount your key and we restrict KMS access to the environment. Jules, want to add?
02:28 Jules Kwan: just to be explicit: for Dedicated and Private deployments we can integrate AWS KMS or HSM. For hosted, bring-your-own-key is on the roadmap but available via a managed customer key partner — we can add that to the pilot SOW.
02:40 Priya Singh: We also need immutable audit trail of deletions - auditors want proof that logs were purged.
02:45 Samir Patel: We have an Audit Log feature: deletion events, who performed them, and a tamper-evident record. It can be exported and signed. That lives separate from request storage and is retained per org policy.
02:57 Ravi Malhotra: what about automatic redaction? can we define regexes to scrub credit card or account numbers?
03:05 Samir Patel: Yes, under Policy > Redaction you can create rules. Let's demo.
03:10 Samir Patel: (navigates) Add Rule: name "Acct-number-scrub", scope: routes matching /shipments/*, pattern: "(Acct|Account)[:=]\s?\d{8,12}" - action: replace with [REDACTED]. you can test against sample payloads here.
03:33 Ethan Park: Nice. Does that run client-side before the request is sent to the model or server-side?
03:39 Samir Patel: Server-side in the gateway before persisting or forwarding. we also have pre-send hooks if you want to do client-side scrubbing in the SDK, but policy-driven server redaction is good for safety nets.
03:52 Maya Chen: Are those regexes evaluated at line speed? we cannot add significant latency.
03:57 Samir Patel: They're compiled into optimized matchers; in our tests match+replace adds under 6-12ms median per request for typical payloads. If you have high QPS we recommend batching or moving to the Dedicated pool.
04:14 Ethan Park: And for audit we need to capture pre-redaction hashes so we can prove what existed without storing PII. do you support deterministic hashing or salted digests?
04:23 Samir Patel: Yes - on the same rule you can set 'hash-before-redaction' which computes a SHA-256 digest and stores only the digest in the log. We can also salt per-tenant. That gives you deterministic but irreversible mapping for verification.
04:40 Priya Singh: acceptable if salts are under our control?
04:43 Jules Kwan: For Dedicated/private we can store the salt in your KMS/HSM so only you can verify. For hosted, salts are stored in our secure vault, but enterprise offering includes tenant-controlled salts. We'll note that in SOW.
04:58 Samir Patel: Next, selective telemetry ejection: you can configure sample rate and route filters for telemetry export. For example, export 100% for support routes, 0% for payments. This reduces exposure.
05:15 Ravi Malhotra: how granular? per-route? per-customer? per-user?
05:18 Samir Patel: All three. We have attribute-based policies: route, org, header-based. You can also set dynamic rules via tags.
05:26 Maya Chen: show me an example for European shipments only.
05:29 Samir Patel: Sure - create a policy: condition: request.headers.X-Region == EU || payload.flags.country == "DE|FR|ES"; action: retention = 7d, eject = false, redaction = strict. (applies filter).
05:46 Ethan Park: Great. What about the API? we need to toggle at deployment time from infra as code.
05:52 Samir Patel: There's a management API. Quick curl sample: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/ht/routes/shipments:patch -d '{"retention":"ephemeral","redaction":[{"name":"Acct-number-scrub","hash_before":true}] }' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' We also provide terraform provider for route-level policy.
06:18 Maya Chen: we'll need RBAC - only specific personas can change retention.
06:22 Samir Patel: RBAC is under Settings > Access. Roles: Admin, Security, DevOps, Auditor. You can create custom roles and tie to SSO groups via SCIM.
06:33 Priya Singh: SCIM sync with Okta?
06:36 Samir Patel: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for groups.
06:40 Lena Ortiz: jumping in - quick pause for a real-world constraint: HarborTech wants to keep embeddings off-request but still need similarity search for internal product features. Any options?
06:50 Samir Patel: You can disable embedding storage entirely or route embeddings to a customer-managed vector DB. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization to reduce storage if you need to keep embeddings but want lower cost. For privacy, route embeddings to your own VPC DB.
07:06 Ethan Park: If we route to our VPC DB, does Redwood see them at all?
07:10 Samir Patel: No, if you configure VPC egress and direct streaming to your DB, Redwood's hosted retention can be set to ephemeral and we never persist those vectors. For Dedicated/private it's fully under your network control.
07:22 Maya Chen: show me the logs and audit UI for a deletion event.
07:26 Samir Patel: (navigates) Audit > Actions. here's a sample deletion event: actor: "Ethan Park", action: delete_request_records, target: route/shipments, timestamp, change-id. You can click and download a signed attestment.
07:45 Ethan Park: signed with what?
07:47 Samir Patel: a timestamped signature from our audit service; we also provide a chain-of-custody export. For higher assurance we can arrange attestations backed by HSM keys.
07:58 Priya Singh: For the pilot, we need to run a redaction test where we send 500 sample requests including edge cases and get a post-redaction report. can Redwood do that?
08:07 Samir Patel: yes, we can run a test harness. Ask Ethan to drop the sample payloads in the shared S3/drive. We'll map rules and run the scrub, then produce summary: hits, misses, latency impacts.
08:20 Lena Ortiz: we'll also include a small perf benchmark; Redwood offered to run a 1k QPS simulated run for the shipments route to measure redaction overhead and latencies.
08:28 Ravi Malhotra: cost question: if we choose ephemeral for most routes but onboard Dedicated for high QPS, how does that change unit cost?
08:36 Jules Kwan: Dedicated decouples you from per-token hosted pricing. You get reserved GPU capacity; cost becomes capacity + some per-request overhead. For storage, Dedicated allows you to route to your own object store which lowers hosted storage charges. We'll send a cost model spreadsheet.
08:50 Maya Chen: any gotchas around GDPR deletion requests? we need to prove erasure across backups and caches.
08:57 Samir Patel: We mark deletions in the metadata store and our backup process supports retention-aware scrubbing. For full proof we recommend Dedicated + your KMS salt so only you can map hashed content. We'll include deletion attestations in exports for legal.
09:12 Ethan Park: is there an option to mask in-flight in the SDK so the data never reaches Redwood tokens?
09:18 Samir Patel: yes, client-side masking hooks exist in SDKs. But we recommend defense-in-depth: client mask + server redaction.
09:25 Maya Chen: small note — our legal team will request a network topology showing where logs could flow.
09:30 Lena Ortiz: we'll attach a network flow diagram and the security whitepaper.
09:34 Samir Patel: Also note the Optimize module: it can analyze your call patterns and suggest where to flip retention to ephemeral to save cost with low impact on debugging. it's non-invasive. We'll demo quickly.
09:46 Samir Patel: (Console > Optimize) here's a heatmap: high debug routes in blue, low risk in green. clicking a bucket gives suggested retention flips and estimated monthly savings. you can apply changes directly or run as dry-run.
10:05 Ravi Malhotra: can it auto-apply after approval?
10:08 Samir Patel: There's an approval workflow: proposed change -> security review -> scheduled apply. All audit logged.
10:15 Maya Chen: ok. For pilot success criteria: 1) redaction rules remove PII in 95%+ of sample cases, 2) latencies under 20ms added per request for EU shipments at target QPS, 3) deletion attestations generated for sample sets.
10:30 Lena Ortiz: noted. we'll add those to pilot SOW.
10:35 Priya Singh: need contractual language about inability to reconstitute redacted data and SLAs for deletion.
10:40 Lena Ortiz: we'll loop legal.
10:43 Maya Chen: one off question - the console showed ability to redact JSON keys. can you redact nested JSON fields?
10:49 Samir Patel: yes, policy supports JSON path extraction and redaction by JSONPath (e.g., $.payment.card.number) as well as regex. We'll demo a quick test.
10:59 Samir Patel: (runs live test) sending sample with nested payment.card.number -> redacted to [REDACTED] and digest stored as SHA256. you can see the test result and the matched rule.
11:17 Ethan Park: nice. any known limitations?
11:20 Samir Patel: edge cases: large free-form user text where PII is embedded in natural language can create false negatives; we recommend combining regex + ML-based PII detection. Redwood offers an ML PII model as an add-on for higher recall.
11:35 Maya Chen: add-on pricing?
11:37 Lena Ortiz: we'll include pricing in the follow-up.
11:39 Ravi Malhotra: ok last thing - support model fallbacks. if the primary model is offline and we fallback to a different model, do retention policies follow?
11:46 Samir Patel: policies are route-based and follow the request regardless of model variant. The runtime will honor the policy before model selection.
11:53 Maya Chen: perfect.

Transcript:
[00:00:04] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call — say hi when you can, and we'll move into objective.
[00:00:12] Oliver: Hi all, Oliver here. CTO at Garnet. Thanks.
[00:00:15] Priya: Priya, platform team.
[00:00:18] Marco: Marco — privacy and compliance.
[00:00:20] Leah: Leah, product.
[00:00:24] Sofia: Great. So objective for today is a short ignition: confirm pilot scope, constraints, timeline, and immediate next steps so we can get infra and security checks started. We want a concrete plan for the first two weeks.
[00:00:36] Ravi: I'll also briefly outline how our Dedicated trial environment would look and what the k8s integration surface is.
[00:00:42] Leah: Quick note from product: pilot is customer-facing in-app chat and semantic search via embeddings for our knowledge base. We want the experience to feel snappy.
[00:00:50] Sofia: Great. Do you have any initial latency targets? P95 or p50?
[00:00:55] Leah: Ideally p95 under 250ms for non-streaming generation, embeddings should be under 100ms p95 if possible. Those are aspirational.
[00:01:03] Ravi: Okay noted. We'll put together expected numbers vs model choices. Quick question for infra — are you on a public cloud VPC or an on-prem cluster?
[00:01:12] Priya: We run a mix. Primary is our private cloud in EU (self-managed k8s on bare metal). We can open egress, but data residency is strict — logs and content must stay in EU.
[00:01:24] Marco: Correct. Any PII or customer transcripts need to be retained for 90 days and then purged. We also need to integrate to our KMS (Azure Key Vault) for secrets and keys.
[00:01:34] Maya: Thanks Marco, that's helpful. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and private deployment — we'll surface the integration notes.
[00:01:42] Oliver: Is there an on-prem agent or does Redwood ship a whole control plane? Need clarity on network layout.
[00:01:48] Sofia: Good Q. For Redwood Private we provide a control plane that can be configured to use customer network peering, or you can run an on-prem package. For this pilot we were thinking a short Dedicated trial that routes within EU and can be pinned to not leave region.
[00:02:03] Priya: Sounds reasonable. We prefer the control plane outside but all inference to run within our VPC or region. Can you do that?
[00:02:10] Ravi: Yes — we can route inference to regional endpoints or dedicate capacity in your region. For the trial we'll propose 2x A100-equivalent nodes, continuous batching enabled, and prefix KV cache. Note: our notes say KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash in older docs, haha.
[00:02:28] Leah: Ha, okay. On models — what are the options? We want open models but also minimal latency.
[00:02:33] Ravi: We typically recommend a curated model from our catalog — a 7B quantized variant for chat or a 13B if you need slightly better quality. We'll provide perf profiles. If latency is critical, we can also try a distilled small model.
[00:02:46] Oliver: How much effort for quantization? I assume Redwood handles infra-level setup?
[00:02:51] Sofia: We handle model onboarding for trial; quantization profiles we can recommend. If you want to bring your own model, we have a model onboarding checklist and we can run compatibility checks.
[00:03:01] Marco: On the security front — need to confirm: are audit logs available, and can they be shipped to our SIEM? Also, tokenization of PII — do you redact?
[00:03:10] Maya: Audit logs are available, and we support forwarding logs via syslog or S3-compatible endpoints. We also have PII redaction options; we'll share the doc with the exact fields and retention controls.
[00:03:22] Priya: Network question: we'll need a port list and CIDR ranges for firewall rules.
[00:03:27] Ravi: We'll send a Network Access Requirements doc — includes IP ranges, ports, and recommended NAT behavior. I'll add the k8s service account and Helm chart notes too.
[00:03:37] Leah: For QA — what observability will be in the trial? We want cost per token, latency per route, and per-user tracing if possible.
[00:03:45] Maya: Console gives per-route latency and token breakdowns. During trial we'll enable debug traces on a subset of requests for deep analysis. We also provide SDK hooks for tracing.
[00:03:56] Oliver: OK. On timeline — product wants pilot in the second half of January, with a go/no-go at the end of the two-week trial. Is that workable?
[00:04:04] Sofia: Yes, aim to start infra prep this week, run the pilot by Jan 18–31 window. We'll treat that as target.
[00:04:11] Priya: Does Redwood require a vendor security review questionnaire? We have a standard infosec packet — will that be an issue?
[00:04:17] Sofia: We expect to complete an initial security review; we'll provide a completed vendor packet and SOC2 summary. If there are bespoke items we'll route to security.
[00:04:25] Marco: Great. Also need key rotation policies documented; we operate on 90-day rotation.
[00:04:30] Maya: We'll include key rotation options and KMS integration patterns for Azure Key Vault.
[00:04:36] Ravi: Quick note about performance trade-offs — batching and cache improve cost but can increase tail latency. For a customer-facing chat we can configure small max batch sizes and a short batching window. We'll show a recommended config.
[00:04:47] Leah: Do you have an example config for the trade-offs?
[00:04:50] Ravi: Yes; we have a recommended presets doc — "interactive-low-latency" and "throughput-optimized". I'll attach and highlight defaults.
[00:04:58] Oliver: Any blockers from your side to get started?
[00:05:01] Priya: We need the runbook, the network IPs, and the SOC2 doc.
[00:05:04] Sofia: We'll deliver the runbook and network doc by 2027-01-07.
[00:05:08] Maya: I'll also create a dedicated Slack channel and invite the key contacts after the call.
[00:05:13] Marco: We'll send the compliance questionnaire back the same week.
[00:05:16] Leah: One more on data residency — what about backups and snapshots? Will they stay in region?
[00:05:21] Ravi: Yes, we can configure storage to be regional-only and disable cross-region backups for the trial. We'll document the backup policy.
[00:05:29] Sofia: Okay, recap of agreed next steps — runbook + network doc, SOC2 summary, schedule arch workshop, create Slack channel, and provision the trial cluster. Any additions?

[00:06:02] Marco: Quick question about billing for the trial — how is that handled?

document.content:
Lodestar - Commitment review & region staging plan

Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start time: 15:00 UTC (scheduled 15:00-15:45)
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Erin Patel (Lodestar - Head of ML), Jonas Berg (Lodestar - CTO), Marta Silva (Lodestar - Platform Eng)
Recording id: ff-20261130-lodestar-01

Auto-summary (auto gen - may be imperfect):
Lodestar is evaluating a +12 month commitment to increase Reserved Capacity and add APAC region. Primary asks: latency targets for APAC, private VPC connectivity details, and updated pricing. Redwood team to run a benchmark against Lodestar's 50 QPS mixed prompt workload and share SOC2/network docs. Next meeting to review benchmark results and final contract amendment.

Topics: Commitment sizing, APAC staging, latency vs cost tradeoff, VPC/on-prem questions, procurement timeline, SOC2 + KMS questions.

Action items (captured in metadata as well): send pricing, schedule benchmark, share diagrams.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hi everyone, thanks for joining, we, uh, we really appreciate you making time. I'm Maya Chen, AE at Redwood. With me is diego ruiz, who's our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Diego: hey team, morning/afternoon, gonna be mostly on the performance and network side.
[00:18] Erin: hey thanks, Erin here. jonas and marta on from our side.
[00:22] Jonas: yeah hi everyone. quick thing, we're on a tight timeline, want to lock something before end of the quarter so we can budget.
[00:30] Maya: great, that's helpful context. quick agenda: confirm capacity numbers, walk APAC staging options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), go over security docs you asked for, and agree on next steps. sound good?
[00:41] Erin: yep, that's perfect.
[00:45] Maya: okay so last time we talked Lodestar was at roughly 45M tokens/month, peak steady state 30 QPS with burst to 50. you had mentioned wanting to add APAC for latency reasons and consider increasing to a reserved tier. is that still accurate?
[01:00] Marta: yes, the 50QPS bursts are the painful bit during our mobile peak windows. APAC users are complaining about 400-500 ms tail latency currently.
[01:10] Diego: got it. with Redwood Dedicated in a APAC region we should be able to get p50 p95 numbers under 120/200ms depending on model size and quantization. if you push most traffic to a local region we avoid cross-pacific hops.
[01:26] Jonas: what about the cost delta though? moving to dedicated GPUs in APAC seems... pricey. we're balancing cost and customer experience.
[01:34] Maya: yep, that's the core tradeoff. we have two common patterns: 1) enable Hosted API across regions and use smart routing + a smaller dedicated pool for spikes; or 2) full Dedicated in APAC if you want strict latency SLOs and capacity isolation. the first is lower commit, second is higher commit but predictable unit costs.
[01:54] Erin: can you send us a modeled cost example for our 50QPS profile? like 3 variants: hosted-only, hybrid with small dedicated pool, and full dedicated?
[02:04] Maya: yes we'll do that. i'll include per-token and per-hour math, and we'll show the effect of turning on prefix caching and 8-bit quantization which materially cuts cost.
[02:16] Diego: quick note: quantization can affect quality, especially for your longer-context prompts. we'll include a recommended quant profile per model variant and example eval diffs.
[02:28] Marta: great — can you also confirm the model variants you recommend? we're evaluating two open models: model-XL and model-XXL.
[02:34] Diego: for latency-sensitive traffic model-XL quantized (8-bit) hits a good balance. for highest quality responses keep model-XXL but consider KV cache warmup and batching to control cost.
[02:42] Jonas: you mentioned KV cache — does that help tail latency?
[02:46] Diego: yes, for multi-turn workflows the KV cache avoids re-computing earlier layers; it reduces per-token compute and improves token throughput. but it increases memory footprint per session, so we size capacity accordingly.
[02:58] Erin: switching to networking: we need VPC peering, private IPs, and we have strict audit log requirements — we need to see how Redwood logs map to our SIEM.
[03:08] Maya: understood. we have examples of VPC diagrams and S3/flow log configs, and we support VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud. we'll share the SOC2 packet and the network architecture diagram after this call. (link: https://redwood.app/security/soc2 and a drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/lodestar-arch)
[03:28] Jonas: also KMS — we require customer-managed keys, is that supported?
[03:32] Diego: yes, KMS/HSM integrations are supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS for at-rest encryption. we'll clarify the exact pattern for hosted with customer keys.
[03:44] Marta: is the Private option the same as your on-prem package? we might consider that for sensitive data stores.
[03:49] Maya: Private is an option — it's a customer-managed control plane with optional on-prem package. tends to be used when regulators or internal policy require it. cost and setup time are higher. for many customers Dedicated + VPC meets the requirements with lower ops overhead.
[04:05] Jonas: timeline question — if we sign a commit by Dec 15, when can we realistically have APAC Dedicated capacity live?
[04:12] Diego: typically provisioning in APAC region for Dedicated takes 3-4 weeks after order for standard configs. if you need faster we can do a burst reserve while Dedicated is being stood up.
[04:22] Erin: on procurement we need a contract amendment for +12 months and a PO. can you put together a draft amendment?
[04:28] Maya: yes i'll send a contract amendment draft with the pricing options.
[04:31] Jonas: any competitors you've seen that do this well?
[04:34] Maya: folks mention MajorCloudAI and InferServe — inferserve has lower entry cost but less observability, MajorCloudAI has global infra but the unit economics are worse for high token volumes. i'll include a short competitor note.
[04:48] Erin: one more technical: can you do a benchmark with our traffic? we can provide sample prompts and a subset of traffic that simulates 50 QPS with mixed short and long contexts.
[04:58] Diego: yes we can run an in-house benchmark or a joint-run against your test harness. i recommend a joint-run so we validate end-to-end network. we'll need a small window of sustained QPS for about 10-15 minutes per model variant, plus collection of p50/p95/p99.
[05:12] Marta: ok i'll share the traffic profile and a prompt set. also we use an internal auth gateway that impersonates calls — we'll provide a test token for the joint run.
[05:21] Diego: perfect. we'll prepare a JMeter script and a run book.
[05:25] Maya: circling back to pricing: for modeling purposes, would you prefer to show monthly amortized cost or a committed discount schedule by tier?
[05:34] Jonas: committed discount schedule with an amortized monthly view would be easiest for finance. they like a per-token blended rate.
[05:41] Maya: good — we'll produce both so you can present to finance.
[05:45] Erin: on security, SOC2 and SSO — we use SAML 2.0 with SCIM for provisioning. will that map to Redwood Console?
[05:54] Diego: yes, Redwood Console supports SAML + SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC. we'll attach the SAML metadata and sample SCIM payloads.
[06:03] Jonas: what about audit log retention? we need 12 months of logs for compliance.
[06:07] Maya: default retention is 90 days but for enterprise add-on we can extend retention to 12 months — that's part of the compliance package. i'll include pricing for extended retention.
[06:18] Erin: good. procurement wants a single invoice monthly, not per-region. is that supported?
[06:24] Maya: yes, we can consolidate billing across regions for enterprise customers and show a single monthly invoice.
[06:30] Marta: curious about model rollouts — if we pin to a specific version, how do rollbacks work? we run A/B for small % of traffic.
[06:37] Diego: Redwood supports A/B rollouts and automatic fallback policies. you can pin versions per route and do canary deploys. if an eval alerts on regression we can auto-fallback to previous stable.
[06:48] Erin: do you integrate with our observability stack? we use Datadog and Sentry.
[06:53] Diego: yes we surface metrics via Datadog and can push traces to your tracing backend. Sentry for error events is supported via webhooks.
[07:02] Jonas: is there a way to limit exposure so some prompts don't leave our VPC? we have a few PII-heavy workflows.
[07:09] Maya: for PII workflows Private deployment or on-prem is recommended. alternatively, you can route those traffic to a private endpoint and keep rest on hosted. we'll note the segregation pattern in an architecture doc.
[07:21] Erin: ok good.
[07:23] Maya: quick commercial check — do you have an internal approval threshold for commits? ie finance needs x to ok.
[07:30] Jonas: anything over $250k annual requires VP approval, but below that procurement can sign. a 12-month commit probably sits near that threshold so we'll need signoff.
[07:40] Maya: good to know, we'll prepare materials accordingly.
[07:44] Diego: moving to the benchmark plan — proposal: 3 runs: model-XL quantized, model-XXL 8-bit, model-XXL fp16; each run 15 minutes at 50 QPS with the provided prompt mix. collect p50/p95/p99 and failure rate. we'll also test with prefix caching on/off. does that sound right?
[08:06] Marta: yes, and please include end-to-end network latency so we can see impact of peering.
[08:11] Diego: will do.
[08:13] Erin: how do we interpret the results wrt cost? we need per-token cost and per-hour cost plus predicted monthly bill.
[08:20] Maya: our benchmark report will include throughput, latencies, and an estimated monthly cost model using your traffic numbers.
[08:27] Jonas: timeline recap: can we get the benchmark week of Dec 6, pricing + contract draft by Dec 2, and internal approvals by Dec 15?
[08:36] Maya: yes that's feasible. we'll aim to get docs out by Dec 2 and run the benchmark week of Dec 6-10.
[08:44] Erin: sounds good. a couple quick clarifications: do you offer SLA credits if latency SLOs are missed?
[08:51] Maya: for Dedicated we offer uptime SLAs and latency targets tied to model families; financial credits are part of enterprise SLA. i'll add the SLA language to the amendment.
[08:59] Jonas: procurement will want a sample security questionnaire answered. can you share a completed one?
[09:04] Diego: yes we have an NDAed security questionnaire and a public one. we'll share both; the public one is faster.
[09:12] Marta: small note — our infra team wants to ensure IPv6 support for endpoints. does Redwood support IPv6?
[09:19] Diego: partial support today; full support roadmap in Q1. we'll note the timeline.
[09:25] Erin: competitor question, we've seen a lower cost quote from EdgeRun but they don't have strong RBAC or observability. curious what you recommend.
[09:32] Maya: if observability and deterministic economics are important, Redwood's tooling helps a lot. we'll include a short compare slide.
[09:40] Jonas: any blockers from Redwood side to hit the Dec 2 doc date?
[09:44] Maya: no blockers, we'll pull pricing from finance and Diego will own the benchmark details.
[09:50] Diego: i'll reach out to marta for test tokens and traffic pattern.
[09:54] Erin: okay great.
[09:56] Maya: just to wrap — recap of commitments: 1) pricing + contract amendment draft by Dec 2, 2) SOC2 + network diagram + SAML/SCIM metadata by Dec 2, 3) benchmark run week of Dec 6 (Diego to prepare run book and JMeter script), 4) Lodestar to provide traffic profile and test tokens by Dec 1, 5) follow-up meeting after benchmark to review results (proposed Dec 10).
[10:22] Jonas: that timeline works for us.
[10:26] Maya: perfect — i'll send calendar invites for the benchmark slot and for the Dec 10 results review.
[10:31] Erin: thanks everyone.
[10:33] Maya: thanks, bye.

Notes/links referenced in call:
- Pricing sheet (draft): https://redwood.app/pricing/lodestar-draft
- Security packet / SOC2: https://redwood.app/security/soc2
- Architecture drive: https://drive.redwood.com/lodestar-arch
- Benchmark runbook template: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/template

document.content:
Solace Therapeutics - model selection & deployment options

Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-18
- Start: 15:30 PST
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Solace Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (CTO), Ethan Park (Security), Lena Ortiz (Data Eng)
- Recording link: (internal) rwd-recordings/ff-2026-11-18-solace.mp3
- Shared artifacts: Deck: https://bit.ly/rwd-models-deck, Security brief: https://drive.redwood/sec-solace.pdf

Summary:
Solace is evaluating open model options for a clinical triage assistant and patient messaging summarization. Main constraints: long context (20k+ tokens for patient threads), multilingual support (EN/ES/FR), strict PHI handling (want private deployment or VPC), and tool-calling to integrate with internal ticketing. They asked about tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private for latency, cost, and compliance. Agreed to run a dedicated benchmark and exchange anonymized prompts.

Topics covered:
- Model selection: open models vs off-the-shelf APIs
- Context length and chunking strategies (20k-40k token needs)
- Multilingual evals and tokenization differences
- Tool-calling and secure connector patterns (ticketing, EHR lookups)
- Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security: SOC2/ISO, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, data residency

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and Diego's here from our SE team. how's everyone doing?
[00:09] Priya Nair: Hi Maya, doing good thanks, we've got Tom, Ethan, and Lena with me. Busy week but excited to dig in.
[00:15] Tom Reynolds: Yeah thanks, hope we can cover model choice and where to host it, that's the key gating for our PoC.
[00:22] Diego Alvarez: Great, we'll try to focus on the model tradeoffs first — latency/cost/quality — and then deployment. quick question: when you say 20k context, is that bursty or sustained?
[00:34] Priya Nair: Mostly thread-based, like patient conversation history plus records, the average thread tops 12-18k but some go to 30-40k when you include attachments transcribed. so we need something that can handle long context or we need clear chunking with retrieval.
[00:48] Maya Chen: OK that's helpful — Redwood supports models with larger context windows and we also do prefix KV cache and retrieval integration. Diego will talk about how we handle continuous batching and KV cache.
[00:58] Diego Alvarez: Right — so for large sequences we typically recommend either a native long-context model (if available) or a hybrid: retrieval + windowing + KV caching. note that native long-context variants can be more expensive per token but simpler for tool-calling because the tool state can live in the same decoder context. Small pause... like sometimes the transcript tool converts KV cache to "K V cash" in our notes ha.
[01:20] Ethan Park: haha yeah that's the transcription. on security, obviously PHI is a no-go for hosted unless we have a BAA and dedicated isolation — what's Redwood's posture?
[01:30] Maya Chen: We do offer hosted with enterprise controls, but for PHI most customers either use Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity and VPC peering or Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane / on-prem). we have SOC2/HIPAA guidance; I'll attach the security brief.
[01:44] Priya Nair: For us, latency matters during live triage — sub 300ms token latency for short prompts, and for long-context summarization we can tolerate a few seconds but throughput matters. how do you balance batching vs latency?
[01:57] Diego Alvarez: Good question — Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching tuned by latency SLOs. you set a target p50/p95 and the router will batch up to that window. Dedicated deployments give you predictable throughput and tighter latency SLAs because you control the GPU pool. Hosted is more variable but easier to start.
[02:14] Tom Reynolds: Cost is huge too. our finance team will compare per-token pricing across vendors. do you have examples for a 1M tokens/month workload?
[02:24] Maya Chen: We'll provide a TCO sheet. rough rule: dedicated commits reduce unit cost by 30-50% vs hosted at scale; private on-prem has higher fixed costs but lowest marginal token cost if you own hardware. we'll send a modeled spreadsheet after this.
[02:36] Lena Ortiz: On multilingual — we need EN/ES/FR production quality. are you recommending a single multilingual model or language-specific models?
[02:45] Diego Alvarez: It depends — single multilingual models are convenient but sometimes a language-specific quantized model yields better tone and hallucination reduction. we can run evals on your sample prompts; we also recommend tokenization profiling because Spanish and French can change token budgets.
[02:58] Priya Nair: We also need tool-calling to query our ticketing system and to trigger a follow-up workflow. any concerns about exposing connectors in Hosted?
[03:07] Maya Chen: For tool-calling we support function-style calls. with Hosted you can use secure connectors and Redwood will not log payload if you opt out, but for strict compliance people prefer Dedicated or Private so connectors run inside their VPC and data never touches public control plane. Diego, maybe walk through typical connector patterns?
[03:22] Diego Alvarez: Sure — pattern A: webhook-based calls with short-lived tokens; Pattern B: VPC connector where we establish a private link; Pattern C: on-prem adapter for air-gapped EHR. for PHI we'd push Dedicated with VPC or Private. note that for some customers we implement a signed token exchange so the model calls the function but the private backend validates it.
[03:41] Ethan Park: What's the auditability? we need immutable logs for tool calls and model inputs for audits.
[03:48] Maya Chen: Redwood exposes audit logs with token-level traces, and you can configure retention. for Private you can keep logs entirely in your SIEM. also we integrate with KMS for key isolation.
[03:59] Priya Nair: Model selection: we were looking at LlamaX variants, Mistral derivatives, and some long-context LLMs. any recommendations?
[04:08] Diego Alvarez: Quick take: LlamaX-style open models are great for cost and customization; Mistral family often scores high on generation quality; for long context look at models that support 64k windows or use memory-augmented approaches. Redwood's model catalog tags models with verified perf profiles — we'll share a matrix.
[04:25] Tom Reynolds: Are you doing model quantization by default on Dedicated? worried about quality regressions.
[04:31] Diego Alvarez: We have quantization profiles — post-training quantization can reduce footprint with minimal quality loss but it's model-dependent. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization settings per workload; for critical clinical text we usually suggest higher-precision variants for the PoC.
[04:47] Priya Nair: For the PoC, we want a canary approach: start Hosted for quick iteration, then move to Dedicated for the perf benchmark, and if compliance requires it, to Private. is that typical?
[04:57] Maya Chen: That's exactly the pattern many customers use. Hosted to prototype, Dedicated for scale and SLA, Private when you need on-prem or air-gap.
[05:05] Lena Ortiz: About integration — latency with tool-calls: do calls block the generation? we want non-blocking function calls so we can parallelize lookups.
[05:13] Diego Alvarez: Our tool-calling supports either blocking sync responses or async callback patterns. you can instrument the runtime to continue generation with placeholders and then splice results in, or enforce sync if you need final consistent output.
[05:25] Tom Reynolds: Any red flags with EHR connectors and PHI? we need BAAs and often on-prem adapters.
[05:31] Maya Chen: We have BAA patterns and customers with EHRs use VPC peering or private deployment. we'll share our HIPAA appendix.
[05:38] Ethan Park: Encryption — can keys be customer-managed?
[05:42] Maya Chen: Yes, KMS/HSM integrations are supported in Dedicated and Private. for Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key for certain enterprise tiers.
[05:50] Priya Nair: Let's talk about expected metrics from your benchmarks. what do you report?
[05:55] Diego Alvarez: We provide p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec throughput, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens under the measured workload. we'll also surface quality metrics: ROUGE/BLEU for summarization and a hallucination score from our eval harness.
[06:10] Priya Nair: Can you run multilingual BLEU/ROUGE for Spanish and French?
[06:14] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we can run language-specific evals — please provide sample references.
[06:18] Maya Chen: Quick logistical thing — what's your timeline for PoC?
[06:21] Tom Reynolds: We want a 6-week PoC starting early Dec, then decision by mid-Jan.
[06:27] Maya Chen: That seems doable. we'll propose a timeline and bench slots.
[06:31] Priya Nair: On the model governance side, how do you support model pinning and rollbacks? we need to ensure reproducibility for clinical behaviors.
[06:39] Diego Alvarez: Redwood supports model version pinning per route, rollout controls with canary/A-B, and automatic fallback policies. all of that is surfaced in the Console and audit logs.
[06:48] Ethan Park: About data residency — some of our records must stay in-region (EU for a subset). can Redwood route by region?
[06:54] Maya Chen: Yes, smart routing by region or tier is supported. you can restrict a route to EU regions only. with Private you of course control exact placement.
[07:01] Tom Reynolds: Competitors — we'd like to see how Redwood compares to Anthropic/OpenAI on latency and cost. can you provide a comparison?
[07:08] Maya Chen: We'll include a competitive slide. generally the difference comes down to model variant and deployment mode; Redwood's value is runtime and ops controls.
[07:15] Priya Nair: Regarding long-context models, do you do partial KV caching across sessions? we have threaded conversations where earlier context is re-used a lot.
[07:25] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have prefix and KV cache strategies; you can cache embeddings or token-level KV depending on model support. caching reduces token costs significantly for repeated context.
[07:35] Lena Ortiz: For the benchmark, what data do you need from us besides prompts? environment specs?
[07:40] Diego Alvarez: Sample prompt set, reference outputs if available, preferred languages, and target latency SLOs. optionally a small anonymized dataset for realistic throughput measurement.
[07:49] Priya Nair: We'll prep that. any thoughts on fallback models for graceful degradation if your primary model is oversubscribed?
[07:56] Maya Chen: We recommend a fall-back stack: primary -> quantized variant -> smaller local model. Redwood's router can do automatic fallback by policy.
[08:06] Tom Reynolds: Question about pricing: do you do committed use discounts for Dedicated?
[08:11] Maya Chen: Yes, monthly/annual commits available; committed plans get lower per-token rates and reserved GPU capacity.
[08:18] Ethan Park: For audit and debug, can you trace back model output to the exact model version and prompt used? we need that for incident reports.
[08:24] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely — token-level tracing with model version IDs and route context is included.
[08:30] Priya Nair: Ok one more: model updates and drift detection — do you have quality monitoring?
[08:36] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. you can set baselines and get alerted on drift.
[08:44] Lena Ortiz: Who would be our day-to-day contact during PoC?
[08:47] Maya Chen: That's me for commercial and Diego for technical. we'll also assign a CSM if we move to Dedicated.
[08:53] Tom Reynolds: sounds good. any blockers for us to start the Hosted PoC this week?
[08:58] Maya Chen: We can spin up Hosted routes quickly; Dedicated benchmark needs scheduling but we can propose next week.
[09:04] Priya Nair: Let's recap next steps — we'll send prompts, you send perf plan and pricing.
[09:10] Maya Chen: Correct. Diego, will you own the test plan?
[09:13] Diego Alvarez: Yes I'll draft it and share.
[09:16] Ethan Park: one last security Q: if we do Hosted for initial tests, will our PHI be excluded from logs by default?
[09:23] Maya Chen: By default Hosted collects telemetry for ops; we can enable log redaction and no-logging for sensitive payloads on enterprise tiers. we'll document exactly how to opt-out.
[09:33] Priya Nair: Great, thanks everyone.
[09:36] Tom Reynolds: Thanks all.
[09:38] Maya Chen: Thanks team, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet, perf plan, and security docs.
[09:43] -- End of meeting --

Post-call notes (auto):
- Agreed PoC timeline: target start first week of December, 6-week duration.
- Benchmark: Dedicated perf slot requested; Redwood to provide GPU config options (A100, H100) and test plan.
- Security packet: Redwood to share HIPAA appendix, BAA template, KMS integration guide.
- Links: Model catalog: https://console.redwood.ai/models, Perf kit: https://bit.ly/rwd-perf-kit

Recorded action items (also in metadata):
- Maya Chen: Send pricing + model perf matrix + security packet (due 2026-11-20)
- Diego Alvarez: Draft perf test plan and propose Dedicated benchmark slots (due 2026-11-19)
- Priya Nair: Provide anonymized prompt threads and reference outputs (due 2026-11-22)
