Q4 Ops Roundup: IT, Finance Ops & Security Coordination

Monthly cross-functional alignment focused on upcoming Q4 procurement and CapEx vs OpEx decisions, SOC2 evidence collection status, scheduled maintenance windows for patching, and cost-center tagging for reserved capacity. Agreed next steps around PO submission, updated chargeback spreadsheet, and a short demo of log export to SIEM.
Q4 hardware refresh / procurement timeline
Billing / chargeback model for Dedicated pools
SOC2 evidence collection and audit readiness
Patching windows and maintenance scheduling
Log retention and SIEM feeds (Splunk)
KMS rotation and key management for private deployments
Alex to share updated chargeback spreadsheet and cost mapping by 2025-10-10
Rachel to submit PO for 8x dedicated GPU nodes (PR #4521) by 2025-10-15
Marisol to assemble SOC2 evidence pack (logs, access lists) and share S3 link by 2025-10-17
Laura to confirm maintenance window Friday 02:00-04:00 PST and notify teams by 2025-10-06
Ethan to run quick SIEM export demo in next sync (20 min) — schedule on calendar
Alex Carter - Update chargeback spreadsheet with cost-center tags and reserved capacity allocations (due: 2025-10-10)
Rachel Kim - Create and submit purchase order for Dedicated GPU commit (due: 2025-10-15)
Marisol Vega - Compile SOC2 evidence artifacts (due: 2025-10-17)
Laura Simmons - Confirm maintenance window and publish outage notice (due: 2025-10-06)
Ethan Zhou - Prepare SIEM/Splunk export demo and test export (due: 2025-10-08)
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-03
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Priya, Alex, Marisol, Ethan, Tom, Laura, Samir, Rachel
---
[00:00] Priya: Okay, uh, good morning everyone. Thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. We're here to align IT, finance and security on the Q4 ops items. We've got about an hour and fifteen, agenda in the invite. Any additions before we start?
[00:12] Tom: No additions from finance, just the usual, we need the final numbers for the chargeback model. Q4 planning's tight.
[00:18] Laura: I want to make sure the maintenance windows are locked — last time we had some surprises with the nightly jobs.
[00:25] Marisol: And SOC2 — we got a calendar hole for evidence, so we'll need logs and access lists. I'll go through the gaps.
[00:30] Ethan: Also quick note — platform wants to standardize asset tags so CMDB stays consistent. That will help procurement and finance tie invoices to cost centers.
[00:38] Priya: Great. First item: procurement and hardware refresh. Rachel, status?
[00:42] Rachel: We're ready to issue the PO, but we need final sign-off for 8 nodes in the Dedicated pool. Finance asked for CapEx vs OpEx alignment — whether we do a reserved capacity commit or pay-as-you-go for the extra Q4 bursts.
[00:55] Alex: From finance side, reserved capacity is nicer for unit cost, but we need to make sure it's allocated to the right cost centers. The chargeback spreadsheet I sent last week needs those cost-center tags filled — otherwise it's a bookkeeping nightmare.
[01:08] Priya: Can you give a quick run-of numbers, Alex? Rough delta between reserved and on-demand?
[01:12] Alex: Yeah, roughly 30-40% saving if we commit 12 months, but Q4 only we might be locking funds. If we do a shorter commit or a partial commit the savings are lower. I'll update the sheet with modeling for 6 vs 12 month commits.
[01:27] Tom: Remember procurement needs PO numbers in the invoice line items — please make sure PR and PO references match. Last invoice was missing PR tag and accounting had to chase.
[01:35] Rachel: Noted. We'll include PR #4521 on the PO.
[01:40] Laura: On the ops side, if we're adding nodes we need a plan for patch windows. Friday early morning maintenance has the least impact. Can we confirm Friday 02:00-04:00 PST?
[01:52] Ethan: That works for platform runner jobs. We should also coordinate with the data team on long-running jobs.
[01:58] Marisol: From security perspective, any maintenance window needs to be documented and change tickets raised. Also I need prior notice for any infra-level credential changes, rotation, or KMS updates.
[02:10] Priya: Good segue — KMS and key rotation is next. We recently had a request about rotating keys for private deployments. Marisol, are we on schedule for the quarterly rotation?
[02:18] Marisol: Partially. We did the staging keys but not prod. There's a dependency on procurement for some HSM time. Also need confirmation whether the private deployments use customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed keys; there was some confusion on the last ticket. The notes in the ticket show both.
[02:33] Laura: For the customers on Private we default to customer-managed KMS, but internal services use Redwood KMS for now. We should record that in the runbook.
[02:40] Priya: Ethan, can you add that to the infra runbook and push one-line summary?
[02:45] Ethan: Yep, will do.
[02:46] [05:00] Tom: On SOC2, Marisol, where are we with log retention? Splunk retention is set to 365 days for most logs, but the control requires evidence of retention policies and some audit exports.
[05:12] Marisol: I have a list of the required artifacts. We need a couple things: (1) an S3 bucket with exported logs for the assessment (2) a mapping of who has access — ideally RBAC lists and console screenshots, and (3) change control tickets showing patch windows. I can assemble.
[05:30] Alex: Does finance need anything else for audit besides invoices and contracts?
[05:35] Samir: Procurement docs, vendor attestations, and evidence of control ownership — basically who owns what control. I'll reach out to the PMs for control rosters.
[05:45] Priya: Ok. Action item: Marisol put together the SOC2 pack and share S3 link. Alex: make sure chargeback numbers are updated with cost tags that match finance's accounting codes.
[06:00] [10:00] Rachel: Quick question on chargebacks — should we include amortized hardware cost across teams or bill directly to a single platform cost center and do internal recharges?
[10:10] Alex: We prefer direct chargebacks to teams where possible. If that's operationally heavy, a platform pool with internal recharges is simpler for Q4. We'll model both in the spreadsheet.
[10:22] Priya: Next — log export to SIEM. Ethan you flagged a demo?
[10:28] Ethan: Yeah, short demo. We're going to push a quick pipeline from our log service to Splunk and show how to pull raw request traces for audit purposes. It's not a full run today, but I can schedule a 20 minute slot next week to demo.
[10:40] Marisol: When you do the demo, show how to filter for admin actions and KV cache hits. Those are common audit queries and sometimes transcription swaps the names so show the exact fields.
[10:52] Ethan: Will do.
[10:55] [15:00] Tom: Invoices — a couple of vendors changed billing address last month; we need to confirm vendor remit address before we pay. Also any credits from last quarter? I think Red... Redwood had a credit on the hosted API line.
[15:15] Alex: Yeah there's a small credit from usage. I'll reconcile and post a note.
[15:20] Priya: Miscellaneous security question — are we masking PII before logs go to Splunk or do we do it at query time?
[15:28] Marisol: Currently we try to redact PII at ingest, but some traces leak in edge cases. We should push more redaction rules. I'll file a ticket to add a couple rules for email and full Social Security-like patterns.
[15:40] Laura: Also, remember network diagrams for the auditor — I updated the VPC peering docs but need a final review.
[15:48] Priya: Who's owning network diagrams?
[15:50] Ethan: I'll take ownership, update by 2025-10-12.
[15:55] [20:00] Samir: There's an outstanding question on encryption in transit for private deployments — are all internal inter-service calls TLS mutual? I thought yes but need to confirm for older clusters.
[20:12] Marisol: Most new clusters enforce mTLS. Some older ones are in the process of migrating. I'll add a matrix mapping cluster -> encryption status.
[20:22] Tom: Back to finance — can we get a one pager summarizing costs for execs? They want CAPEX impact and monthly run rate.
[20:30] Alex: Yes, I'll build a one-pager and include side-by-side reserved vs on-demand comparisons.
[20:36] Priya: Good. Next, change management. Laura mentioned surprise jobs last patch window — what's the root cause?
[20:43] Laura: One of the nightly analytics jobs had a runaway partition and slipped into the maintenance window. We didn't have a pre-checklist to pause long-running batch jobs.
[20:55] Ethan: We can add a gating checklist that ops runs 24 hours prior — a quick query to surface long jobs. I can add a script to warn if a job runs > 6 hours.
[21:06] Marisol: Also ensure access lists are captured in Jira tickets to show who approved the change.
[21:10] [25:00] Rachel: Procurement question — if we do a reserved capacity commit, who signs? Is it VP Finance, or do we need Board sign-off for the amount?
[25:12] Tom: For the amount we're discussing, VP approval is sufficient, but anything above $500k needs additional review. This commit is below that for now.
[25:24] Rachel: Great. I'll proceed with VP sign-off route.
[25:30] Priya: Any downstream teams that should be notified if we spin up the Dedicated nodes?
[25:36] Ethan: Data platform and ML infra will care — they may want direct nodes for batch jobs. We'll tag nodes with pool names and notify via the internal channel.
[25:46] [30:00] Tom: Re: invoices — please include cost-center tags as an invoice line item. Last quarter the mapping script failed and entries landed in the wrong GL.
[30:12] Alex: I'll validate the mapping script and add a manual review step before posting to general ledger.
[30:20] Marisol: SOC2 evidence again — screenshots are noisy, auditors like exported CSVs for user lists. Can we export IAM user lists?
[30:28] Laura: Yes, we can export consolidated IAM lists. We'll need to scrub any service accounts per the auditor's request.
[30:34] Priya: Good. Next item: access control and Okta SSO. We had a ticket about errant group membership. Rachel, procurement touched some service accounts recently?
[30:44] Rachel: We did create a handful of service accounts for vendor onboarding; I left notes in the ticket but maybe not the full access scopes.
[30:52] Marisol: I'll run a membership audit and flag any accounts with excessive privileges.
[30:58] [40:00] Ethan: Small ops note — our monitoring shows a spike in 95th percentile latency during backup windows. We need to stagger backups or throttle IO.
[40:12] Laura: That's likely related to the nightly DB snapshots. We can schedule snapshots in multi-window blocks or use incremental snapshots.
[40:18] Priya: Let's prioritize reducing impact to inference latency; customers will notice.
[40:22] Tom: Which brings me to chargeback — if backups are causing customer-visible latency, teams consuming infra should be billed for the incremental cost.
[40:30] Alex: We'll factor that into the spreadsheet as a separate line item (backup IO surcharge) if we need to.
[40:36] [50:00] Marisol: Quick FYI: vendor security questionnaire — one of our third-party vendors requested our incident response playbook. We should have a sanitized copy for vendor sharing. Samir, any objection?
[50:12] Samir: No objection. We'll produce a redacted playbook showing SLA and contacts.
[50:18] Priya: OK. Ryan (not present) asked about the Redwood Dedicated naming — FYI some transcriptions and docs say "Redwood Dedicate" which is causing search mismatches. Minor but annoying.
[50:28] Ethan: Haha, will grep the docs and fix common typos in the repo.
[50:34] [60:00] Rachel: Procurement final note — invoicing cadence? Vendor offers monthly billing but finance prefers net-30 with monthly statements. Any objections?
[60:10] Tom: Net-30 monthly is fine; just ensure we get consolidated statements to reconcile.
[60:18] Alex: I'll confirm with AP.
[60:22] Priya: Great. Final quick items: any blockers for the SOC2 audit timeline?
[60:28] Marisol: Gaps are small: log exports, one-off evidence items, and a few access lists. All should be ready within two weeks if teams respond.
[60:36] Priya: Perfect. Recap: Alex update spreadsheet, Rachel submit PO, Marisol compile SOC2 evidence, Laura confirm maintenance window, Ethan demo SIEM next week.
[60:48] Tom: Also please include an executive one-pager for finance.
[60:52] Priya: Noted. Anything else?
[61:00] Laura: No, thanks everyone.
[61:04] Priya: Thanks all — we'll follow up in threads and update action items. Meeting ends.
---
References noted in call: PR #4521, chargeback-spreadsheet v2 (internal link), SOC2 evidence S3 bucket (to be created), maintenance change ticket CHG-2025-10-06.

Pioneer Orbit implementation ignition and security handshake

Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-02-08 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (CSM), Liam O'Neill (SE), Anita Rao (Pioneer Orbit), Carlos Mendes (Pioneer), Sofia Liu (Pioneer), Evan Brooks (Pioneer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
Quick kickoff to align on activation plan for Pioneer Orbit's LLM inference use case, confirm security/compliance blockers, agree next steps for a Dedicated pilot and private deployment POC, and schedule technical deep-dive.

Topics: onboarding timeline, security & KMS, VPC/networking, billing and pilot scope, runbook and SLOs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Daniel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, welcome. Uh quick intros — I'm Daniel, AE on the account, Maya is our CSM, and Liam will run the tech bits.
[00:18] Anita: Hi, thanks. I'm Anita, head of MLOps at Pioneer Orbit. We own the integration and ops for the model infra.
[00:26] Carlos: Carlos here, platform eng, I'll be doing the VPC and peering.
[00:31] Sofia: Sofia, security architect. We'll focus on compliance, KMS, and audit trails.
[00:36] Daniel: Great. High level — Pioneer told us you want predictable latency for in-product suggestions, and strict data isolation. Is that right?
[00:46] Anita: Yes. We have a latency SLO of 120ms p95 for the small prompts, and we need to keep any customer PII never leaving our VPC.
[00:57] Maya: To confirm, you're interested in Redwood Dedicated with a Private deployment option for the initial pilot?
[01:04] Evan: Correct, we want Dedicated capacity but also the option to run a private control plane in our cloud.
[01:12] Liam: For the Dedicated pilot we typically set up reserved GPU pools and a private control plane — the network pattern is either VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink. From a tech standpoint we'll need to validate egress rules and KMS access.
[01:28] Carlos: We prefer peering, we have strict firewalling and don't allow cross-account IAM roles without an extra approval.
[01:38] Sofia: On KMS — we use a HSM-backed KMS and require customer-managed keys. Can Redwood integrate with an external KMS?
[01:46] Liam: Short answer: yes, you can bring your own KMS. We do support external customer-managed keys. There are some integration steps for the private control plane that we'll detail in the network checklist.
[01:58] Anita: Perfect. A couple of red flags from procurement — data retention and audit logs. We need logs for 13 months and access to token-level usage for billing reconciliation.
[02:10] Daniel: Understood. Maya, we've captured that for the runbook.
[02:13] Maya: Yep, will add retention and token-level exports as acceptance criteria for the pilot.
[02:21] [02:30] Liam: Also worth calling out: for inference economics we recommend KV caching and small sequence batching for your prompt shapes — that reduces cost and helps hit latency SLOs. But batching increases tail latency occasionally.
[02:44] Carlos: We saw mention of K V cash in the docs last week — is that the same? The transcription in the doc said K-V cash and we were confused.
[02:53] Liam: Haha yeah, that's a transcription artifact — KV cache, key-value cache. It retains past tokens for chat-like workloads.
[03:02] [03:15] Anita: On timeline, we're aiming to start the pilot in late Feb and run for 8 weeks — success metrics would be: meeting p95 latency, cost per request under target, and zero data leaks.
[03:32] Daniel: Good. For the pilot we usually propose a three-node Dedicated pool with autoscaling turned off initially so we can measure steady-state.
[03:40] Evan: That seems fine. How does billing look for that model?
[03:45] Daniel: We'll send a pricing estimate — monthly reserved capacity plus overage billing for extra bursts. I'll include a sample commitment schedule.
[03:54] [04:10] Sofia: A few technical questions now: do you provide audit logs with per-token identifiers, and can we hook them into our SIEM?
[04:19] Liam: Yes, audit logs are available; we stream logs to an S3-compatible endpoint or push to your SIEM via secure syslog/forwarder. Format is JSON with request IDs, model, tokens, and redaction flags.
[04:33] Sofia: And redaction — is there automatic PII redaction or do we need to apply post-processing?
[04:40] Maya: We have best-practice guides; automatic redaction is limited — most customers do a combined approach with prompt-level redaction and post-hoc scanning. We can include our redaction guidance in the runbook.
[04:52] [05:02] Carlos: Network: what ports/protocols should we open for the control plane in a peered setup?
[05:09] Liam: Primarily HTTPS on 443 for API calls, and a few gRPC endpoints for streaming. For KV cache and model data transfer we use internal secure channels, we'll provide a concise CIDR list for firewall rules.
[05:25] Anita: Any known gotchas for on-prem style networks? We have some legacy NAT'ing and symmetric routing.
[05:33] Liam: Symmetric NAT can break certain long-lived streams; if you have that we recommend using our PrivateLink path which avoids asymmetric routing. We can table the deep network checks for the next session.
[05:47] [06:05] Daniel: Let's talk runbook and owners — Maya will lead onboarding, Liam will own the tech checklist, Daniel sign contracts and pricing, and Pioneer will own infra.
[06:18] Maya: I'll send an onboarding runbook draft with milestone gates: network sign-off, KMS verification, pre-prod validation, go/no-go.
[06:29] Evan: For pre-prod validation what tests do you recommend?
[06:34] Liam: We'll run a load validation at expected qps with KV caching and without to measure delta, and a failover test to ensure fallback to hosted variants if the private control plane loses connectivity.
[06:48] [07:00] Anita: Can we do a short smoke test next week? 30 minutes to validate connectivity and a simple generation?
[07:07] Liam: Absolutely — I'll schedule a 30-minute smoke with Carlos and his infra pair.
[07:13] [07:30] Sofia: On compliance docs — send SOC2 reports and any ISO attestations. Also, do you have a data residency policy for EU customers?
[07:40] Maya: We have region-aware deployments and can pin model serving to EU regions; I'll include the region map in the packet. SOC2 and ISO docs will be attached.
[07:53] [08:15] Carlos: Regarding rollout — how do you handle model updates and rollbacks? We need a predictable path so we don't have sudden regressions in customer experience.
[08:26] Liam: We support canary rollouts by traffic slice and automatic fallback to a previous model variant if quality drops. We also version models so you can pin a model id in routes.
[08:38] Anita: Good. One more — evals. We want to run a quality check against our prompt set before each rollout. Can you help with integrating Redwood Optimize or do we run it separately?
[08:49] Daniel: We can connect you with the Optimize team; for the pilot we can share a basic eval harness and measurement dashboard.
[08:59] [09:15] Maya: Ok let's recap and assign next steps.
[09:18] Daniel: Recap — pilot scope: Dedicated 3-node pool, private control plane in your VPC with peering, KMS BYOK, audit logs retained 13 months, SLOs we'll test in pre-prod.
[09:30] Anita: Correct.
[09:35] Evan: Timeline — pilot kickoff late Feb, 8-week run.
[09:39] Daniel: Action list and owners as we discussed. We'll share pricing and the onboarding runbook in the next 48 hours.
[09:48] Maya: I'll follow up with calendar invites for the smoke test and the deep-dive.
[09:55] Sofia: I'll send the KMS policy and compliance Qs by Thursday.
[10:02] Daniel: Great — any final questions?
[10:05] Anita: No, thanks everyone. Looking forward.
[10:09] Daniel: Thanks all — meeting adjourned.

References mentioned: onboarding runbook (link to be shared), SOC2+ISO pack (link to be shared), sample pricing spreadsheet (Daniel to share).

Notes on transcription quality: multiple minor mis-transcriptions of technical terms ("KV cache" shown as "K V cash" in an earlier doc). Speaker attribution generally correct but occasional short overlaps not captured.

Scaler AI: Customer Podcast Interview with Redwood

Date: 2025-03-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood Content), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Head of ML, Scaler AI), Diego Alvarez (CTO, Scaler AI), Rina Park (Marketing Lead, Scaler AI)
Recording: Fireflies.ai auto transcript
Notes: This was recorded as a marketing podcast / customer testimonial. Some transcription artifacts expected.
Short customer marketing interview focusing on Scaler AI's journey moving inference to Redwood Inference: topics include latency improvements, cost reduction, deployment modes (dedicated vs hosted), ease of rollout, and a few customer soundbites we'll use in a case study. Customer agreed to provide assets and sign a release waiver.
[00:00] Jordan Kim: All right welcome everyone, thanks for joining. This is the Redwood x Scaler AI customer interview recording. We're keeping it casual, we'll pull soundbites and a case study. Maya, want to kick us off with a quick intro to Scaler?
[00:23] Maya Chen: Sure yeah hi everyone, I'm Maya head of ML at Scaler AI. We do real-time personalization for long form content, and about a year ago we started hitting cost and latency problems as usage scaled.
[00:37] Diego Alvarez: And I'm Diego, CTO, we were evaluating a bunch of options open source, hosted APIs, tried batching on our own cluster, there was a lot of ops overhead.
[00:49] Jordan Kim: Great, cool. So how did you first hear about Redwood?
[00:55] Maya Chen: We saw the benchmarks and the open model catalog, and then uh Jordan's team reached out with a quick POC offer. The POC turned into a two month pilot.
[01:10] Priya Patel: Can you recall the first impression — like immediate benefits you noticed?
[01:17] Maya Chen: Yeah the first thing was latency consistency. Our p95 drops from about 1.2s to sub 600ms for the recommended model variant. So users notice snappier suggestions which matters for conversion.
[01:33] Samir Rao: Was that hosted or Dedicated?
[01:35] Diego Alvarez: We started on Hosted for dev then moved to Dedicated reserved pools. The predictability with dedicated GPUs was the key, predictability and cost per token.
[01:46] Rina Park: From a marketing perspective, the reduced latency made product demos easier for customer success — fewer excuses in demo. [laughs]
[01:56] Maya Chen: Also the Redwood console made rollout simpler — canary deploys, automatic fallback to lighter quantized variants when we had bursty traffic. That prevented a lot of 500s which we used to see.
[02:10] Jordan Kim: Nice. Any surprises in terms of total cost?
[02:14] Diego Alvarez: We saw about 28% savings month over month after we tuned batching and enabled prefix caching. Worth noting the initial committed costs looked higher but the unit economics improved.
[02:27] Maya Chen: Yeah total TCO went down once we accounted for reduced engineering time too; less time babysitting infra.
[02:36] Jordan Kim: Questions on security or compliance? We often get asked about SOC 2, private VPCs, KMS, etc.
[02:42] Maya Chen: Security was critical for us. We asked for SOC 2 type II evidence, KMS integration, and an option for private control plane with VPC. Redwood provided the SOC report and we ran a quick audit; that was fine.
[02:58] Diego Alvarez: We also pushed for retention controls — we wanted request logs short lived. Redwood's retention config and audit logs were acceptable.
[03:08] Samir Rao: We had a follow-up technical session where we walked through p50/p95 numbers and the KV cache behavior; any part of that stood out?
[03:17] Maya Chen: The automatic KV cache for repeated prefixes gave a big lift for our use case, a lot of identical prompt prefixes. But the transcript may say KV cash in places [laughs].
[03:29] Rina Park: [interrupting] Can I ask a quick marketing-y question — would you be comfortable with a short quote for the case study saying the percent improvement?
[03:36] Maya Chen: Yes, I'm okay with something like: "Redwood reduced our p95 latency by over 50% and lowered inference unit costs by nearly 30% while making rollouts much safer."
[03:48] Diego Alvarez: You can also mention we moved from a brittle in-house serving stack to Redwood's unified runtime.
[03:54] Jordan Kim: Great soundbites — Priya we'll capture those. Anything you want us to avoid mentioning?
[04:01] Maya Chen: Please don't publish internal SLA numbers beyond high level percentages, and don't include customer names in the background dataset example we discussed.
[04:10] Priya Patel: Noted, we'll send a release waiver.
[04:14] Jordan Kim: Switching gears — what about developer experience? How'd your engineers take to the SDK and API?
[04:20] Maya Chen: The SDK was very straightforward. The docs saved us a bunch of time; Samir's session with your SE team helped us optimize batch sizes and quantization profiles.
[04:31] Samir Rao: There was that one surprise where the tokenizer behavior differed slightly for a third-party model — we recommended tokenization checks.
[04:39] Diego Alvarez: Right, we had to change a couple pre-processing steps. Not a big deal but worth flagging.
[04:46] Jordan Kim: For the recording we'll cut out the technical deep dive but Samir can provide a short appendix for the case study.
[04:54] Maya Chen: Works for us.
[04:57] [05:00] Jordan Kim: Okay let's do a couple anecdotal bits — any wipes or stories about switching?
[05:07] Maya Chen: One funny thing: our SRE tried to battle the KV cache and accidentally disabled it in one test env, and we saw a mini meltdown — that proved how much the cache was helping.
[05:18] Rina Park: [laughs] That's going straight into the newsletter.
[05:22] Jordan Kim: Do you have a preferred quote length? One liner vs paragraph?
[05:27] Maya Chen: One liner for the header and a short paragraph for the case study body. Keep it punchy.
[05:33] Priya Patel: We'll draft two options and you can pick.
[05:36] Jordan Kim: Anything about onboarding timeline, keys, or legal red tape worth noting for other customers?
[05:42] Diego Alvarez: The onboarding was surprisingly fast. From POC to Dedicated move took about 6 weeks. Legal reviewed SOC2 and data processing addendum, which added another two weeks. So total six-eight weeks end-to-end depending on procurement.
[05:58] Jordan Kim: Helpful. Any metrics you want us to include in the case study aside from p95/p50 and cost reduction?
[06:04] Maya Chen: Maybe conversion bump on the product side — we measured a 3.2% lift in click-throughs on suggested content after improving latency. You can treat that as non-sensitive aggregated metric.
[06:17] Jordan Kim: Great. We'll ask Samir to attach the performance spreadsheet link in follow-up.
[06:23] Maya Chen: Another thing — the support from Redwood during the initial surge window was critical. Your on-call SEs were helpful.
[06:31] Jordan Kim: Thanks — I’ll pass that to the team. Do you mind if we pull Diego's CTO quote into the case study about moving away from in-house infra?
[06:39] Diego Alvarez: Fine with attribution.
[06:41] [06:45] Rina Park: Any assets format preference? Headshots, 1500px PNG or vector logos?
[06:50] Priya Patel: PNG or SVG for logos, headshot high res jpeg is fine. Also short bio (1-2 sentences).
[06:58] Maya Chen: We'll send those.
[07:02] Jordan Kim: Okay quick recap of next steps: Priya to draft release and quotes, Jordan will send the waiver, Samir will share perf spreadsheet, customer sends assets. Anything else?
[07:13] Maya Chen: We'll also confirm preferred quote language by Friday.
[07:17] Priya Patel: Cool. Any final off-script notes?
[07:20] Diego Alvarez: Just thanks, it's been a smooth collab.
[07:23] Jordan Kim: Awesome. We'll end recording here. Thanks everyone.
[07:28] [END RECORDING]

Note: timestamps above are approximate and the transcript contains occasional mis-attributions and small transcription errors (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "V-P-C" for VPC).

Kestrel Ventures Tokenflow & p95 Throughput Discovery

Discovery call focused on p95 latency targets and token/sec throughput for streaming chat workloads. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private due to compliance and burst traffic. Agreed to run benchmark and share pricing + security docs.
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-04-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam O'Reilly (CTO, Kestrel), Sana Patel (Platform Lead), Markus Li (SRE), Ana Gomez (Product)

Auto-summary (auto): Customer wants p95 under 600ms for streaming token flow during peak, tolerates slightly higher during cold starts; interested in Dedicated for burst windows but wants private for regulated pipelines.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intros, then we'll dive into traffic shapes and p95 goals.
00:18 Speaker 2 (Liam): Hey, thanks. Our primary thing is realtime summarization in the product, so streaming latency is the big one. We're trying to get p95 of, like, under 500ms for user visible tokens, otherwise the UX feels laggy.
00:35 Speaker 3 (Maya): Got it. When you say "user visible tokens" do you mean partial token flushes per streaming chunk or end-to-end response p95?
00:42 Speaker 2 (Liam): Partial streaming. We stream as the model generates. So p95 per token chunk is the key number.
00:50 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Okay, good. Can you share expected concurrency? tokens/sec peaks?
01:02 Speaker 4 (Sana): We see about 250 concurrent active sessions in the EU region during peak; average request length is 120 tokens prompt + 300 tokens response historically. Burst can go up to ~700 concurrent for a marketing campaign.
01:20 Speaker 3 (Maya): Quick note: that response length is substantial. For 300 tokens response, sustained token/sec and KV cache reuse matter a lot. Do you have any prefix reuse across requests?
01:34 Speaker 4 (Sana): Yes, lots of repetition—system prompt and a few contextual turns are similar across sessions. So KV cache should help.
01:42 Speaker 5 (Markus): Our constraints: infra is hybrid — primary in-cloud but some workflows must run on-prem for regulated customers. Also strict key management, we need HSM/KMS integration and audit logs.
01:55 Speaker 3 (Maya): That's fine. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; Dedicated has isolated capacity but still managed control plane, and Hosted is the fastest to get started. We can walk through lat/throughput tradeoffs.
02:10 Speaker 1 (Jordan): For p95 goals, are you targeting single-digit token latency or end-to-end?
02:16 Speaker 2 (Liam): Realistically we want p95 per partial chunk under 400–600ms during non-burst, and under 800–1,000ms acceptable during big bursts as long as we don't drop sessions.
02:28 Speaker 3 (Maya): Good benchmark to aim at. For a 300 token response streamed, you'll hit token/sec limits depending on model size and GPU type. What model families are you planning to run?
02:40 Speaker 2 (Liam): We're evaluating open models right now; want something high-quality but quantized for cost. Probably an LLaMA-derivative, 34B-ish.
02:52 Speaker 3 (Maya): Okay, that maps well to Redwood Dedicated profiles. We typically recommend 8xA100-equivalent for heavy streaming, but with quantization and kernel selection we can increase throughput. With prefix caching you can reduce effective compute per request.
03:07 Speaker 5 (Markus): Network jitter is a big factor for us; sometimes inter-region routing adds spikes. Do you do region pinning or fallback?
03:16 Speaker 3 (Maya): Yes — smart routing can pin traffic to a region and we have automatic fallback to adjacent region/model-variant to preserve availability. But that adds a little latency on failover.
03:26 Speaker 6 (Ana): Question on KV cache: how much does it actually buy us in real traffic?
03:32 Speaker 3 (Maya): In our experience with similar customers, when there's high prefix reuse you can see 30–60% reduction in consumed tokens and 20–40% latency improvement on p95, depending on model and batch sizes. But depends on hit rates.
03:48 Speaker 2 (Liam): Important for us: we can't accept any logs being stored in a shared control plane for regulated flows. Private offering needs to support air-gapped or VPC-only control.
03:58 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Understood. For Private we do offer on-prem packages; control plane can be customer-managed and logs kept behind your VPC. We'll share the security pack after this call.
04:10 Speaker 3 (Maya): Back to numbers — can I confirm your p95 target: 400–600ms per streaming chunk at 250 concurrency typical, with 700 concurrency burst up to 1,000ms p95 acceptable?
04:22 Speaker 2 (Liam): Yes that's right. Also want to look at token/sec throughput per GPU and cost.
04:29 Speaker 3 (Maya): For a 34B quantized model on an 8-GPU Dedicated pool, rough rule of thumb: sustained aggregate throughput ~6k–10k tokens/sec depending on kernel/quantization. With a single request producing 300 tokens, that implies X concurrency before you saturate — we can run a precise token/sec run with your prompt set.
04:50 Speaker 4 (Sana): Can you also test streaming tail-latency (first-token vs steady-state)? Our UI is sensitive to first-token latency.
04:58 Speaker 3 (Maya): Absolutely, we capture first-token latency and p95 for stream chunks. We'll include that in the benchmark.
05:05 Speaker 5 (Markus): For Dedicated, what's the autoscaling behavior during bursts? We don't want cold-starts that make p95 spike.
05:14 Speaker 3 (Maya): We have configurable autoscale with warm pool and burst capacity. You can keep a minimum number of instances warm to meet p95 SLOs; During sudden spike we have fallback policies to smaller model variants to keep latency bounded.
05:30 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Pricing note: Dedicated commits give you reserved capacity with lower per-token cost but you pay for baseline. Hosted is usage-based, higher unit cost but zero management. Private is a license plus ops. I'll send a cost model.
05:45 Speaker 6 (Ana): How do you measure p95 in streaming scenarios? Token boundaries vs chunk boundaries?
05:53 Speaker 3 (Maya): We measure both: first-byte latency, chunk p95 (n tokens), and end-to-end response p95. For dashboards we break them down per route/model.
06:06 Speaker 4 (Sana): Network: our egress limits may mean we need to colocate inference near customers. Do you support regional deployments?
06:13 Speaker 3 (Maya): Yes, Hosted has multiple regions; Dedicated can be provisioned in a chosen region; Private can obviously be on-prem. We'll document region options in the follow-up.
06:22 Speaker 2 (Liam): Can Redwood run a mixed strategy: Hosted for general traffic, Dedicated reserved for peak sessions, and Private for regulated customers?
06:30 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Absolutely — hybrid routing is a core pattern. You can route by policy: percent to Dedicated, failover to Hosted, and direct-regulated flows to Private.
06:39 Speaker 5 (Markus): Curious on observability — can we get token-level cost breakdown and per-token latency?
06:45 Speaker 3 (Maya): Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route p95, and trace hooks; you can export logs to your SIEM.
06:55 Speaker 4 (Sana): Anything about model fallbacks — is content and safety preserved when you downgrade to a smaller model during burst?
07:04 Speaker 3 (Maya): We recommend a canary test and quality gating; fallbacks preserve prompt context but quality will vary. We can set rollback thresholds based on evals.
07:13 Speaker 2 (Liam): Okay, high-level makes sense. Next, can you run that benchmark you mentioned with our prompt set? We want numbers: first token p95, streaming chunk p95, aggregate tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens on Dedicated vs Hosted.
07:31 Speaker 3 (Maya): Yes. We'll need sample prompts and a small dataset of representative sessions. Also, network conditions are important — if you can replicate jitter we'll do it in the run.
07:42 Speaker 4 (Sana): We'll provide a subset of 500 sessions and a synthetic burst plan.
07:49 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Great. I'll attach the cost model and SLA comparatives. Also sharing SOC 2 / ISO docs and PKI/KMS notes.
07:58 Speaker 6 (Ana): One last ask — can you show P95 drift over time? We need to know how p95 behaves under model updates.
08:06 Speaker 3 (Maya): We can set up quality monitoring tied to eval prompt sets and alert on regressions. That's part of Redwood Optimize.
08:15 Speaker 2 (Liam): Cool. Timing: we want to make a decision in two weeks if benchmarks show we can meet p95 at peak with reasonable cost.
08:23 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Sounds achievable. We'll aim to deliver benchmark results and pricing within 5 business days.
08:30 Speaker 5 (Markus): Small note: encryption in transit and at rest must conform to our compliance list — we'll email legal.
08:40 Speaker 3 (Maya): We'll include the compliance checklist.
08:45 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Recap — Jordan shares pricing + security pack, Maya runs benchmark with Kestrel prompts, Kestrel provides prompts + network profile, schedule Private architecture deep-dive if needed.
08:59 Speaker 2 (Liam): Thanks everyone, talk soon.
09:05 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Thanks, bye.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions where product names heard as "Redwood Privatee" or "KV cash". Speakers sometimes labeled generically. There was overlap at 03:30 with cross talk.

Customer is risk-averse on data residency. Strong candidate for hybrid approach: Dedicated for cost-sensitive steady-state and Private for regulated pipelines. Benchmarks will drive final commit.
Jordan to send Dedicated vs Hosted cost model spreadsheet (by 2028-04-21)
Maya to run a 1-hour token/sec benchmark with Kestrel sample prompt set (target week of 2028-04-24)
Liam to share SSO/SAML requirements and data residency note (by 2028-04-20)
Schedule on-prem/private deployment architecture review (tentative 2028-04-28)
Jordan Park | Share pricing spreadsheet and example SLA language | 2028-04-21
Maya Singh | Run 1hr benchmark on Dedicated 8-GPU pool with Kestrel prompts | 2028-04-26
Liam O'Reilly | Provide network egress limits & expected peak concurrency | 2028-04-20

document.content:
MedCore POC kickoff - open-model shortlist & benchmark plan

Kickoff to scope MedCore POC focused on selecting open-source models for clinical note understanding across English + Spanish, defining success metrics (accuracy, hallucination threshold, latency), sizing workload, and planning benchmarks and timeline.
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-05 14:30 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (MedCore Head of ML), Marcus Lee (CTO), Sophie Turner (PM)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
We scoped an initial POC to evaluate open models for clinical note understanding. Agreed on data share, target metrics (p95 latency <250ms for typical 256-token requests, throughput target // 50 RPS peak, accuracy/F1 targets), and a bench plan. Next steps: Redwood to provide shortlist and bench scripts; customer to upload sample data and acceptance criteria.

Topics: success criteria, model shortlist, quantization & cost, multilingual support, benchmark timeline, compliance.

Action Items (auto): see separate action_items field.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? I'm Avery, AE at Redwood Infer — sorry Redwood Inference, got the old nick in my head.
[00:12] Priya Desai: Hi, I'm Priya, I run the ML team at MedCore, mainly doing clinical NER and summarization.
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Marcus, CTO. We're sponsoring the POC, looking to see whether open models can get us near production accuracy at lower costs.
[00:26] Sophie Turner: Sophie, Product, will own acceptance criteria and stakeholder comms.
[00:30] Diego Ramos: Diego, SE at Redwood. I'll drive the performance side and help design the bench.
[00:36] Avery Chen: Great. High level: you asked us to help pick a shortlist of open models, size the workload for the POC, and run benchmarks comparing tradeoffs between quality and cost—especially for bilingual English/Spanish clinical notes, right?
[00:48] Priya Desai: Yep. We have a corpus of anonymized clinical encounter notes, about 10k records and we'd like to test NER, structured extraction, and a small summarization task. Multilingual mainly English with ~15% Spanish and a handful of Portuguese. Domain is heavy on medication names, laboratory values, and negation.
[01:05] Diego Ramos: Good to know. A few clarifying Qs: typical request size (tokens)? concurrency/peak RPS expectations? and any strict latency SLO?
[01:14] Marcus Lee: Typical prompt+response is around 180-400 tokens. Peak concurrent users could translate to 30-50 RPS during burst windows. For SLO, we'd like p95 latency under 250ms for single-turn structured extract calls, ideally closer to 200ms if possible.
[01:29] Sophie Turner: For accuracy, Priya's team will propose thresholds but intuitively F1 > 0.88 for key entity classes and hallucination rate < 2% on critical spans would be acceptance.
[01:40] Priya Desai: Yeah those are rough numbers; we'll formalize. Also we need audit logs and retention for 6 months — SOC2-relevant controls.
[01:48] Avery Chen: Perfect. On the model shortlist, we recommended starting with a mix of instruction-tuned and base models to compare quality vs cost. Our initial list: Llama 2-70B-instruct (hosted at lower perf), Mistral-instruct (33B), Falcon-180B-instruct (heavy but good open instr), Mosaic MPT-30B-instruct, and a domain-adapted small model (provisionally called xgen-med) that some partners have tuned. We can also include Llama 3-70B if you want — it's newer; licensing wise we should check.
[02:13] Priya Desai: Are those models good with Spanish? We need multilingual performance.
[02:18] Diego Ramos: Short answer: some are better than others. Mistral and Falcon variants tend to have decent multilingual capabilities when instruction-tuned, but you lose domain adaptation. For clinical lexicon, we expect the domain-adapted xgen-med or a fine-tuned Llama variant to outperform generic models at entity extraction.
[02:34] Marcus Lee: Cost-wise, what's the delta if we run a 70B vs 33B quantized to 4-bit on Redwood Dedicated?
[02:40] Diego Ramos: Ballpark: 70B full FP16 on GPUs will cost several x vs a 33B 4-bit quantized run. With Redwood's batching and KV caching, you can push effective costs down — for POC we typically test both a quantized 4-bit path and an 8-bit path to see quality deltas. We'll include per-1M-token cost estimates in the spreadsheet.
[02:57] Priya Desai: Is there an easy way to determine hallucination rates in our bench?
[03:02] Avery Chen: We'll define a set of gold spans and high-risk queries. The bench will compute false positive extractions and will flag hallucinations. Diego will add a hallucination-check script that compares model outputs to ground truth and also runs adversarial prompts.
[03:14] Sophie Turner: For timeline, how long would the POC baseline and then optimized runs take? We have a go/no-go decision point by end of April.
[03:22] Diego Ramos: Typical POC cadence: week 0 data ingest & baseline config, week 1 baseline runs across 3-4 models, week 2 quantized runs and additional caching/batching configs, week 3 final runs + analysis. That fits a ~3-4 week window. If you need end of April decision, starting immediately is necessary.
[03:37] Marcus Lee: Data ingestion — can we keep it in our VPC? Data privacy is key.
[03:42] Avery Chen: For POC we can do a few options: hosted with customer-provided S3 + presigned access + strict retention, or run on Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment if you want VPC connectivity. For the initial bench, presigned S3 and dedicated capacity is common. We'll also supply audit logs.
[03:58] Priya Desai: We will prefer VPC/Dedicated for the benchmark because of compliance reviewers, but presigned S3 is fine for the initial sample upload.
[04:06] Diego Ramos: Noted. On metrics collection: we'll capture p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost/1M tokens, F1 per entity, precision on critical spans, hallucination percentage, and regression checks vs our baseline model.
[04:18] Priya Desai: Baseline model meaning?
[04:20] Diego Ramos: Whatever you're currently using in production — if none, we'll pick a reasonable open baseline like a 13–30B instruct model. If you already have a provider model, please share sample outputs.
[04:29] Priya Desai: Currently we have a mix of vendor LLM+rules; I'll share the exports.
[04:34] Sophie Turner: For multilingual testing, do we need separate bench runs or can we mixed-batch?
[04:38] Diego Ramos: Best to run stratified tests: English-only, Spanish-only, and mixed. That tells us if quality drops on Spanish or if caching/batching helps mixed throughput.
[04:46] Marcus Lee: Any special hardware requirements? GPUs, inference optimizations?
[04:50] Diego Ramos: We'll use A100-like nodes for large FP16 runs; for quantized 4-bit we can use cheaper GPU types. Redwood runtime will pick kernels automatically, but we should document the hardware mapped to each model run in the bench spreadsheet.
[05:03] Priya Desai: What about tokenization differences across models for clinical abbreviations?
[05:07] Avery Chen: Good call-out. Tokenization and vocab coverage can affect extraction. We'll add a tokenization analysis to the bench (avg tokens per note, tokens for key spans). Some models tokenize 'mg/dL' differently which affects entity boundaries.
[05:19] Sophie Turner: On acceptance thresholds, we said F1 > 0.88. Is that realistic for off-the-shelf models?
[05:24] Diego Ramos: For non-adapted models maybe not; fine-tuning or prompt-engineering/chain-of-thought and retrieval augmentation improve results. We propose three acceptance tiers: baseline (no fine-tune), adapted (prompt + few-shot + retrieval), and tuned (fine-tune or LoRA). We'll show delta per tier.
[05:41] Priya Desai: How do we try retrieval? We have a vector store of clinical snippets.
[05:44] Avery Chen: Redwood supports a retrieval augmentation workflow. For the POC bench we'll simulate retrieval calls (embedding + KNN) and test a few cache/embedding dimensions; Diego will include retrieval latency in the end-to-end.
[05:55] Marcus Lee: Security — we need KMS integration and audit trail.
[05:58] Avery Chen: We support customer KMS for Private/Dedicated; audit logs are available and we'll produce a SOC2 artifacts packet. We'll attach our security brief in the follow-up.
[06:08] Sophie Turner: Back to models: can you rank the shortlist by expected cost/quality tradeoff?
[06:12] Diego Ramos: Rough ranking (quality -> cost): Falcon-180B-instruct (high quality, high cost), Llama3-70B (high qual, mid-high cost), Llama2-70B-instruct (mid-high qual, variable), Mistral-instruct-33B (good quality, mid cost), MPT-30B (mid quality, lower cost), domain xgen-med (if available, best domain quality but depends on tuning). We'll quantify this in the spreadsheet.
[06:36] Priya Desai: For the xgen-med model — is that something Redwood provides or a partner?
[06:40] Avery Chen: It's partner/tuning work — we can either test a partner-tuned artifact or run a LoRA fine-tune as part of POC. We'll note licensing and provenance in the doc.
[06:51] Marcus Lee: If fine-tuning is required, how long and how much data?
[06:54] Diego Ramos: For LoRA-style adaptation, 5–20k labeled examples can move the needle; full fine-tune is heavier. For POC we'll try LoRA/few-shot and see.
[07:04] Priya Desai: On hallucination measurement: how does the bench differentiate hallucinations from partial matches?
[07:08] Diego Ramos: We'll flag outputs that contain entities not present in ground truth and then run a manual review sample for false positives to calibrate thresholds. We'll provide a confusion matrix and an estimated hallucination rate with confidence intervals.
[07:19] Sophie Turner: Any advice on prompt templates for structured extraction?
[07:22] Diego Ramos: Use constrained output formats (JSON schema) and ask the model to refuse when uncertain. Also provide examples (few-shot) and include explicit anchors (e.g., "if not present, return null"). Results are more stable with schema enforcement.
[07:35] Priya Desai: Do you support function-calling style outputs that integrate with our downstream parser?
[07:38] Avery Chen: Yes — Redwood supports function/tool-calling and structured outputs; we can test that path in the bench.
[07:44] Marcus Lee: For cost calc, please show both hosted API and Dedicated reserved capacity options — we want to compare both economic models.
[07:51] Avery Chen: We'll include hosted per-token pricing estimates and Dedicated monthly capacity numbers plus an amortized cost per 1M tokens under expected utilization.
[07:58] Sophie Turner: Who will own the bench runs?
[08:00] Diego Ramos: Redwood will run baseline and quantized tests; MedCore will provide dataset and acceptance criteria; joint review session at end of each week.
[08:08] Priya Desai: Ok. One more: multilingual token labeling — will you score Spanish same as English? We need weighted metrics because Spanish sections are less frequent but higher impact.
[08:18] Diego Ramos: We'll provide per-language metrics and a weighted aggregate where you define weights. We'll also run a separate Spanish-only pass to ensure parity.
[08:27] Marcus Lee: Any red flags on latency with KV cache + streaming for our request sizes?
[08:31] Diego Ramos: KV cache helps for multi-turn; for single-turn structured extraction caching helps less unless many requests share prefixes. Batching and the right sequence length target are bigger levers. We'll test continuous-batching policies in the bench.
[08:44] Sophie Turner: Great. Let's recap and agree on dates.
[08:47] Avery Chen: Recap: Redwood sends shortlist & bench matrix by Friday 2025-03-07; MedCore uploads sample data and acceptance spreadsheet by 2025-03-10; bench baseline week of 2025-03-17; quantized + retrieval week of 2025-03-24; joint review and decision by end-April. Any objections?
[09:04] Priya Desai: Sounds good. I'll coordinate data upload.
[09:07] Marcus Lee: Fine. Please include SOC2 docs in follow-up.
[09:10] Avery Chen: Will do. Diego, anything to add?
[09:13] Diego Ramos: I'll prepare the perf scripts and a sample benchmark runbook. Also I'll include example prompts and the hallucination-check harness.
[09:22] Sophie Turner: Thanks all. We'll await the spreadsheet and schedule the baseline run.
[09:26] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone — meeting adjourned.

Note: transcript occasionally mislabels product names (Redwood Infer, redwood infra) and model tokens; this is expected in auto transcription.
Redwood: share open-model shortlist, cost/latency estimates, and benchmark matrix by 2025-03-07
Customer: provide redacted sample dataset (10k notes) + success criteria spreadsheet by 2025-03-10
Schedule baseline Dedicated latency/throughput run w/ Redwood week of 2025-03-17
Both: agree on evaluation metrics and acceptance thresholds by 2025-03-12
Avery Chen: Send model shortlist, quantization recommendations, and preliminary cost calculations; due 2025-03-07
Priya Desai: Upload redacted clinical notes (10k) and list of high-risk spans to S3 share; due 2025-03-10
Diego Ramos: Draft perf benchmark scripts and KV/prefix-caching config recommendations; due 2025-03-14
Marcus Lee: Confirm compliance gating (SOC2 scope and data residency) and share internal reviewers; due 2025-03-11

Weekly integration pulse — SDK function gating & structured output

Mid-poc sync focused on SDK integration issues: function-calling gating criteria, structured-output failures in one workflow, KV cache warm-up behavior and suggested tuning. Redwood to run larger latency benchmarks on dedicated pool; customer to share failing traces. Agreed to a technical deep dive after benchmark results.
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-30 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (StratusPay Lead Eng), Carlos Mendez (Platform Eng), Janelle Park (Product)

Summary (auto): quick sync to triage two main issues seen in the pilot: intermittent function-calling failures during heavy load and structured-output JSON schema drift for the payments reconciliation flow. Discussed KV (K-V) cache warm up and autoscaling policy tweaks.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check, audio ok?
[00:05] Priya Desai: yep good here, thanks maya.
[00:10] Maya Chen: awesome. real quick agenda — liam will go through the benchmark we've run lightly, then we want priya to walk through the failing output examples you uploaded, then triage next steps and gating for function-calling.
[00:25] Liam O'Neill: cool, i'll share my screen, but i also posted the quick gist link in the chat, it's the p99 tail run against a small dedicated pool with our default kv-cache settings.
[00:40] Carlos Mendez: i clicked it, seeing some odd spikes around the 10 minute mark. are those synthetic or real traces?
[00:48] Liam O'Neill: those are synthetic, we replayed a 10k request workload that mirrors your peak shape — the spike aligns with cache cold starts plus a rebalancing event on the worker nodes. sometimes the autoscaler overshoots then reconverges, so you'll see a short mid-run latency blip.
[01:05] Priya Desai: is the blip because of kv cache eviction? we've seen situations where the K-V cash isn't warmed for our long-tail customers and the first invocation trips a lot of overhead.
[01:15] Liam O'Neill: yep, kv cache warm-up and prefix cache misses are the main culprit. two levers we typically suggest: 1) aggressive pre-warm (provisioned prefix population) for known keys, 2) tweak batching window slightly to allow more aggregation at p50-sensitive endpoints.
[01:30] Janelle Park: that makes sense. our primary requirement is p50 under 200ms for interactive UI flows, p99 can be up to 1s but we'd prefer lower.
[01:40] Maya Chen: good to call that out. for gating, we usually propose p50 < 250ms and p99 < 800ms as an initial check for pilot workload, then tighten in production. is that reasonable?
[01:55] Priya Desai: sounds reasonable as a staging gate. we need to be mindful of cost though — provisioning extra warm cache or larger capacity has money impacts.
[02:05] Liam O'Neill: totally — Redwood Optimize will run a quick cost delta simulation once we pick a profile. i'll include that in the benchmark output.
[02:15] Carlos Mendez: ok, second issue: structured output. we had 6% of calls failing schema validation; i attached two failing payloads earlier. priya can you talk us through those?
[02:30] Priya Desai: sure — in the reconciliation path the model returns a list of "matches" but occasionally it's returning 'match' singular or an object with unexpected keys. sometimes it also emits stray commas or a top-level string. so the JSON parser errors out and downstream processors stop.
[02:48] Maya Chen: is this using the function-calling helper in the SDK or are you parsing text output?
[02:55] Priya Desai: a mix — primary flow uses the SDK function invocation; fallback does a text-to-JSON parse. failures are coming from the fallback path when the function call times out and we try to reconstruct.
[03:10] Liam O'Neill: that aligns with what we saw. the fallback parsers are brittle when the model is in a degraded mode or when the prompt gets very long. two mitigations: enforce stricter function signatures with required fields so the runtime rejects weird shapes, and add a simple shim on your side to coerce single objects into arrays when appropriate.
[03:30] Janelle Park: the problem is sometimes it's not coercible, there's context missing. we need to capture the exact prompt/response pair for investigation.
[03:38] Priya Desai: i'll upload the three representative failing prompt/response pairs we saw yesterday.
[03:44] Maya Chen: perfect — that will help liam reproduce. liam, are you able to run a replay with the exact traces?
[03:50] Liam O'Neill: yes, if priya uploads them to the shared drive i'll run them through our sandbox runtime and toggle the function-call timeout and the structured-output parser settings. i'll add the results to the ticket.
[04:05] Carlos Mendez: about the function-call timeout — currently we're using a 1.5s client timeout. i guess that's borderline?
[04:12] Liam O'Neill: 1.5s is tight for some heavier workflows. with dedicated capacity and warmed cache we usually see p50 ~120-180ms on our medium models, but spiky sequences with long KV lookups can push >500ms. increasing to 2.5s or adding a soft-deadline with early partial responses is another option.
[04:30] Priya Desai: what's the impact on token cost if we increase the timeout or change batching?
[04:36] Liam O'Neill: timeout alone doesn't change tokens; batching window increases tokens-per-batch but reduces CPU/GPU overhead per token so cost/unit tends to drop. there is a tradeoff with tail latency — more batching can increase p50 slightly but reduce p99 dedicated cost. we'll give you the delta numbers in the benchmark artifact.
[04:55] Janelle Park: can you also show us the quantization/precision profile you used in the dedicated pool? some of our legal folks ask about fp16 vs int8 artifacts and how that interacts with hallucination rates.
[05:10] Liam O'Neill: we used an int8-ish profile for the load test to be cost realistic, but we can re-run with a higher-precision profile. quick note: hallucination rates depend more on prompt engineering and evaluation harnesses than quantization for these models, but we'll include a short regression check.
[05:30] Maya Chen: switching gears, priya — you mentioned two failing structured-out JSON examples. can you paste the raw one now?
[05:38] Priya Desai: sure, here — response 1 shows an array but with mixed types: [ {"id": "abc123"}, "unexpected_string", {"id": "xyz"} ] — our validator fails.
[05:50] Liam O'Neill: thanks, that's a pretty clear parse mismatch. i'll try a stricter function signature and force the SDK to only accept top-level arrays of objects.
[05:58] Carlos Mendez: and what's the SDK behavior when the function returns non-JSON? does it surface the raw text?
[06:04] Liam O'Neill: yes, the SDK surfaces both the raw model text and the parsed payload if available. in your fallback path it's the raw text, so your parser is the last line. we recommend using the SDK's validate-and-normalize helper which will attempt coercions and return structured error objects.
[06:20] Priya Desai: we didn't realize that helper existed, that might simplify our integration.
[06:24] Maya Chen: we'll send a short code snippet highlighting the helper and suggested error handling patterns after the call.
[06:30] Janelle Park: great. question on security — our security team wants to confirm KMS key rotation and that Redwood does not see plaintext of customer-managed keys. status?
[06:40] Maya Chen: short answer: for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS and Redwood's control plane does not have access to your CMK private key material. for Hosted/Dedicated we provide envelope encryption patterns with customer-managed keys in supported cloud KMS providers — i'll attach our security whitepaper and SOC 2 addendum.
[07:00] Carlos Mendez: ok please attach that. also we need the VPC peering checklist — we hit a networking snag last week where the peering was set up but traffic restricted by an ACL.
[07:10] Maya Chen: will do. we'll add a short checklist and common ACL rules to the runbook.
[07:18] Priya Desai: back to performance — can you explain the autoscaler overshoot you mentioned earlier? is it the default kubernetes-based policy?
[07:26] Liam O'Neill: it's a custom autoscaler — it favors quick scale-ups to keep tail latency low, sometimes overshooting when there's a short-lived spike. tuning the cooldown window from 60s to 120-180s helped in other customers with similar bursty traffic. also tying scale triggers to application-level metrics (cache miss rate) instead of just cpu helps.
[07:48] Janelle Park: any risk to consistency or dropped requests when you extend cooldown?
[07:53] Liam O'Neill: minimal if you have a small burst buffer and prefix cache prewarm. the idea is to let a small transient spike be absorbed without spinning up many instances that later idle.
[08:05] Maya Chen: quick note — we also ran a canary with the function-call soft-fallback enabled which returns a structured partial result and a continuation token when the model can't complete. this reduced hard failures by ~40% in internal tests.
[08:20] Priya Desai: that continuation token idea could work — we could retry with a narrower prompt or hand off to a simpler heuristic process.
[08:28] Carlos Mendez: about telemetry — are you able to surface per-request input prompt size and token breakdown in the console? our ops team wants to correlate prompt length with failures.
[08:36] Liam O'Neill: yes, the console traces include token counts, per-token latency, and a kv-cache hit/miss tag if you enable the prefix-caching telemetry. we'll show you the fields in the dashboard export.
[08:48] Maya Chen: shall we pivot to timeline and gating: what needs to be green to move to next phase?
[08:55] Janelle Park: from product side: structured-output pass rate > 99% on smoke tests, p50 < 250ms for core flows, and documented mitigation for the remaining edge cases.
[09:05] Priya Desai: engineering wants reproducible benchmarks that match our traces and a plan for private key handling if we go Private.
[09:12] Maya Chen: ok so immediate items: 1) liam runs replay benchmarks, 2) priya uploads traces and failing payloads, 3) maya sends runbook + security attachments. any other blockers?
[09:24] Priya Desai: maybe one more — we saw an intermittent 502 from the SDK layer when a worker restarted. can you explain the retry semantics?
[09:32] Liam O'Neill: the SDK has exponential backoff with jitter by default for transient 5xx; it will retry up to 3 times with increasing delay. in your case we also saw a failing healthcheck that caused the worker to drain, which coincided with the 502. increasing graceful shutdown time on your side helped in one test.
[09:50] Carlos Mendez: ok we'll look at graceful shutdown.
[09:55] Janelle Park: question for sales — any change to pricing if we pivot to dedicated pool earlier?
[10:02] Maya Chen: pricing tiers for Dedicated are committed monthly capacity; we can discuss a short-term trial commit to prove performance with a billing credit offset — i'll follow up with a formal quote after the benchmark.
[10:15] Priya Desai: are there limits on model variants we can pin for dedicated? we wanted to try two small/medium variants side-by-side.
[10:22] Liam O'Neill: yes you can pin model families and we support multi-variant routing. that is part of the Dedicated configuration and we'll include suggested profiles in the benchmark report.
[10:33] Maya Chen: ok we're approaching the last 20 minutes — liam do you want to walk through a quick demo of the sandbox replay UI?
[10:40] Liam O'Neill: sure, small demo — i'll show the trace upload, the toggle for KV prewarm, and how we change the function-call timeout per route.
[10:48] [screen share noise] Liam O'Neill: here you can see the uploaded trace, we toggle prewarm and re-run; notice the p50 drops by ~70ms after prewarm.
[11:05] Priya Desai: curious — how do you determine which keys to prewarm? we have thousands of customer keys and can't prewarm all.
[11:12] Liam O'Neill: good question — we recommend a hot-key heuristic: prewarm keys that appear in the top 5% of traffic or those tied to SLAed flows. we also support an LRU-style warm window and targeted prewarm APIs.
[11:26] Carlos Mendez: could you share the script you used to generate the synthetic 10k workload so we can reproduce locally?
[11:33] Liam O'Neill: yeah i'll add it to the artifact bundle. it's in the gist link.
[11:38] Janelle Park: ok last item — can we agree on tentative dates for the deep-dive after the benchmark?
[11:45] Maya Chen: propose 2026-10-12 or 2026-10-13 for a 60–90 minute deep dive with your infra + security. which works?
[11:52] Priya Desai: 10/12 works for us.
[11:55] Maya Chen: great. i'll send a calendar invite after the call.
[12:00] [wrap-up silence]
[12:05] Maya Chen: recap — liam runs the full benchmark and posts results and cost delta by 10/07. priya uploads traces and two failing examples by 10/04. maya sends security runbook and VPC checklist by 10/01. deep-dive set for 10/12. anything else?
[12:20] Carlos Mendez: nope that's it from me. thanks all.
[12:25] Janelle Park: thanks, bye.
[12:30] Priya Desai: thanks, bye.

Notes about transcription: occasional word swaps (K-V cash instead of KV cache), timestamps approximate, some speaker labels simplified. Links referenced: gist://redwood/benchmarks/stratuspay-20260930, drive://stratuspay/trace-uploads, security://redwood/soc2-addendum.pdf

Quarter Zero Kickoff & Operating Theater

MEETING HEADER:
Date: 2026-01-08
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: All-hands - virtual (Zoom)
Attendees: Maya Patel (CEO), Leo O'Connor (CTO), Daniel Park (CFO), Ava Martinez (Head of GTM), Sara Nguyen (VP Product), Nina Kapoor (Reliability), Allie Chen (Eng), Tomás Rivera (Infra), Priya Khanna (Security), Jamal Edwards (Sales), Emily Zhao (Data Science), Riley Brooks (PM)
---
AUTO-SUMMARY (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Leadership framed "Quarter Zero" as a focused reset: stabilize core inference SLAs, trim nonessential projects, accelerate Dedicated sales pilots.
- Product to tighten model onboarding timelines and prioritize quantization/ops items.
- Reliability to run soak tests and revise SLOs; security to close three high-priority compliance gaps.
- Clear next steps and owners assigned; follow-ups scheduled.
---
TOPICS (auto):
1) Company posture and "Quarter Zero" narrative
2) Performance & reliability metrics update
3) Product roadmap reprioritization
4) GTM and sales motions for Dedicated / Private pilots
5) Security/compliance hot spots
6) Q&A and open-floor
---
TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya Patel - CEO: okay good afternoon everyone uh happy new year i know this is the first all hands for the year um so i wanted to start with a bit of context about what we're calling quarter zero, um it's not a new fiscal quarter it's uh a deliberate pause and tighten, right, um to make sure the platform is solid before we push more product surface area.
[00:18] Leo O'Connor - CTO: yeah and i'll add, technically we saw some regressions over the holidays with certain load patterns, the kv cache priming wasn't clearing like we expected so you'll see infra notes on that.
[00:29] Allie Chen - Eng: sorry can you say kv cache priming again i think i missed that?
[00:32] Leo O'Connor - CTO: kv cache priming, yeah basically some prefix cache warmed state persisted longer than intended and that caused OOMs in a tiny fraction of requests.
[00:41] Tomás Rivera - Infra: right we had two node groups that didn't drain properly, and the autoscaler policy didn't reconcile in time under the holiday traffic skew.
[00:49] Maya Patel - CEO: so the narrative here is twofold, one is stability, two is efficiency we need to show customers predictable latencies and better unit economics. that is what's going to unlock our next wave of Dedicated deals.
[01:08] Daniel Park - CFO: on the economics point, we ran a quick unit cost analysis versus our committed pricing and there's a gap, not huge but material. we need both batching and better quantization adoption to hit target margins.
[01:21] Sara Nguyen - VP Product: on product, we're pausing three lower-priority experiments, that frees up 2 FTEs and 4 GPU-weeks that we can reassign to model optimization and the deploy pipeline.
[01:31] Riley Brooks - PM: when you say pausing, is that an indefinite pause or timeboxed?
[01:35] Sara Nguyen - VP Product: timeboxed for 8 weeks, after which we'll reassess with metrics.
[01:39] [crosstalk] Multiple voices: okay, good.
[01:44] Nina Kapoor - Head of Reliability: runbooks are being updated, and we're planning a 48-hour soak starting next Tuesday on canary with realistic traffic replay. we'll capture latency p95/p99 deltas and cost regressors.
[01:56] Priya Khanna - Security: i want to flag three compliance items: 1) gap in audit log retention policy, 2) KMS rotation automation not fully hooked into private deployments, 3) missing documentation for on-prem packaging specifics. all are prioritised.
[02:11] Jamal Edwards - Sales: from the field, customers are asking for clearer SLAs and an easier path to on-prem pilots, they're also sensitive to vendor lock-in — we should script a clear migration story.
[02:25] Ava Martinez - Head of GTM: good, we'll build a pilot playbook that includes migration clauses, success metrics and a tech contact matrix.
[02:31] Emily Zhao - Data Science: quick question about evals, are we prioritizing per-route evals or model-wide evals for the regression alerts?
[02:39] Sara Nguyen - VP Product: route-level first, but we still need coverage on model regression suites for infra-facing changes.
[02:46] [05:00] Leo O'Connor - CTO: (presenting slide) okay here's the reliability dashboard we ran this morning, p95 sits around 340ms but p99 spikes to 2.2s under burst, and the tail is where customers feel the pain. the mitigations are threefold: batching improvements, cache TTL sanity checks and fallback routing to lighter quantized variants.
[05:20] Allie Chen - Eng: do we have a telemetry hook to see which customers saw the spike?
[05:24] Leo O'Connor - CTO: yes but it's noisy — infra will correlate trace ids with account ids tomorrow.
[05:30] Tomás Rivera - Infra: and i should note the canary cluster uses a different kernel set, so performance numbers aren't 1:1 but they do show the regressions.
[05:42] Maya Patel - CEO: moving to GTM, Ava?
[05:45] Ava Martinez - Head of GTM: thanks, quick overview: we'll run three Dedicated pilot plays this quarter, targeted to mid-market SaaS and one enterprise in fintech. pricing will be conservative — we need to lock in the economics first. Jamal will lead the fintech effort with support from solutions engineering.
[06:03] Jamal Edwards - Sales: to clarify, fintech pilot — expected timeline?
[06:06] Ava Martinez - Head of GTM: 6-8 weeks from pilot start to production checklist if no blocker; we need security sign-off within 10 days.
[06:13] Priya Khanna - Security: yes that's tight but doable if they agree to our standard controls; for anything custom we need additional legal review.
[06:20] Daniel Park - CFO: and finance will table a pricing floor — we can't discount below X for dedicated until we see better unit costs.
[06:27] [09:15] Sara Nguyen - VP Product: product reprioritization detail: the top three dev tasks are kernel selection automation, batch scheduler tuning, and model quantization baseline. that covers 65% of expected cost upside.
[09:31] Emily Zhao - Data Science: about quantization, are we standardizing on 8-bit or exploring fp16/qlo?
[09:36] Leo O'Connor - CTO: we'll test multiple paths; 4-bit research is ongoing but for now we operationalize 8-bit/ptq as the default.
[09:44] Riley Brooks - PM: does that change the testing matrix for compatibility?
[09:47] Allie Chen - Eng: slightly, yes — we need more fuzz testing on model outputs under quantized paths.
[09:53] [12:00] Nina Kapoor - Head of Reliability: the incident queue had three repeat items we want to close: autoscale reconciliation, disk pressure on long-lived pods, and tracer ingestion spikes. we'll swap in additional alert thresholds and add a backlog ticket per repeat incident.
[12:14] Tomás Rivera - Infra: disk pressure one was exacerbated by stale logs during a backup job, we've got a patch to rotate logs more aggressively.
[12:22] Priya Khanna - Security: for tracer ingestion we should obfuscate PII at ingestion, that's a requirement for some of the regulated customers.
[12:31] [15:00] Maya Patel - CEO: okay i want to highlight three asks of leadership: 1) be ruthless about priorities, 2) protect engineering focus time, 3) communicate openly with customers about "quarter zero" rationale.
[15:18] Leo O'Connor - CTO: and engineering leaders, please mark any projects that touch inference cost in the tracker by end of week.
[15:27] Jamal Edwards - Sales: i'll sync with our top 10 accounts and surface any immediate SLA concerns.
[15:33] [18:00] Audience Q&A:
[18:05] Speaker 7 - Kevin: hi quick thing, will this affect headcount or hiring freezes?
[18:10] Sara Nguyen - VP Product: short answer: no immediate hiring freeze, but we're re-allocating some reqs; detailed plan will come from people ops.
[18:17] Speaker 8 - Lila (Eng): will we get more dedicated time with SEs for pilots? last time that was a bottleneck.
[18:23] Ava Martinez - Head of GTM: yes, we'll book a rotating SE schedule for pilot weeks and create a playbook so SEs know the templates.
[18:30] [22:00] Maya Patel - CEO: i'd also like to surface risk tolerances — we will accept short-term throughput reduction if it buys reliability, but not indefinite performance losses. we need concrete rollback plans.
[22:15] Nina Kapoor - Head of Reliability: agree, rollback automation is on the roadmap and we'll prioritize canary rollback safety checks.
[22:22] Daniel Park - CFO: on budgeting, expect a small reserve to cover pilot costs, we won't be dipping into runway but it will be reflected in Q0 forecasts.
[22:31] [26:00] Mini lightning reports:
[26:05] Allie Chen - Eng: infra feature flag work is merged, small risk on e2e tests flakiness.
[26:11] Tomás Rivera - Infra: canary soak plan submitted, replay traffic dataset attached in the ticket.
[26:16] Priya Khanna - Security: SOC2 doc refresh is 70% done, scheduling audit window.
[26:21] Emily Zhao - Data Science: eval baseline updated, will publish notebooks.
[26:25] Riley Brooks - PM: roadmap doc to be circulated after this meeting.
[26:30] [32:00] Open mic / harder questions:
[32:04] Speaker 2 - Jordan: does this change our public messaging or will customer-facing comms be quiet?
[32:09] Maya Patel - CEO: we'll have a short blog post about focus and stability but no major PR. messaging will reassure customers about SLAs and pilot pathways.
[32:18] Speaker 3 - Priya S: are we deprioritizing any strategic bets long-term?
[32:22] Sara Nguyen - VP Product: they're timeboxed; strategic bets remain but we'll stage them.
[32:27] [38:00] Leo O'Connor - CTO: technical deep dive quick note — model routing changes are being tested to allow fallback to smaller quantized variants when latency SLOs breach, this is not a feature toggle yet but it's in the canary group.
[38:18] Allie Chen - Eng: we should ensure telemetry labels are consistent across fallback paths.
[38:22] Tomás Rivera - Infra: agreed. infra will add a check for tag consistency.
[38:28] [44:00] Security corner:
[44:03] Priya Khanna - Security: for Private deployments, we need a clearer KMS playbook and standard templates for network setup. we also need to close a doc gap for on-prem packaging. i'll share a one-pager.
[44:16] Maya Patel - CEO: perfect, make that one-pager actionable and we'll review before pilot sign-offs.
[44:23] [50:00] Final recap and alignment:
[50:12] Ava Martinez - Head of GTM: recap — three Dedicated pilots, pilot playbook by 01-11, pricing floor by finance, SE rotation schedule, and customer comms draft.
[50:26] Nina Kapoor - Head of Reliability: reliability follow-ups: canary soak next Tuesday, rollback runbook, tracer ingestion fix.
[50:36] Sara Nguyen - VP Product: roadmap reprioritization doc to be published 01-12, quantization and batching are top priorities.
[50:47] Daniel Park - CFO: finance to publish a brief on unit economics and pricing floors by 01-11.
[50:54] Maya Patel - CEO: thanks everyone, thank you for candidness. smaller teams will meet to operationalize this plan. expectation is weekly syncs and a mid-quarter review.
[51:05] [Closing chatter/people leaving]>
[55:00] Riley Brooks - PM: will we have a shared dashboard for progress?
[55:04] Nina Kapoor - Head of Reliability: yes, a simplified Q0 dashboard will go up in confluence and i'll send a link.
[55:12] Jamal Edwards - Sales: i'll prioritize the fintech pilot kickoff next week.
[55:17] Maya Patel - CEO: great thanks, meeting adjourned.
---
