LucidMesh Integrator Onramp Discovery — Redwood + LucidMesh

Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and LucidMesh to evaluate an integrator onramp. Covered architecture options (hosted vs private/VPC), security/compliance, pilot scope and test plan; agreed on delivering documents and sample workloads for benchmarking.
[00:00] Evan (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for taking time — Evan from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Ari (LucidMesh CTO): Ari here.
[00:08] Priya (LucidMesh): Priya here.
[00:10] Sam (LucidMesh): Sam on infra.
[00:12] Maya (Redwood SE): Maya here, will take the technical run.
[00:15] Jordan (Redwood): Jordan — solutions eng.
[00:18] Evan: Cool, thanks. Agenda — quick intros, high-level goals for the integrator onramp, constraints (security / VPC / data residency), then dive into technical patterns and pilot scoping, then next steps.
[00:31] Ari: Sounds good. For context: LucidMesh is building an enterprise search/agent layer for our OEM partners. We're evaluating partners to help with inference at scale — especially private deployments and OEM routing. The thing we want to avoid is doing the whole serving infra ourselves.
[00:44] Priya: And to add, our legal/compliance folks will require SOC2 + audit logs, plus KMS integration. We also have a few regulated EU customers asking for EU-only residency.
[00:55] Maya: Good to know. On Redwood side we support three main deployment modes — hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC or on-prem). For integrator onramp, most partners choose either a VPC private control plane or a dedicated reserved pool that we can route to.
[01:12] Sam: Quick question — what does the private option look like? Is Redwood running control plane in our VPC or do we bring a runtime bundle?
[01:21] Jordan: There are a couple options. The private deployment we usually do is a customer-managed VPC with a lightweight control plane that talks back to Redwood for management metadata; optionally we can ship an on-prem bundle for air-gapped setups. For LucidMesh, VPC-hosted control plane + customer-managed GPU nodes would be the sweet spot if you want network isolation.
[01:40] Ari: And the data flows — are prompts or payloads ever persisted on Redwood side? We need guarantees around PII retention.
[01:47] Maya: Good point. We have configurable data retention. For private deployments, we can ensure request payloads never leave your VPC; logs and metrics can be forwarded to your SIEM. For hosted API, we have options to opt out of retention and we provide audit logs + tokenization options and KMS for encryption.
[02:05] Priya: KMS — we use Azure Key Vault and sometimes Hashi HSM. Will Redwood integrate with customer KMSs?
[02:12] Evan: Yes, we integrate with common KMS providers — AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM integrations for enterprise. We can document the exact flow.
[02:20] Ari: Great. On performance: our models are latency-sensitive — sub-150ms tail for short-turn completion on some routes. Does Redwood support low-latency routing and KV-cache to help with that?
[02:33] Maya: We have a GPU-optimized runtime with KV cache management and prefix caching. Realistically, low 100ms tails are achievable on some model+GPU combos for short sequences, but it depends on batching, quantization, and the exact model. If you need strict SLOs, dedicated capacity pinned to GPU pools is the most reliable.
[02:52] Sam: So the trade-off is cost vs latency? If we pin dedicated GPUs we pay more but reduce the variability?
[02:58] Jordan: Exactly. We also have smart routing: you can set policies to route high-SLO traffic to premium pools and lower-priority requests to cheaper quantized variants. That helps manage unit cost.
[03:11] Ari: Do you support autoscaling within a dedicated pool? Our workload is bursty — big spikes during partner demos.
[03:18] Maya: Yes — dedicated pools support autoscaling with configurable warm pools and burst capacity. We can set autoscale policies that prefer hot warm instances so cold-starts are rare.
[03:27] Priya: On networking, for VPC private control plane, what's the ingress model? We want to ensure no public IP egress for customer data.
[03:34] Jordan: Typically we use private peering or customer-managed NAT with strict egress rules. The control plane only needs minimal connectivity for registration and metrics if you want centralized updates; otherwise we can run a fully offline runtime that only speaks to your internal telemetry.
[03:45] Sam: Any gotchas with Kubernetes deployments? We run a 1.25 cluster and use Nvidia GPUs with MIG profiles on the nodes.
[03:52] Maya: We support K8s 1.24–1.26 officially, but in practice our runtime is fairly portable. MIG is supported but performance tuning is required — charge for smaller MIG slices can affect throughput. We'll need to test.
[04:04] Ari: What about quantized model variants? We sometimes tolerate a small quality drop for cost savings. How does Redwood suggest quantization profiles?
[04:12] Maya: Redwood Optimize component generates quantization and model recommendations per workload; we can run a sensitivity test during pilot to show quality vs cost curves. We typically run evals on your prompt set and return delta metrics (exact-match, bleu-ish, or custom evals).
[04:28] Priya: From a partner perspective, how do you see commercials? Are there partner tiers for integrators?
[04:34] Evan: Yes — we have partner tiers: marketplace integrators, resellers, and strategic partners. Each has a mix of referral fee, discounted committed capacity, and co-marketing credits. I'll share the one-pager after the call.
[04:47] Ari: Good. For pilot scoping — what would you propose as a minimal realistic pilot to validate both performance and integration friction?
[04:55] Jordan: Typical pilot: 2–4 weeks, run on a small dedicated pool (1–3 GPUs depending on model) with representative prompt corpus you provide, measure latency, cost per 1k tokens, and functional regressions. We'll also run a small canary to exercise failovers and routing.
[05:10] Sam: We can provide a dump of our traces for three main customer flows — search, follow-up Q, and agent-initiated summarization.
[05:17] Maya: Perfect. We'll use those for the KV/prefix caching tests. Also we'll instrument the token-level cost and per-route dashboards so you can see where costs are occurring.
[05:28] Priya: Security review — are you SOC2 Type II? And do you provide penetration test results?
[05:33] Evan: We're SOC2 Type II compliant; we can share the report under an NDA. We also have penetration test summaries and third-party attestations.
[05:41] Ari: Data residency — we need EU-only for a couple of clients. Can you pin region routing?
[05:46] Jordan: Yes, routing policies can pin by region and we also support private deployments inside EU cloud regions or on-prem within EU for full data residency.
[05:56] Sam: On operational side, how are incidents surfaced? We want alerting hooks and a runbook for escalations.
[06:02] Maya: The Console exposes per-route alerts, traces and model-level error budgets. We can integrate with PagerDuty/Slack/Teams; we'll agree an escalation matrix in the pilot plan.
[06:13] Priya: One risk we have: network egress cost with cloud GPUs. If Redwood routes traffic externally during fallback, that could spike egress. How do you mitigate that?
[06:23] Jordan: Fallbacks are policy-driven. For private deployments we avoid external fallbacks unless explicitly enabled. For hosted customers, we suggest cost-aware policies that degrade to smaller quantized models rather than crossing regions. We'll include egress estimates in the pilot costing.
[06:37] Ari: Any existing integrations with SI partners we should be aware of? We have a preferred systems integrator list and want to ensure compatibility.
[06:44] Evan: We maintain a partner catalog and many SI partners already integrate with Redwood. We'll map your SI list and check compatibility — I'll follow up.
[06:51] Sam: On the runtime side, are there proprietary kernels or is everything standard like cuBLAS/cudnn?
[06:57] Maya: We use a mix — some optimized kernels for attention patterns and fused ops. In some cases we fall back to standard libs; performance profiles will show kernel-level breakdowns.
[07:07] Ari: One more on evaluation metrics — besides latency and cost, we need hallucination/regression checks. Can you run baseline vs our current stack?
[07:15] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll take your prompt set and measure outputs from your baseline and Redwood-served models, then run diff/eval and surface false positive / factuality metrics. Redwood Optimize can detect regressions and alert on quality drops.
[07:28] Evan: Okay, want to recap action items and timeline?
[07:31] Priya: Sure.
[07:32] Evan: From Redwood: we'll send partner one-pager + pricing tiers (Evan), security artifacts under NDA, and a draft pilot scope (Maya/Jordan). From LucidMesh: sample traces, prompt corpus, and a stakeholder list including procurement/legal timelines (Priya/Sam/Ari). Agreed targets — the one-pager by 2026-09-03, pilot draft by 2026-09-07.
[07:55] Ari: That timeline works. Our procurement window is end of Q3, so we'd like to kick pilot in early Oct if possible.
[08:02] Maya: Early Oct pilot is realistic if we get the artifacts in the first two weeks of September.
[08:08] Sam: We'll start packaging up the traces today. Expect upload within a week.
[08:13] Evan: Any blockers from security right now? Priya?
[08:16] Priya: No blockers, but legal will need the SOC2 and the KMS flow doc before sign-off.
[08:21] Evan: Noted — we'll share those.
[08:24] Ari: A couple quick nitpicks — what about multi-tenant isolation if we run multiple OEM partner tenants on the same pool?
[08:31] Jordan: We support tenant isolation at runtime via namespace-level KV caches and per-tenant models; we can also pin tenants to separate pools when higher isolation is required.
[08:42] Priya: And do you provide RBAC integration with our existing SSO? We use Okta and SCIM.
[08:47] Maya: Yes — SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported, along with fine-grained RBAC.
[08:52] Sam: Last question: do you keep model weights or is that in our control?
[08:56] Evan: For open models we host the weights; for cases where customers want to bring-your-own-weights (BYOW), we can support private weight hosting in your VPC or a customer-owned object store. We'll map options in the pilot doc.
[09:08] Ari: Great. Thanks everyone, this felt efficient.
[09:12] Evan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
[09:16] Maya: I'll include an initial pilot scoping template.
[09:19] Jordan: And I'll add a checklist for infra readiness (K8s version, MIG profile notes, network peering).
[09:25] Priya: Okay — thanks.
[09:26] Sam: Thanks all.
[09:27] Ari: Bye.
[09:28] Evan: Bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache, "MIG slices" heard as "MIG sizes"), speaker labels sometimes generic — left as recorded. References / artifacts mentioned: partner-one-pager (link to be sent), Redwood SOC2 summary (NDA), pilot scoping template (to be shared).

Meeting length: 55 minutes (roughly covering all topics above; timestamps are approximate and condense sections).

document.content:
Governance & Log Export Orchestration review w/ Zenosia Tech

Redwood walked Zenosia through what admin/activity/audit logs are captured, options for streaming and batch export to customer destinations, encryption/KMS patterns including CMEK and HSM options, retention and legal-hold patterns, and an orchestration approach for high-throughput exports. Action items: Redwood to share export throughput worksheet, KMS integration guide, and a proposed POC plan to validate 1Gbps sustained exports to Zenosia S3 bucket.
Jordan to send KMS integration guide and SOC2 audit extracts (by 2026-11-27)
Priya to share export throughput worksheet and sample NDJSON logs (by 2026-11-26)
Schedule POC kick-off (customer wants week of 2026-12-07)
Zenosia to provide destination S3 bucket details and contact for networking
Jordan Lee (Redwood) — Send SOC 2 summary + evidence pack link by 2026-11-27
Priya Raman (Redwood) — Export throughput worksheet + sample NDJSON (2026-11-26)
Marcus Hsu (Zenosia) — Provide S3 bucket ARN and cross-account role by 2026-11-30
Lina Alvarez (Zenosia) — Share internal SIEM schema requirements (no due date yet)
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM); Marcus Hsu (CISO, Zenosia), Lina Alvarez (Infra Eng), Trevor Ng (Cloud Ops)

Summary/Context: Zenosia is evaluating Redwood for inference serving but has strict audit/export requirements for regulated lines of business. They want to understand exactly what admin and activity telemetry is captured, where it can be exported to, how keys are handled, and retention/legal hold patterns.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Marcus: Marcus here.
[00:08] Lina: Lina — hi.
[00:09] Trevor: Trevor here.
[00:11] Jordan: great. Priya and Samir from our side too — Priya will walk through the log model and export options. Samir will cover support/SLAs.
[00:22] Priya: thanks. I'll start with what we typically capture: admin actions (create/update/delete of routes, model pinning, role/permission changes), user-level API events (token usage, request metadata), system telemetry (scheduler events, autoscale activity), errors and tracebacks, and important security events like failed auth, token revocations, and KMS key usage logs.
[00:45] Lina: when you say user-level events, do you capture full prompt text or just metadata?
[00:51] Priya: good q. Defaults: hosted plan redacts customer prompt content for shared-hosted; dedicated and private deployments can keep full request payloads depending on customer config and data residency needs. We surface both high-level metadata and, when requested via config, full request bodies — that is typically gated by contract and retention rules.
[01:12] Trevor: is that redact automated or manual? we need deterministic controls for audits.
[01:16] Priya: it's automated. We have a mask-and-redact pipeline — you can choose token-level redaction, regex-based PII masks, or full payload retention. The setting is per-deployment.
[01:28] Marcus: SOC 2 auditors will want immutability and chain-of-custody for admin actions. How do you support immutable exports?
[01:35] Jordan: we support immutable delivery to customer-owned storage. For example, we can write NDJSON batches to an S3 bucket with object lock enabled (compliance mode), or stream events via Kafka to a customer-managed cluster. We also support signed, time-windowed download artifacts for snapshots.
[01:52] Priya: to add — for Dedicated/Private, we can ship logs direct to your SIEM (Splunk/Elastic/BigQuery) via secure connectors. For hosted, we stream via TLS and sign events with Redwood's HSM when requested, or with customer-managed KMS for CMEK flows.
[02:14] Trevor: CMEK — do you support AWS KMS CMKs and HSM-backed keys?
[02:18] Priya: yes. For AWS we do cross-account key usage patterns: Redwood can encrypt logs at rest with customer CMKs; for more stringent needs we integrate with HSM-backed KMIP providers. There is an extra attestation step and we'll have security to review, but we have customers running CMEK.
[02:34] Lina: curious about key rotation — if we rotate the CMK, do earlier objects become unreadable?
[02:40] Priya: typical AWS KMS envelope encryption pattern handles rotation. Old objects remain decryptable as long as the key policy allows (we recommend re-encrypting if you want to rekey older objects). We can provide a re-encryption job as part of the POC if you want.
[02:58] Marcus: retention policies — we have a 7-year regulatory retention for some admin trails, but we also need short-term indexes for quick lookups. How do you reconcile?
[03:06] Priya: common pattern: short-term hot store (searchable index retained 90-180 days), and long-term cold archive where raw NDJSON/Parquet is written to S3 with lifecycle rules. We support manifest files and partitioned Parquet for efficient later queries.
[03:24] Jordan: and for legal hold we can flag objects with S3 object lock or add a retention flag in the manifest so nothing is auto-deleted until hold is released.
[03:33] Trevor: about throughput — we need to export ~1Gbps sustained for peak jobs, with spikes to 3Gbps. can your streaming pipeline handle that?
[03:42] Priya: yes, but we need to validate with a POC. Our export worker pool scales horizontally; we'll provide a throughput worksheet that maps ingestion rate to export worker count and expected egress. For very high sustained egress, we recommend a dedicated export cluster in your VPC.
[04:00] Marcus: networking — cross-account roles, signed URLs, or do you expect inbound pulls from our side?
[04:06] Jordan: options: push via cross-account role and PutObject to your S3; push to Kafka over TLS (mutual TLS); or provide a pull endpoint if you prefer to pull snapshots. Push with cross-account IAM role is common — we create a role and you grant PutObject.
[04:18] Lina: does Redwood store the destination credentials? we prefer you not hold long-term creds.
[04:22] Priya: we avoid long-term customer creds; we either assume role (short-term sts) or use signed ephemeral credentials that rotate. For pull models we provide signed URLs that expire.
[04:34] Trevor: audit log format — is it JSON, NDJSON, Parquet?
[04:38] Priya: primary format is NDJSON (one JSON event per line) for maximal compatibility. We can optionally batch to Parquet for cost-efficient long-term storage. Each event contains a consistent schema: timestamp, event_type, actor_id, actor_role, resource, action, before/after delta (if applicable), request_id, model_version, latency_ms, region, and optional obfuscated request/response.
[04:59] Marcus: will auditors accept that schema?
[05:02] Priya: we've worked with auditors; we provide a mapping document and sample extract. For SOC 2 we provide evidence bundles — snapshots of config, key rotation records, and export manifests.
[05:15] Jordan: another question — do you need per-route token-level cost breakdown or just admin action audit?
[05:20] Marcus: both. we need to show who changed model pins and who ran what requests for privileged users.
[05:26] Priya: we capture admin actor context (SSO identity, IP, session id) and API-level actor (token ID). We correlate tokens to SSO principals via our identity sync logs; we include SAML assertion IDs when available.
[05:40] Lina: SSO/SCIM sync events — do you log SCIM deltas (user add/remove) with old/new?
[05:45] Priya: yes, SCIM provisioning events are captured as admin events with before/after. We can also integrate with your IdP for push notifications.
[05:55] Trevor: what about RBAC — is there an audit trail that shows permission escalation?
[05:59] Priya: every role change is an admin event with actor and rationale if provided. We store the JSON diff and the state snapshot at time of change to support forensics.
[06:12] Marcus: hypothetical: a rogue admin rotates keys and wipes logs. are logs protected?
[06:18] Jordan: that's where separation of duties and immutable exports help. If you route logs to your S3 with object-lock, Redwood cannot delete them. Also we support write-only cross-account roles which prevent deletion by Redwood principals. For on-prem/private setups, we recommend a dedicated write-only collector in your network.
[06:36] Priya: also internal RBAC: our control plane has RBAC and admin actions are gated by roles. We store approval flow events for high-privilege ops.
[06:45] Marcus: can you push logs to our SIEM in near-real-time and also keep a backup stream to S3?
[06:50] Priya: yes — typical pattern is dual-write: stream live to SIEM via Kafka and batch snapshots to S3 every X minutes. We can also mirror to a cold bucket for long-term retention.
[07:03] Trevor: do you do signing of events? we need cryptographic proof of integrity.
[07:07] Priya: we support HMAC signing per-record and optional CMS/CAdES signatures at object level. For high-assurance customers we sign events using an HSM and provide the public verification keys and log to a transparency ledger.
[07:19] Lina: interesting. what's the operational burden for key management if we require HSM signing?
[07:24] Priya: slightly higher; we need more frequent audits and a KMS attestation. We'll codify requirements in the KMS integration guide.
[07:33] Samir: I can jump in on SLA and support. For export reliability we have SLAs on delivery success for Dedicated customers — we alert on failed deliveries, retry with backoff, and escalate to ops. For hosted, delivery is best-effort but we provide guaranteed retention windows.
[07:51] Marcus: curious about failure modes — if an export fails for 24 hours, what happens to data?
[07:56] Priya: we buffer in an internal durable queue (encrypted), with retention for up to configurable days. We try multiple delivery paths — if primary fails, we spill to an alternate (S3 snapshot) and notify you. We'll include those retention numbers in the worksheet.
[08:14] Trevor: an ask — can you produce sample logs that match our SIEM mapping so our parser team can validate?
[08:19] Priya: absolutely; I'll send NDJSON examples and a sample Parquet partition.
[08:24] Jordan: ok let's run a quick scenario — Lina, say you want to prove who pinned a model and when, and capture the full request payload for the top 10 calls that day. How would you do that?
[08:34] Lina: we need an auditable trail plus snapshots with payload for sampling.
[08:38] Priya: we'd mark the route to retain full payload for 30 days, log the admin change event with before/after, and emit a snapshot job to S3 for the top N requests. We'll tag snapshots with retention_policy: 7y if required.
[08:52] Marcus: for retention policies — do you have UI controls or is it config-as-code?
[08:57] Priya: both. Redwood Console provides per-route retention settings and export scheduling. For Dedicated/Private you can also configure via YAML manifests and Git-integrated deploys.
[09:07] Trevor: any PII scanning built in? we need to avoid storing SSNs in logs.
[09:12] Priya: we have built-in PII detectors (regex and ML-based) and you can apply automatic redaction on detection. But we recommend defense-in-depth: pre-send client-side masking and server-side redaction.
[09:24] Marcus: one more on residency — some data must remain in EU. Does your export pipeline support region-limited egress?
[09:30] Jordan: yes. We can route exports to region-specific endpoints. For hosted we keep data in-region for supported clouds and can route export workers to EU-only egress. For private/on-prem you control egress entirely.
[09:42] Lina: about monitoring — are export delivery metrics surfaced in Console?
[09:46] Priya: yes, you get per-export throughput, error rates, latency, and per-object checksums plus delivery success logs. We also emit export-level Prometheus metrics and CloudWatch logs if you want.
[09:58] Trevor: what about schema evolution — if you add fields to events, will older ETL break?
[10:03] Priya: schema is versioned. Each event has schema_version and we maintain backward compatibility; for heavy changes we write adapters in the manifest so your parsers can migrate.
[10:14] Marcus: legal hold flow — if we put hold on a run of objects, who has to request release?
[10:19] Jordan: policy-driven: release requires an authorized admin (your side) and a legal approver. Redwood will not release objects on your behalf. For hosted, we store hold metadata in a tamper-evident ledger and require signed release calls.
[10:32] Lina: ok curious: have you done a SOC 2 audit that covered these export controls?
[10:36] Jordan: yes — SOC 2 Type II included controls around log capture, retention, and export for customers on Dedicated/Private. We'll ship the SOC 2 report and the control mapping for export flows.
[10:46] Marcus: cool. can you include the control mapping for our compliance team?
[10:49] Jordan: yes, action item noted.
[10:51] Priya: technical note on latency: the export pipeline is asynchronous; live SIEM streaming typically has 3–10s lag, snapshots depend on batch frequency. For cryptographic signing there's extra CPU overhead — we can run a signing farm if needed.
[11:08] Trevor: if we want immutable logs but also need to correct metadata (e.g., tag misclassification), what's the pattern?
[11:13] Priya: we don't alter immutable objects. Instead we write compensating records: a correction event that references the original object id. That preserves immutability but allows auditors to reconstruct corrected state.
[11:25] Marcus: how do you surface attribution if multiple admins share SSO accounts?
[11:29] Priya: we log session ids and SAML assertion IDs; if accounts are shared it shows the shared principal. We can also enable higher-fidelity—MFA challenge records and per-user authn logs — to help disambiguate.
[11:41] Jordan: ok let's pivot to the POC outline — Priya, can you propose a minimal POC to validate export semantics and throughput?
[11:48] Priya: sure. Phase 1: export schema validation — we push sample NDJSON to your test bucket and confirm parsers. Phase 2: throughput test — we run synthetic event generation to target 1Gbps sustained for 30 min and validate delivery and retries. Phase 3: legal hold and CMEK — we test object-lock and decryptability via your CMK. Deliverables: worksheet, sample logs, and a runbook.
[12:12] Marcus: timeline? we prefer to kick off first week of Dec.
[12:15] Jordan: we'll aim to deliver the artifacts by 2026-11-27 so you can schedule.
[12:20] Trevor: network/firewall question — do you need inbound ports opened?
[12:23] Priya: only for mutual TLS or if you host a Kafka endpoint that requires inbound. For S3 PutObject push, no inbound is needed — it's outbound from Redwood.
[12:33] Lina: regarding logs containing model outputs — we may want to retain small samples for quality checks. Is that handled separately from admin logs?
[12:40] Priya: request/response samples are in the request logs bucket; retention is configurable separate from admin audit trails. We can also create a sampled dataset that strips PII for QA.
[12:50] Marcus: ok any blockers on your side to doing the POC?
[12:52] Priya: none. We'll need the bucket details, a cross-account role if S3 push is chosen, and CMK ARN if you want CMEK.
[12:58] Samir: I'll include support contact and escalation matrix in the POC plan.
[13:03] Trevor: one more: do you provide a playbook for auditors? sometimes they ask for direct evidence collection steps.
[13:09] Jordan: yes — we provide an auditor playbook that shows how to collect snapshots, map events to controls, and verify signatures. We'll include that in the evidence pack.
[13:20] Marcus: that helps.
[13:22] Jordan: ok let's move to quick Q&A.
[13:25] Lina: do you keep admin logs for deleted users? we need to show historical access after user removal.
[13:31] Priya: yes — admin logs are immutable and include before/after user state. Deleting a user does not remove their historical events.
[13:38] Trevor: are you able to redact specific fields post-hoc if compliance requires?
[13:43] Priya: post-hoc redaction of immutable archived objects is not typical; we perform compensating records or re-encryptions. For eg if a field must be removed, we can re-encrypt and re-upload a sanitized object to the archive and mark original as superseded, or we can provide a trimmed extract for auditors. We'll document the workflows.
[13:59] Marcus: good. I think that's most of our concerns. Can you confirm the deliverables and dates?
[14:05] Jordan: yes — deliverables: KMS integration guide, SOC2 summary and control mapping, export throughput worksheet, sample logs (NDJSON and Parquet), POC runbook. Delivery by 2026-11-27. POC kickoff week of 2026-12-07.
[14:20] Marcus: accepted. I'll get the bucket details by 2026-11-30.
[14:23] Jordan: great. thanks all.
[14:25] (meeting ends)

References shared: KMS integration guide (link will be sent), sample NDJSON files (attached later), POC runbook (template). Customer emphasized dual-write to SIEM + S3 immutable archive. Redwood to validate 1Gbps POC. Auditor playbook requested.

document.content:
Governance & Risk Triage - MSA/DPA/SLA Pricing Handoff

Intro call to align legal/procurement/security on MSA/DPA/SLA terms, pricing model choices (hosted vs dedicated), KMS/egress expectations, and next steps for pilot paperwork. Customer wants clear commitments on data residency, audit logs, and an optional dedicated path for PII workloads. Action items assigned for pricing worksheet, security pack, and pilot SOW.
MSA redlines and timeline
DPA clause questions (subprocessors, data residency)
SLA uptime/latency targets and remedies
Pricing model: hosted per-token vs dedicated commitment
KMS/HSM key options and egress fees
Pilot SOW and benchmark cadence
Samir Patel | Send pricing worksheet with both hosted and dedicated scenarios | 2025-08-01
Jules Kim | Share technical benchmark spreadsheet and proposed latency SLOs | 2025-08-04
Aria Gomez | Upload SOC2 report, data flow diagram, and DPA template link to shared drive | 2025-07-30
Priya Ramesh (Customer) | Provide list of required DPA redlines and minimum SLA clauses | 2025-08-06
Redwood to circulate pricing scenarios and optional dedicated commitment template
Customer legal to send DPA redlines; Redwood legal to review and schedule follow-up
SE to run a short latency/cost benchmark with Peregrine sample prompts next week
Schedule follow-up call with procurement + legal on 2025-08-07 to review redlines
Meeting header: 2025-07-28 15:00 PDT — Duration 58m — Recording: yes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Kim (Redwood SE), Aria Gomez (Redwood CSM); Maya Torres (Peregrine Procurement), Evan Li (Peregrine InfoSec), Priya Ramesh (Peregrine Legal), Noah Grant (Platform)

00:00 Samir Patel: All right, good afternoon everyone thanks for making the time. quick intro — I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on your account, with Jules on the technical side and Aria who will be helping with onboarding.
00:14 Maya Torres: Hi all, Maya here, thanks. we wanted to get procurement + legal and security aligned before we go into a pilot. few things on the docket: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, and pricing tolerances.
00:28 Jules Kim: Great, we'll run through the typical playbook; apologies in advance if I mis-say any of your internal names, still learning some of the org.
00:36 Priya Ramesh: No worries. we're mostly concerned about data residency and subprocessors in the DPA; also need to confirm audit log retention and exportability.
00:47 Evan Li: And keywise — KMS/HSM; we need to understand whether Redwood's KMS integration allows customer-controlled keys for private deployments, and what the egress billing model looks like.
01:02 Samir Patel: Yes — at a high level we offer three deployment modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem. For PII workloads customers usually prefer Dedicated or Private with customer-managed KMS. For hosted, we have envelope encryption and can do BYOK via KMS integration but there are nuance — we'll put the details into the security pack.
01:26 Maya Torres: Pricing wise, procurement is nervous about per-token variability. we'd like to see a committed monthly spend for the pilot with a blended price for tokens and an option to switch to dedicated after acceptance.
01:40 Samir Patel: Totally reasonable. Typical approach: pilot with a small committed amount on hosted, then if you need predictable unit economics we map you to a Dedicated commit with burst capacity. The pricing worksheet I'll send will show examples: 3 months pilot, 50k USD commit, estimated token throughput, and break-even points for Dedicated.
01:59 Noah Grant: Quick question — if we go dedicated, can we pin model versions? we need stable outputs for regulatory reviews.
02:08 Jules Kim: Yes, Dedicated lets you pin model versions and control rollout. We also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to older variants. There's a model pin field in the deployment config.
02:21 Priya Ramesh: On the DPA, we have two particular asks: subprocessors list up front, and a clause about data residency for EU patient records. also need a 90-day data deletion guarantee post-termination.
02:36 Samir Patel: Subprocessors list is something we provide; we can include a committed list and a change notification process. deletion windows are typically 30-90 days depending on the plan; for Private deployments we can do shorter since data never leaves your VPC. We'll capture the exact language in the DPA template.
02:55 Maya Torres: Can you clarify audit logs? our auditors want immutable access logs for 12 months and the ability to export them to our SIEM.
03:06 Aria Gomez: We retain per-request logs for 12 months under our enterprise retention option, and we can export via S3 push or syslog integration. There are settings for token-level redaction before export.
03:20 Evan Li: And about SLA: uptime is one thing, but latency tails are critical. If an LLM endpoint has a 95th percentile of 200ms today, we want a commitment for 95th at no more than 300ms for the pilot. what's your policy on remedies?
03:36 Jules Kim: We publish model/region latency profiles and we can set SLOs per route. For Dedicated we can set hard SLOs, and remedies are typically service credits; severe breaches escalate to engineering and can trigger buyback clauses in rare cases. We'll capture the exact numbers in the SLA doc.
03:56 Priya Ramesh: Service credits are fine but we need a cap and also an operational runbook that explains fallbacks.
04:06 Samir Patel: Absolutely. We'll include a runbook: routes to canary, fallback to cheaper model family, and a contact SLA for incident responses.
04:15 Maya Torres: Egress — if we move datasets between regions for regulatory reasons, who covers the transfer fees?
04:23 Samir Patel: Egress fees are typically borne by the customer; we'll itemize egress in the pricing worksheet. For Dedicated with reserved capacity we can negotiate a different egress allowance.
04:35 Noah Grant: For the pilot, we want to run privacy-sensitive prompts and measure both latency and cost. can you run a bench with our sample prompts?
04:44 Jules Kim: Yes, send a small sample set (we need 50-200 requests representative of tails) and we'll run it against two model families and two quantization levels. We'll return a spreadsheet with per-token cost and latency percentiles.
05:00 Maya Torres: We'll need to see the benchmark methodology, i.e., sequence length assumptions, KV-cache warmup, and concurrency profile.
05:10 Jules Kim: We'll include methodology notes; often the transcribing engine makes assumptions about KV cache; we'll make it explicit.
05:20 Priya Ramesh: On the MSA front: we have a few finance asks — indemnity caps and governed liability. who handles redlines?
05:29 Samir Patel: Our legal team typically takes the DPA/MSA redlines and responds; simple redlines we turn around in 3-5 business days, more complex ones take longer. We'll ask you to send the annotated MSA and DPA and we'll route to legal.
05:41 Maya Torres: Can you email your standard MSA with comments and point persons? procurement wants to track on our side.
05:48 Aria Gomez: I'll upload the MSA and DPA template to the shared folder and cc Samir and Jules, plus the SOC2 and architecture diagram. link: https://redwood.example.com/share/peregrine-onboarding (note: placeholder)
06:05 Evan Li: A technical nit — for BYOK with cloud KMS, what are the rotation policies and can we audit key usage?
06:14 Jules Kim: Key rotation is customer controlled for BYOK, and we surface key usage logs via the audit trail. For on-prem HSMs we can support customer-run attestation.
06:24 Priya Ramesh: Do you offer a data escrow option for long-term regulatory retention?
06:29 Samir Patel: We have partners for data escrow; it's not standard but enterprise customers can add it as an add-on. We'll surface options and rough cost in the pricing packet.
06:40 Maya Torres: Ok timeline — Procurement needs a draft MSA/DPA by next week to route to finance. Is that feasible?
06:47 Samir Patel: We can push an initial draft DPA and our standard MSA by Thursday; full redline response after we get your annotated version.
06:55 Noah Grant: One more: is there an established path for FedRAMP / higher compliance? even if you're not FedRAMP'd today, we need to understand roadmap.
07:05 Aria Gomez: We have a compliance roadmap and a list of controls; I'll include the compliance roadmap doc and the timeline for audits.
07:12 Maya Torres: Great. can you also outline the onboarding schedule for a quick pilot — we want a 2-week pilot: week 1 ingest + setup, week 2 run benchmarks and do acceptance.
07:23 Jules Kim: Sounds good. We can do a 2-week pilot. Week 1: access, sample dataset ingestion, baseline run. Week 2: benchmarking, quality checks, acceptance criteria runbook. We'll include an SOW template.
07:36 Priya Ramesh: For the acceptance criteria — we'll need reproducible outputs for a small prompt set and a cost target not to exceed X per 1k tokens.
07:46 Samir Patel: We'll make the acceptance criteria explicit in the SOW and include cost guardrails.
07:52 Maya Torres: Ok wrapping up, any open items?
07:55 Samir Patel: Recap: Redwood to send pricing worksheet, security pack (SOC2, architecture, DPA draft), technical benchmark method and spreadsheet. Peregrine to send annotated MSA/DPA redlines and sample prompts for bench. We'll schedule procurement/legal follow-up on 2025-08-07.
08:12 Priya Ramesh: Sounds good thanks everyone.
08:16 Maya Torres: Thanks all, talk soon.

End of recording.

document.content:
Skylark Retail - Security decision criteria intake

Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-08-30 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~44 minutes
- Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood); Priya, Carlos, Ellen (Skylark)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
Skylark exploring Redwood for customer-facing recommendation and chat features. Primary gating items are SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO (SAML) + SCIM onboarding, RBAC for multi-tenant access, end-to-end encryption options (customer KMS), and audit log retention for 7 years. They are evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private due to data residency and regulated PII workloads. Next step is a technical deep dive focused on KMS integration and audit log schema.

Topics: SOC2 evidence, ISO controls, SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data retention/TTL, hosting (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), sample compliance docs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we'll go round and then jump into what you're trying to solve.
[00:06] Priya: Hi, Priya here, Head of AI at Skylark. We're looking to add chat and product recommendation LLM features to our mobile app but need to make sure security and compliance line up first.
[00:12] Carlos: Carlos, security engineer. I'll be owning the KMS and logging questions.
[00:15] Ellen: Ellen, CTO — timing is Q4 but we need security gating this quarter.
[00:20] Maya: Great. Liam from our infra team will cover the nitty gritty later. High level — are you leaning hosted, dedicated, or private?
[00:28] Priya: We started with hosted for speed, but a handful of payment and returns flows include PII. Our legal ops pushed back — likely want dedicated or Private for specific workloads.
[00:37] Maya: Totally understandable. To clarify, Redwood Hosted can be used with strict retention and encryption defaults, but Dedicated gives isolated capacity and Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full customer network control.
[00:46] Priya: Quick question — SOC2 and ISO, what can you provide? We need at least SOC2 Type II and a gap map for ISO 27001 controls.
[00:55] Liam: We have SOC2 Type II report and an ISO control mapping doc. I can send redacted artifacts. For audits, we also supply a control implementation narrative — that shows where Redwood's controls meet ISO clauses.
[01:03] Carlos: Is the SOC2 covering encryption key management if we use customer-managed keys? We need to know what responsibilities fall on us vs Redwood.
[01:10] Liam: Good callout. For Hosted with customer KMS we have a split responsibility model: you manage key rotation and HSM/backing in your KMS, while Redwood stores only encrypted blobs and performs crypto ops with transient access tokens. We can provide a diagram of the crypto flow.
[01:22] Ellen: Do you support AWS KMS, GCP KMS and an HSM option? Some of our infra is hybrid.
[01:28] Liam: Yes — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and we support customer HSM via PKCS#11 for Private/on-prem. For Dedicated we can plug into your cloud KMS through secure peering.
[01:36] Priya: On SSO, we use Okta with SAML and SCIM. We'll want RBAC meshes for dev/prod separation and granular model access controls.
[01:44] Maya: Redwood supports SAML and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based with custom roles; you can lock down API keys to routes and models, and audit all token issuance.
[01:52] Carlos: How granular? Can we restrict who can run embeddings vs who can deploy model rollouts?
[01:56] Liam: Yes — roles can restrict generation, embedding, reranking, and rollout actions, plus environment scoping (prod vs staging). We also expose an audit log stream with event types for auth, model inference, model deploy, and admin actions.
[02:08] Priya: About audit logs — retention and tamper evidence are big. We need immutable logs for 7 years and schema that includes request headers, masked prompts, response latency, model version, and the user id.
[02:18] Liam: We ship audit logs to your SIEM via TLS syslog or Kafka, and retention policy is configurable. For Hosted, we can provide a forwarded stream; for Dedicated/Private you keep logs within your VPC. Tamper-evidence can be achieved with append-only storage and checksums; we can share implementation notes.
[02:31] Carlos: Masked prompts — we can't send raw PII. Do you offer prompt redaction or client-side encryption for prompt bodies?
[02:37] Liam: Currently we recommend client-side tokenization or redaction if prompts contain PII. For Private deployments you can run a pre-processor inside your network to tokenize prior to sending. There's also an in-transit encryption plus at-rest using your KMS for model caches and stored KV.
[02:52] Priya: If we keep certain flows on Hosted, how do you guarantee data residency? Some EU customers require EU-only processing.
[02:58] Maya: We have region-based hosts and routing policies. You can pin traffic to EU regions; for strict residency we'd recommend Dedicated in the region or Private in your cloud region.
[03:08] Ellen: Any blockers for using function/tool calling with Private? We have internal tools that the model needs to call.
[03:14] Liam: Function/tool calling works with Private; you'll host the tool endpoints inside the same VPC and Redwood's runtime will make outbound calls over private networking. We can discuss NAT/proxy requirements in the deep dive.
[03:24] Maya: Pricing/commitment aside, what are your success criteria for security sign-off?
[03:29] Ellen: For us: (1) SOC2 evidence + ISO control mapping, (2) SAML+SCIM and RBAC that fits our org, (3) KMS support with clear responsibility docs, (4) audit log delivery and retention, (5) data residency guarantees.
[03:40] Priya: Also, we need a plan for regression monitoring; if prompt quality drops after quantization or rollout, we need rollback hooks and eval sets.
[03:48] Liam: Redwood Optimize includes rollout controls and can tie regressions to eval prompts. For Dedicated/Private you can pin model versions and configure automatic fallback to a baseline model.
[03:59] Carlos: On the audit logs format — can you give a sample JSON schema? We want to map fields into our compliance lake.
[04:05] Liam: Yes, we'll include an example schema in the follow-up (event_type, timestamp, actor_id, auth_method, model_id, request_hash, masked_prompt, response_token_count, latency_ms, region).
[04:16] Priya: About retention: legal might require some logs to be retained for 7 years but the prompts to be purged earlier for privacy. Can you do tiered retention?
[04:24] Liam: Yes — audit metadata can be retained long-term while payloads (masked_prompt, raw_response) can have shorter TTLs. We'll surface config options in the retention matrix.
[04:33] Maya: Any non-negotiables from your side we should know?
[04:36] Carlos: We need ability to rotate encryption keys without service interruption, and proof that key deletion removes access to cached KV.
[04:44] Liam: Key rotation with minimal interruption is supported; we use envelope encryption so rotating the master key rewraps data. For cached KV we can evict or re-encrypt. We'll detail expected failover windows.
[04:55] Ellen: What about pen tests and external attestation? We may require vendor pen test results or permission to include Redwood in our vendor sweep.
[05:01] Maya: We perform internal security testing and share summaries; for customers pursuing deeper assurance we can support a quick third-party test coordination.
[05:09] Priya: Good. Can you also send a sample contract clause language for data processing and KMS responsibilities?
[05:13] Maya: Yup, legal will provide standard DPAs and KMS annex.
[05:17] Carlos: I want to schedule the deep-dive — 60–90 minutes — focus on KMS integration (AWS/GCP), audit log delivery (Kafka/syslog), and RBAC mapping.
[05:26] Maya: I'll get Liam and our solutions engineer scheduled. Suggested slots in week of Sep 6?
[05:30] Priya: That works.
[05:32] Maya: Ok last quick notes: I'll send SOC2 redacted report, ISO mapping, security deck, and a short security FAQ link: https://redwood-inference.com/security-docs. Liam will attach KMS diagrams and sample audit schema.
[05:44] Ellen: Great, thanks.
[05:46] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with next steps and calendar invites.
[05:50] [END]

References/Shared artifacts mentioned:
- Redwood security deck (link above)
- SOC2 Type II (redacted)
- ISO control mapping spreadsheet (will be attached)
- Sample audit log schema (to be provided)

Call wrap/recap (auto):
- Redwood to provide SOC2/ISO artifacts and security attachments
- Schedule technical deep dive for KMS and audit logs
- Customer to send retention and dataset privacy categorization

This transcript contains auto generated speaker labels and timestamps; occasional transcription errors are expected.

POC weekly: capacity readiness & burst runbook

Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-18
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Carlos Ruiz, Priya Nair (Redwood); Tom Alvarez, Nina Park, Harold Bennett, Aisha Khan, J. Lee (LumenPay)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, optional):
- Weekly POC sync focused on Dedicated sizing, autoscale policy tuning, and burst capacity rehearsal.
- Agreed to run a staged 30-minute burst test on staging and iterate autoscale thresholds.
- Redwood will provide sizing/cost delta doc and a concrete runbook for priming KV cache and graceful degradation.

Topics: Dedicated sizing, autoscale thresholds, burst pool, KV/prefix cache priming, fallback models, SLOs, security checkpoints

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do status and then a focused section on burst planning and autoscale knobs, sound good?
[00:12] Tom Alvarez: Yup, that'll be great, want to make sure we're comfortable for Friday's spike rehearsal.
[00:18] Carlos Ruiz: Quick note, I tweaked the autoscale policy based on the telemetry last week, increased the ramp window from 60 to 90 seconds to reduce oscillation.
[00:26] Nina Park: We saw the jitter but also a small tail at p99, is that related?
[00:30] Carlos Ruiz: Possibly, the longer ramp helps steady throughput but can add a little tail latency under sudden surges — it's a tradeoff.
[00:38] Harold Bennett: We're okay with a slightly higher p99 for the demo, but for production we want p95 under 300ms if possible.
[00:45] Maya Chen: Right, so quick recap of current POC numbers: staging on Dedicated pool, model: opt-6B-q4 (note: shorthand), average throughput ~1.8k tokens/sec across the pool, median latency ~120ms, p95 ~260ms, p99 ~520ms during the 2nd-week surge test.
[01:05] Aisha Khan: That p99 number is concerning if we hit 3x traffic. What's the plan to handle 3x?
[01:12] Carlos Ruiz: We have two levers: 1) pre-warm burst pool (reserve extra nodes) and 2) aggressive autoscale with instant burst capacity. The burst pool is basically a hot standby that can accept traffic without cold start.
[01:22] Tom Alvarez: Can you explain the pre-warm steps? Last time it took longer to warm the KV cache and we saw a lot of regen.
[01:30] Priya Nair: Yeah so priming the KV/prefix cache is key — if you replay representative traffic first we can populate KV cache and reduce regen cost. We'll include curl examples in the runbook.
[01:40] J. Lee: From security, are there any extra considerations for a burst pool? e.g., network isolation, KMS keys, audit logs?
[01:47] Maya Chen: Great point — for Dedicated we can provision burst instances within your VPC and they inherit the same KMS/HSM keys and audit streaming. We'll include the SOC 2 / audit log mapping in the doc.
[01:57] Nina Park: Awesome. Also can you confirm the instance types? Are we on H100 or A100? That affects warmup time.
[02:04] Carlos Ruiz: Currently the Dedicated pilot is using A100-80GB equivalents. If you want H100 we can run a variance estimate but that will change cost numbers.
[02:12] Harold Bennett: Cost is important — we're trying to model the delta between a larger steady pool vs. a smaller steady pool + burst.
[02:18] Maya Chen: We'll send a spreadsheet with modeled scenarios. Example: steady 6 GPUs vs. steady 4 + burst 3 for peaks. The steady+burst tends to be cheaper by ~18% for your traffic shape, but that assumes good cache hit rates.
[02:34] Tom Alvarez: What's the cache hit rate threshold to see that saving?
[02:38] Priya Nair: Generally >60% prefix/KV cache hit gives you the cost leverage because fewer tokens are recomputed. If hit rate drops below ~40% then steady pool is preferable.
[02:47] Aisha Khan: How do we measure that in our telemetry?
[02:50] Carlos Ruiz: We'll send the exact metrics: kv_cache_hit_ratio, average_batch_size, token_compute_per_sec, p95_latency_by_route — those are in the Console traces.
[02:58] Maya Chen: For the runbook itself, propose three phases: 1) staging burst rehearsal (30 min), 2) canary rollout to 10% traffic with live metrics and auto-fallback to a smaller model if latencies creep, 3) full switch.
[03:12] Tom Alvarez: The fallback to smaller model — you mean model routing to a quantized variant?
[03:16] Carlos Ruiz: Exactly, e.g., route to opt-6B-8bit or a distilled variant if latency > threshold. That reduces token cost and latency.
[03:24] Nina Park: Are the model variants pre-installed on the burst pool or do they cold start?
[03:28] Priya Nair: We recommend pre-pulling the variants used by the fallback. The runbook will include a pre-pull phase to avoid cold-starts.
[03:35] Harold Bennett: Ok. For the rehearsal, what are the triggers for manual intervention vs automated rollback?
[03:40] Maya Chen: Triggers we suggest: sustained p95 > 400ms for 3 minutes, error rate above 1%, or queue depth increasing > 30% for 2 minutes. Any of those should trigger automatic rollback or a model fallback.
[03:52] Aisha Khan: Can we get the exact thresholds editable in the console?
[03:55] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, those are configurable per-route in the Redwood Console; we'll share screenshots.
[04:00] Tom Alvarez: About priming — you mentioned a tool to replay traffic. We'll need read-only access to Redwood's staging endpoint and a secure S3 path to drop logs and replay script?
[04:12] Maya Chen: Correct, we'll set up a short-lived API key scoped to staging endpoints. Tom, please send the S3 path and we will confirm access.
[04:18] Tom Alvarez: Will do.
[04:20] [pause - a few seconds of typing/crosstalk]
[04:28] Maya Chen: Quick run through of autoscale policy parameters: min_replicas, max_replicas, scale_up_threshold (requests/sec per replica), scale_down_cooldown, ramp_window, burst_pool_size, and burst_grace_period.
[04:40] Nina Park: What did you set scale_up_threshold to for last test?
[04:43] Carlos Ruiz: We set it to 400 reqs/sec per replica, max_replicas 12, and burst_pool_size 3. That gave us the >1.5k tokens/sec sustained.
[04:52] Harold Bennett: If we expect 3x traffic, should we set max_replicas higher?
[04:56] Priya Nair: Depends on budget — the runbook includes two presets: conservative and aggressive. Conservative keeps max_replicas lower but requires larger burst_pool; aggressive raises max_replicas and shrinks burst reliance.
[05:08] Maya Chen: For Friday's rehearsal we recommend the conservative preset first so we can test priming and warmup. Then next week try aggressive.
[05:15] Aisha Khan: What's the expected warmup time for the KV cache during priming?
[05:19] Carlos Ruiz: For your traffic we estimate roughly 8-12 minutes to reach steady-state cache hit above 60% if the replay covers top 80% of routes.
[05:27] Tom Alvarez: Good to know. We'll schedule the replay to start 20 minutes before the rehearsal window.
[05:32] Maya Chen: Perfect. Next I want to call out fallback policies — when we hit the threshold, do we prefer model downgrade or region fallback?
[05:40] J. Lee: Region fallback raises compliance questions for us, prefer model fallback.
[05:44] Harold Bennett: Agreed. Model fallback first, region fallback only if absolutely necessary.
[05:48] Priya Nair: We'll add a route-based priority chain in the runbook: 1) throttling (graceful degradation), 2) model fallback, 3) spill to alternative region with explicit approvals.
[05:58] Maya Chen: On instrumentation, please make sure you have traces for per-token compute time and batch size breakdown per replica so we can correlate latency spikes.
[06:06] Nina Park: We have Datadog ingest for most metrics — will Redwood export to our DataDog?
[06:10] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, we can forward metrics to your Datadog API key; we previously set that up in the sandbox. We'll reconfirm the metrics list.
[06:17] Aisha Khan: Anything about compliance we should be aware of for the burst pool?
[06:21] Maya Chen: No different from Dedicated; burst nodes are provisioned in your VPC and inherit same KMS and audit log pipelines. We'll include required operation checklist for SOC 2 and data residency.
[06:30] Tom Alvarez: On costs again — can you give an example run number of cost for a 30-minute burst with 3 A100s?
[06:36] Carlos Ruiz: Rough back-of-envelope: a 30-min burst with 3 A100s is about X dollars — exact will be in the spreadsheet because it depends on reserved vs on-demand pricing and your commitment level.
[06:45] Harold Bennett: Okay, we'll review that.
[06:47] [brief silence, keyboard sounds]
[06:52] Maya Chen: Let's capture concrete next steps — do we have agreement to run the staging rehearsal Friday at 11:00 PT?
[06:58] Tom Alvarez: Yes, Friday 11:00 PT works for us.
[07:02] Nina Park: I'll be on call for the replay and SRE checks.
[07:05] Maya Chen: Great. I'll send calendar invites and the runbook link. Carlos will attach the priming scripts.
[07:12] Carlos Ruiz: I'll also include a simple script to generate traffic with ramp profiles and a CSV of the top 200 prefixes to prime the cache.
[07:20] Maya Chen: Any other blockers?
[07:22] Aisha Khan: Not from product side. Just need cost numbers and runbook.
[07:25] J. Lee: Security asks for the ephemeral API key and an access policy doc.
[07:29] Maya Chen: We'll provide the key with scope limited to the staging cluster and expiration 48 hours.
[07:34] Tom Alvarez: I'll share the S3 path after this call.
[07:37] Maya Chen: Perfect. Ok we'll recap at the end.
[07:40] [wrap-up]
[07:42] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to share Dedicated sizing spreadsheet and cost delta, deliver burst runbook + priming scripts, provision ephemeral staging key, run 30-minute burst rehearsal Friday 11:00 PT. LumenPay to provide S3 replay path and confirm attendance.
[07:58] Tom Alvarez: Sounds good.
[08:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and next steps.

End of transcript.
Run 30-minute burst test on staging with 2x concurrent clients (LumenPay to coordinate)
Redwood to send updated Dedicated sizing spreadsheet and cost delta by 2026-02-20
Schedule canary rollout window and rollback playbook for 2026-02-24
Maya: share burst simulation spreadsheet and knobbed autoscale policy examples - due 2026-02-20
Carlos: prepare step-by-step burst runbook + curl examples for KV cache priming - due 2026-02-21
Tom: validate traffic replay tooling access and provide S3 path for logs - due 2026-02-19

PineGate POC weekly - retention, SSO & SOC2 checkpoint

Weekly POC sync focusing on security/compliance items: SSO integration progress, audit log ingestion and retention configuration, SOC2 evidence collection, and a short review of early inference results. Agree to run a short log export test and share SOC2 scoping doc by next Tue.
SSO (SAML/SCIM) integration status
Audit logs & retention policy configuration
SOC2 evidence & responsibilities
Data encryption/KMS and RBAC
Initial inference latency/cost observations
[00:00] Jamie Ortega: Okay, thanks everyone for joining, well give it a minute for folks to pop in. uh quick intro from our side, Jamie here AE, Samir is our SE, Rina is on CSM.
[00:18] Lena Morris: Hey Jamie, thanks. Were running a little late but ready to go, here's Lena.
[00:22] Chris Yu: Chris, SRE, morning.
[00:25] Jamie Ortega: Great. Agenda for today: SSO status, audit logs and retention question, SOC2 evidence handoff, and a quick results snapshot. Any additions?
[00:35] Dana Park: No additions, maybe touch on perf cost briefly.
[00:38] Jamie Ortega: Yep, we will. Samir, do you want to kick off SSO?
[00:42] Samir Patel: Sure. So status: we completed the SAML metadata exchange last week, PineGate side configured the IdP and we pushed the SP metadata into your tenant. We did see one mismatch on NameID format, which was causing failed assertions, thats fixed now. SCIM provisioning - we still need a couple attributes mapped for groups.
[01:05] Lena Morris: That aligns with what we saw. Our SCIM schema is customized for department codes, so we need a mapping example.
[01:12] Samir Patel: Got it. Ill send a mapping sample; can do a mapping that adds a department claim in SCIM 2.0. Also to confirm: are you planning to use SSO for admin users only initially or for all users in the pilot?
[01:26] Dana Park: Admins only for the pilot, we want to keep control of who can spin up models.
[01:30] Jamie Ortega: Makes sense. From Redwood's side we'll treat that as RBAC with admin role bound to SAML group. We can also support SCIM-group to RBAC sync.
[01:40] Lena Morris: Okay next on audit logs. We received the sample endpoint you set up last week but the format didn't include request payloads, only top-level event types. We need full request/response pairs for traceability.
[01:53] Samir Patel: Right, current runtime emits structured events but payload masking is on by default. We can toggle debug-level logging for a short window to capture request bodies, but we want to make sure customer consents because that captures sensitive content.
[02:09] Chris Yu: We can do an ephemeral window. We'll set up a buffer rule and only run it for two hours, but we need the export format to be JSONL and include timestamps in ISO with nanoseconds if possible.
[02:21] Samir Patel: JSONL is fine. The runtime stores audit events in our managed audit pipeline for hosted customers, but for the PineGate pilot we suggested a forward to your AWS Kinesis Firehose. That still works?
[02:33] Chris Yu: Yes Kinesis is fine. We'll provide a temporary stream and credentials.
[02:38] Jamie Ortega: Important note: for Private deployments we can ship audit logs directly to a customer-controlled S3, if you switch to Private later you get more direct custody.
[02:48] Lena Morris: We're evaluating that, but for pilot Kinesis -> S3 is our preference. Next, retention. What are the default retention windows for hosted audit logs and for inference artifacts?
[03:00] Samir Patel: Default for hosted audit logs is 90 days. Inference artifacts (prompt/response KV cache fragments) are retained for 14 days by default with options to shorten. We can configure for longer if you need. For SOC2 you might need 1 year of certain records, so we can configure long-term export to Glacier as well.
[03:20] Lena Morris: For our compliance team, we need 12 months for auth events and 24 months for admin change history. Is that feasible?
[03:29] Samir Patel: Yes, we can configure tiered retention: keep auth events 12 months, admin change history 24 months, export to your S3 bucket then lifecycle to Glacier. We'll need to document the retention policy in the SOC2 mapping.
[03:41] Marco Silva: Quick procurement question - does extended retention impact pricing materially?
[03:45] Jamie Ortega: There is a storage cost; we can provide a conservative estimate. In general the incremental cost is small relative to per-token inference costs, but long-term cold storage has a minimal monthly fee. I will include an estimate in the pricing note.
[03:58] Dana Park: Great. SOC2 - Lena, do you have a list of specific evidence items you still need from us?
[04:03] Lena Morris: We have a checklist but we need clarity on where to find change logs for model deployments, tenant-level access logs, and any key rotation logs for KMS usage.
[04:12] Samir Patel: For model deployment change logs, those are recorded in our control plane audit stream and forwarded to the same audit pipeline. Tenant-level access logs are part of the auth events. KMS key rotation is logged in both Redwood's operational logs and in the KMS audit trail; for hosted customers we can surface a consolidated export.
[04:28] Jamie Ortega: I'll attach a mapping doc that shows which log type corresponds to which SOC2 control. That should make it easier for you to pull evidence.
[04:35] Lena Morris: Perfect. A couple of nitty gritty items: encryption in transit and at rest - we need confirmation that customer data is encrypted with customer-managed keys for Private, and for hosted that BYOK via KMS is supported.
[04:48] Samir Patel: Yes, hosted supports Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) via AWS KMS for customers who want it. For Private deployments you can run with your HSM/KMS. In both cases we rotate keys per your policy; rotation events are part of the audit stream.
[05:03] Chris Yu: On RBAC - can we get more granular roles beyond admin/read-only, like model-deploy-only or cost-view-only?
[05:09] Samir Patel: Yes, we have a role matrix. We can create custom roles that map to specific console and API permissions. I'll share the role matrix with examples.
[05:18] Jamie Ortega: Switching gears to a brief results review — Samir do you want to summarize the early inference metrics?
[05:23] Samir Patel: Sure. Over the last 48 hours the pilot ran about 8k requests, median latency 140ms for short prompts (~128 tokens predicted), p95 420ms. Cost per 1k tokens is trending lower than our initial hosted estimate because caching hit rate is about 28% for repeated prefixes.
[05:43] Dana Park: That latency is good, were mostly concerned about p95 spikes during batch windows.
[05:48] Samir Patel: Right the p95 spikes correlated with a nightly batch job that saturated the worker pool; we recommend an autoscale policy tweak to reserve capacity for interactive traffic. We can also set a routing policy so interactive goes to dedicated low-latency nodes.
[06:03] Chris Yu: Is that an additional charge to reserve capacity?
[06:06] Jamie Ortega: If you want guaranteed reserved capacity it's part of Dedicated offering, but we can set soft reservations with minimal cost impact for the pilot. We'll capture the options in the note.
[06:16] Lena Morris: Back to SSO test: Marco, do you have availability to run the provisioning test this week?
[06:22] Marco Silva: I can carve out time Friday morning, but need clear steps for the mapping and creds.
[06:27] Samir Patel: I'll email a step-by-step SCIM mapping doc and a checklist for Friday. Also include a small Python script for provisioning so you can run it locally.
[06:36] Lena Morris: Good. One more security ask: we need to validate that audit logs cannot be altered after ingestion. Can you describe immutability guarantees?
[06:45] Samir Patel: For hosted audit streams we maintain a write-once pipeline with SHA256 signatures appended and object versioning enabled on S3; you can also enable WORM policies on your bucket. For Private, you control the storage, so immutability is enforced by your S3/WORM/HSM settings.
[07:03] Chris Yu: Will those signatures include the full payload hash?
[07:07] Samir Patel: Yes, full payload hash; we keep a separate integrity index that you can query. That index can be included in the exported evidence.
[07:16] Dana Park: Any blockers on our side for SOC2 timeline? Were aiming for readiness review in late April.
[07:22] Lena Morris: We need the mapping doc and evidence locations this week, plus a successful SSO and log export test to close a few controls.
[07:31] Jamie Ortega: We'll prioritize the mapping doc. Rina will coordinate follow-ups and the SOC2 packet. Rina?
[07:35] Rina Cho: Yep Ill own the packet and will schedule a short working session next Tue to walk through the mapping with Lena and Chris.
[07:44] Marco Silva: Procurement question: once we confirm security and retention, whats the next contractual step?
[07:49] Jamie Ortega: Typically we move to a pilot amendment that captures retention SLAs and any privacy addendum; I'll draft and share a redline.
[07:57] Chris Yu: Quick note on audit log export test — we'll need a sample of redwoods JSONL schema to validate our parsers.
[08:03] Samir Patel: I'll attach the JSONL schema and an example file to the follow-up email.
[08:08] Dana Park: For the perf snapshot, can we see the dedicated worker config your SE suggested? We want to understand CPU/GPU allocation.
[08:15] Samir Patel: Yes, the config is small: worker type g4dn.xlarge for pilot, 16 concurrent processes, batch size guidance 8-16 depending on latency SLO. I'll put the exact YAML in the doc.
[08:29] [crosstalk] Lena Morris: sorry, go ahead.
[08:31] Samir Patel: Also note quantization profile used for the model is int8 with a small quality delta; we can run quality regression tests if you want.
[08:40] Dana Park: Please run that and show us delta on responses for our test prompts.
[08:45] Samir Patel: Will do.
[08:47] Jamie Ortega: Any regulatory residency questions?
[08:49] Lena Morris: For now EU residency for customer EU tenants — we need logs and data to stay in eu-west-1.
[08:55] Samir Patel: We can route regionally; for hosted we'll ensure data plane for EU tenants stays in eu-west-1, control plane remains global but with minimal PII. We'll document that architecture.
[09:09] Marco Silva: On pricing again - can you give a rough delta between enabling BYOK and standard managed keys?
[09:15] Jamie Ortega: BYOK has a minor setup fee and some additional monthly KMS charges, mostly driven by encryption API calls. I'll include a line-item estimate.
[09:26] Lena Morris: Okay lets recap next steps and owners.
[09:29] Jamie Ortega: Recap: Samir attach JSONL schema and provisioning script; Jamie send SOC2 mapping and pricing note; Rina schedule working session next Tue; Chris run audit log export test and share endpoint; Marco confirm availability Friday for SCIM run. Everyone in agreement?
[09:50] Chris Yu: Agree.
[09:51] Lena Morris: Agree.
[09:53] Dana Park: Agree.
[09:54] Jamie Ortega: Great, we'll follow up in email. Thanks all.
[09:58] [meeting end]
Redwood to send SOC2 scoping checklist and map of where evidence lives - due 2026-03-10
Customer to run audit log export test and confirm format - due 2026-03-09
Schedule dedicated SSO test window with PineGate SSO admin - propose 2026-03-11
SE to provide small perf snapshot from dedicated worker config - due 2026-03-08

Parkside Studios — API adoption pathway & credits discussion

Meeting header: 2025-06-05 16:00 PDT | Duration ~48m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Parkside Head of ML), Jamie (Eng Mgr), Daniel (Security), Samira (Product)

Summary (auto): Parkside evaluating Redwood for embedding/search and chat assistants; wants quick path to first token with hosted API but is also evaluating commit/dedicated options for predictable throughput and data controls. Main concerns: costs at scale, latency for interactive studio tooling, and compliance for client media. Agreed next steps: pricing + credits, quickstart links, set up a technical bench test.

00:00 - Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
00:08 - Alex (Parkside): Hey, Alex here, head of ML.
00:11 - Jamie (Parkside): Jamie, engineering manager.
00:14 - Daniel (Parkside): Daniel, security.
00:17 - Samira (Parkside): Samira, product.
00:19 - Luca (Redwood SE): Luca here, I’ll go deep on perf and integration.
00:22 - Priya (Redwood SE): Priya, SI/quickstart assist.
00:25 - Maya: Perfect. Goal for today is to understand your stack, constraints, and get you to a fast path to first token with Redwood Hosted or a plan for Dedicated/Private if needed.

02:03 - Alex: High level — we build creative-assist tools for video editors, a lot of metadata extraction, embeddings for search across assets, and a chat experience for studio producers. We tried a few things with OpenAI for prototypes but cost and latency when we scale to thousands of users is the worry.
02:25 - Jamie: Also, we have internal policy about client media not leaving certain regions; some clients require contracts about data retention. So the model hosting options matter.
02:40 - Daniel: And SOC 2, audit logs, SSO are table stakes for RFPs. We need to know what you support.

04:05 - Maya: Totally — makes sense. Quick Qs about current infra: do you host most stuff on GCP or on-prem?
04:12 - Alex: GCP primarily, some on-prem for larger customers.
04:18 - Maya: Good. For a quickstart path we usually recommend Redwood Hosted API for time-to-first-token — we give free credits to explore, there are sample repos and SDKs. If you hit steady traffic/predictable spend or need VPC controls, we move to Dedicated or Private.

05:00 - Jamie: What does the typical timeline look like to go from quickstart to a POC for production traffic?
05:07 - Luca: Usually teams can get first token in under an hour using the SDK and sample prompt kit. A POC for qps/latency takes 1–3 weeks depending on dataset and bench objectives. For Dedicated provisioning, lead times can be a few weeks depending on GPU availability and config — we’ll scope that if you need isolated capacity.

07:30 - Samira: Free credits — how much are we talking? Enough to simulate a few days of normal load?
07:38 - Maya: We allocate trial credits depending on the profile — for a PLG self-serve trail often $500–2,000 equivalent. For enterprise evaluation we can top that up for specific bench runs — that's usually coordinated after the initial discovery.

09:45 - Daniel: Security stuff — SSO/SAML? KMS? Audit logs? We need to know encryption at rest and key management.
09:56 - Priya: We support SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC scopes in the Console, and integration with customer KMS options for Private deployments. Hosted has managed keys but we also offer Bring-Your-Own-Key for Dedicated/Private. Audit logs and token-level tracing are in the Console; we can share SOC 2 docs.
10:28 - Daniel: Good. Send those docs.

12:15 - Alex: Latency — our interactive tool requires ~200ms median response for short prompts, and embeddings queries need low single-digit ms for small vector lookups. Is Redwood able to hit that on Hosted?
12:30 - Luca: For short prompt generation, Hosted with a low-latency profile and continuous batching can hit 150–250ms medians for 1–2k token models in many regions; higher volume shifts you to dedicated pools. Embeddings lookups are usually dominated by your vector DB; our embeddings call latency is often sub-50ms. We should bench with your exact payloads.

14:02 - Jamie: How do autoscaling and burst capacity work if we go Dedicated? We don't want throttling during big render spikes.
14:10 - Maya: Dedicated has autoscaling and optional burst capacity. You set throughput targets and we can configure a small hosted fallback policy to prevent outages — fallback to Hosted or to a lower-cost model variant. That reduces risk during spikes.

16:05 - Alex: Cost modeling — can you share examples for 10k monthly users with average 20 calls per month? We need a rough per-user cost envelope.
16:18 - Maya: We'll send a model, but quick rule: embeddings and short generations are the big drivers. We'll include device-level token costs and show how batching and KV caching reduce per-token costs.

18:30 - Samira: For the quickstart, what's the smoothest path? Repo, SDK, or Postman?
18:36 - Priya: SDK plus a starters repo. We have a dockerized example to demo streaming and embeddings; that repo contains a sample dataset ingestion pipeline and a notebook. Luca will share a link.

20:10 - Luca: (shares link) https://redwood.example/starter-repo — contains code to get first token within 10 minutes if you use the env sample and API key. Note: the link above is representative in this transcript, actual link to be emailed.

22:00 - Alex: Any gotchas with our current infra (GCP + private storage)?
22:08 - Luca: If you keep assets on GCP, you can either call Hosted API directly or use Private deployment to keep inference in your VPC. For Hosted, we recommend using signed URLs and not uploading full media to Redwood. For embeddings we recommend pre-processing and passing metadata pointers.

24:45 - Daniel: Data residency — some clients mandate EU-only processing. Is region pinning available?
24:53 - Priya: Yes, we can pin model serving to specific regions for both Hosted and Dedicated. For strict residency we usually recommend Private within a customer VPC.

26:30 - Jamie: From a dev experience standpoint, any rate limits or token limits we should watch?
26:37 - Luca: There are rate limits for free tiers; for enterprise we set quotas per account. Token limits depend on the model variant; the Console exposes token-level metrics so you can tune batching.

28:55 - Alex: We have a media-heavy workload with big context windows — do you support KV caching and chunked attention?
29:02 - Luca: Our runtime supports KV cache reuse for chat flows and sequence length optimizations; for very long contexts we recommend embeddings+retrieval or chunking with summaries to keep latency predictable. We'll propose a configuration in the POC.

31:10 - Samira: On billing, do you do usage-based for Hosted and reserved pricing for Dedicated? Any blended options?
31:18 - Maya: Exactly — hosted is pay-per-use; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits. We offer blended/volume discounts and we can model blended scenarios in the pricing sheet.

33:05 - Daniel: Compliance checklist — can you email SOC 2, ISO certs, and an outline of audit-log retention?
33:13 - Maya: Yes, will attach full security pack.

35:00 - Jamie: If we want to test quickly, what permissions do you need? A service account?
35:06 - Luca: For quickstart to Hosted just create an API key via the Console and we can supply sample envs. For Dedicated or Private benching we'll need an infra contact for VPC peering details or a service account to push images (if on-prem).

37:20 - Alex: What are failure modes — e.g. network throttles, regional outages?
37:27 - Priya: We advise multi-region routing and automatic fallback policies. For Dedicated we can provision standby capacity; for Hosted we have regional fallbacks and model variant fallbacks to reduce user-visible errors.

39:00 - Samira: Can Redwood run model evals against our prompt set to detect regressions?
39:07 - Luca: Yes, Redwood Optimize has eval hooks — you can attach prompt sets and get quality/regression alerts and tie them to rollouts. We'll demo that in the POC if desired.

41:30 - Maya: Quick recap — we’ll: 1) send pricing + trial credits ranges; 2) Luca sends starter repo + quickstart steps; 3) Parkside to provide representative dataset/latency SLOs; 4) schedule bench test week of 6/16.
41:50 - Alex: Sounds good. On credits — could we get a bump for the bench run to simulate 24-hour traffic?
41:59 - Maya: Yes, we can allocate additional credits for specific bench tests once scope is agreed.

44:00 - Daniel: Last Q — do you have an architecture diagram for a Dedicated with hosted fallback?
44:08 - Priya: Yes, we have a reference architecture. I’ll include that in the pack.

46:20 - Jamie: Anything else we should know before we wrap?
46:25 - Maya: Nothing major — we'll follow up with the material and propose concrete POC goals (latency targets, qps, cost envelope).

47:00 - Alex: Thanks all.
47:05 - Maya: Thanks everyone, we’ll follow up by tomorrow with the docs and pricing.
47:12 - (meeting ends)

References (to be attached via email): Redwood quickstart repo link, security pack (SOC 2), pricing spreadsheet template, starters notebook for embeddings and streaming.

Notes about transcript: occasional recognition errors present — e.g., some proper nouns and acronyms may be mis-transcribed. This is an auto transcription exported from Fireflies.ai.
