document.content:
Weekly POC sync — Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) networking & upgrade review

Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-05
Start time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Carlos Rivera (Aegis DevOps), Priya Nair (Aegis Platform Eng), Tom Holden (Aegis Security), Mei Zhang (Aegis ML Infra), Justin (Aegis SRE)

Summary (auto): weekly POC checkpoint for Redwood Private on VPC-connected on-prem pilot. Reviewed this week's benchmark results after kernel/quantization tweaks, discussed a recurring routing flap causing 503s, confirmed required network changes (peering and NAT), agreed on a low-risk kernel rollout window, and captured next steps.

[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, thanks everyone for joining. I see most folks are here, we'll aim for about 45 minutes. Quick roll call - Maya (Redwood), Samir (SE), Lena (CSM) - and on the Aegis side?
[00:12] Carlos Rivera: Carlos here, Priya, Tom, Mei and Justin on this call as well.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Perfect. Quick agenda: 1) results from the last tweak (kernel + quantization change), 2) the intermittent routing issue Justin flagged, 3) network changes needed for peering and NAT, and 4) next steps. Samir, you want to start with perf notes?
[00:31] Samir Patel: Yeah sure. So we rolled the 2.1 kernel optimization on Tuesday night to the pilot cluster — this included a slightly different attention kernel and an updated fp16 fallback path for one of the layers. We also adjusted the quantization profile for the 8-bit int path, mainly to avoid a small accuracy drift we saw in the first run.
[00:52] Mei Zhang: Quick q — did you keep the KV cache change we talked about or revert? The KV cache clipping had looked promising for prefix heavy workloads.
[01:03] Samir Patel: We left the KV cache change in but lowered the aggressive expiry threshold. That preserved most hit rate while preventing cache thrash in short-lived sessions.
[01:15] Priya Nair: From our side we ran the nightly load run — 10k synthetic requests with our typical prompt mix. Overall p50 dropped by about 12%, p95 by 18%, p99 about 9% — CPU on the control plane agent was lower too. But we still saw a spike of 503s around 03:00 UTC.
[01:39] Justin (SRE): Yep that spike is what I'm worried about. It looks like a routing flap between the customer VPC and the on-prem NAT gateway — not sure if it's a BGP withdraw or a transient MTU issue. The SRE logs show timeouts at the egress for ~30 seconds.
[01:56] Tom Holden: Security side — that 503 window also correlates with failed audit log uploads to our SIEM. If logs are missing we can't prove compliance for that window. We need a mitigation that keeps logs buffered locally until connectivity is back.
[02:10] Lena Ortiz: Good call — buffering is doable, Samir can you speak to local buffering in the agent?
[02:18] Samir Patel: The private control plane agent can spool logs to disk and retry with exponential backoff; that's already in the agent but the default spool size is small. We can bump spool to 1GB for the pilot cluster; need an OK on disk usage from Aegis.
[02:32] Carlos Rivera: We can allocate extra disk on the pilot nodes, 1GB is fine. But the bigger concern is the root cause for the network flap. Justin says it could be BGP-related — are we peering through a transit gateway?
[02:47] Justin (SRE): We're peering via the cloud transit gateway and then an on-prem BGP session to our edge. The timing shows the transit gateway replaced a route on a health check failure; that coincided with a connection drain on the Redwood agent.
[03:02] Maya Chen: Okay, two actionable threads: 1) make logs resilient, bump spool, 2) root cause network flap. Samir, you mentioned kernel rollout — what's the expected downtime and risk?
[03:14] Samir Patel: The kernel patch is rolling as a rolling restart with no required model reload in theory, but in practice each worker restarts and reconnects to the gRPC frontends. We recommend a 15–30 minute maintenance window to observe drains and fallbacks; there might be a small p95 blip during the window. We have a canary group in the cluster so we can stage it to 10% first.
[03:37] Priya Nair: We need to coordinate with our change window — next Thursday night is preferred for us 02:00–03:00 local. Is that compatible with your canary plan?
[03:46] Samir Patel: That works. We'll do 10% canary for 20 minutes, monitor errors and latency, then ramp. If errors exceed threshold we'll auto rollback.
[03:56] Mei Zhang: On the accuracy side, did the quantization change trigger any regression? Our eval suite flagged a 0.6% drop in one of the sensitive prompt categories.
[04:08] Samir Patel: Good catch. The 0.6% was within expectations but we can push a tweak: slightly increase per-channel scale for that layer to reduce the bias. That will cost ~2% more perf at the microkernel level but should restore accuracy.
[04:26] Carlos Rivera: We'd prefer accuracy >99.5% on the eval set for that category. If the tweak does it, go ahead; just document the expected perf delta.
[04:35] Samir Patel: Will do.
[04:38] [05:00] (background) Unknown Speaker: um hmm
[05:02] Justin (SRE): Returning to routing, one pattern — when our primary transit health-check fails it fails a handful of connections and the transit gateway switches to backup path that passes through a different edge with an MTU 1400 vs our usual 1500. That causes path MTU discovery issues and fragmentation leading to gRPC stalls.
[05:25] Maya Chen: Interesting, so it may be an MTU drop causing gRPC stalls which surface as 503?
[05:31] Samir Patel: gRPC is sensitive to path MTU, yeah. If packets are fragmented and the agent doesn't handle sticky sessions at the application layer, the connection can reset. A quick mitigation is to enable MSS clamping or ensure tunnel path MTU is consistent.
[05:44] Priya Nair: We can set MSS clamp on the edge devices but that requires a config change and a short window. Justin, can you coordinate with network ops?
[05:52] Justin (SRE): Yep I'll open a ticket right after this call. Also recommend Redwood add a client-side keepalive and slightly longer gRPC retry before surfacing 503 to the app.
[06:03] Samir Patel: We can bump the keepalive interval and retries in the agent; that'll reduce transient 503s from short flaps. We'll push a config that doesn't need a full agent restart.
[06:12] Tom Holden: From compliance, we still need to ensure audit logs are marked as 'delayed' with a clear chain of custody when buffering happens. Will Redwood provide log checksums on upload?
[06:24] Samir Patel: Yes, logs are hashed and we support upload with a manifest that includes SHA256. When we spool and then push we include the manifest so you can verify integrity.
[06:35] Mei Zhang: On perf numbers, can you show the raw latency histograms again? The dashboard snapshot we looked at showed mean 80ms down to 70ms but p99 is still kinda noisy.
[06:48] Maya Chen: Lena, can you drop that dashboard link in the notes?
[06:52] Lena Ortiz: Sure — sending now in the chat — "link: pilot-cluster-dashboard/aegis-0305"
[07:00] [07:15] Maya Chen: Great. Let's pivot to routing fixes and peering planning — Carlos, you mentioned CIDR overlaps earlier?
[07:22] Carlos Rivera: Right, our staging VPC uses 10.0.0.0/16 and our pilot VPC is 10.1.0.0/16, transit is 10.255.0.0/16 but the on-prem uses 10.0.0.0/14 for historical reasons. That overlap could cause unexpected route preference during failover. We need to confirm no overlapping prefixes are installed to the transit.
[07:45] Mei Zhang: That could explain why the transit sometimes picks a path that routes internal traffic back to the wrong edge.
[07:52] Priya Nair: We can carve out a dedicated /20 for the Redwood peering to avoid overlap. It's low touch but requires change control.
[07:59] Maya Chen: Redwood requires that the peering prefix not overlap with any customer internal prefixes; if you can confirm a /20 that is unused we can provision the VPC peering and NAT rules. Also note we need route propagation disabled for that peering to avoid accidental export.
[08:18] Carlos Rivera: I'll check and propose a /20 by Monday.
[08:21] Justin (SRE): Also check egress NAT gateway limits — during the benchmark we spiked and the NAT threw connection limits causing some resets. We might need multiple NAT gateways or a higher throughput tier.
[08:34] Maya Chen: Good call. For pilot, dual NAT or a single HA NAT is recommended. We'll document the recommended network topology in the follow-up.
[08:41] [09:00] (typing) Lena Ortiz: dropping network topo doc link: "docs/aegis-network-topo-v1"
[09:08] Priya Nair: On encryption and KMS — Tom — any new asks?
[09:12] Tom Holden: We want to ensure CMKs are customer-managed for Private. If keys are rotated we need a pre-signed key rotation plan and notice. Also need proof of HSM-backed keys if possible for later compliance.
[09:25] Samir Patel: Redwood private supports BYOK via KMS and can integrate with HSM-backed providers. We'll attach the KM integration guide in the follow-up.
[09:34] Tom Holden: Also need proof of SOC2 controls around key access, can you share that doc?
[09:39] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send the SOC2 control mapping for Private deployments. Lena will attach in the follow-up.
[09:46] Mei Zhang: Another smaller item — model pinning behavior during canary rollouts. If we can pin a model SHA to canary nodes it would help reproducibility. Are rollouts model-aware?
[09:58] Samir Patel: Yes, rollouts can be model-version-aware. We do canary groups by node label and model-version pinning. We'll provide the rollout recipe we plan to use for the 2.1 kernel canary.
[10:10] Maya Chen: Good. Let's capture the agreed maintenance window: Thursday 02:00–03:00 local for Aegis, Redwood to start 10% canary at 02:05, monitor 20 minutes then ramp. If errors >1% we roll back. Samir, confirm?
[10:24] Samir Patel: Confirmed. We'll provide a runbook and the rollback metric thresholds.
[10:29] [10:45] Justin (SRE): On the quick term routing mitigation, I'll set MSS clamp on the edge and increase health-check timeout to reduce false failovers. That should reduce flaps.
[10:57] Carlos Rivera: We'll also provision the extra disk for spool and validate that agents pick up new spool size without restart.
[11:07] Mei Zhang: After the kernel roll, can we run a focused bench for our heavy-prefix prompts and then reconvene? I want a p95/p99 comparison within 48 hours of the rollout.
[11:18] Lena Ortiz: I'll schedule a benchmark run and a follow-up 48-hour sync.
[11:23] Maya Chen: Awesome. Any other blockers?
[11:26] Priya Nair: One ask — can Redwood provide a short note on the expected perf delta if we revert the KV cache expiry tweak? We want to know risk surface if we need to rollback fast.
[11:37] Samir Patel: I'll include a revert impact note in the runbook — expected p50 up by ~8% if we revert, and p95 may go back to previous levels.
[11:47] [12:00] (short crosstalk; someone says thanks)
[12:03] Maya Chen: All right, quick recap — Samir will share kernel changelog/runbook + revert impact + log spool config by 2025-03-06; Carlos will confirm /20 for peering and NAT capacity by 2025-03-10; Mei will provide payloads and latency targets by 2025-03-09; Lena will schedule the benchmark and send SOC2/key docs. Redwood and Aegis agree on timeline and Thursday night canary.
[12:25] Maya Chen: Any objections?
[12:28] Tom Holden: No objections. Just need the audit log manifest and SOC2 mapping.
[12:33] Maya Chen: We'll include those. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and in the shared docs.
[12:40] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional misattributions and background speech; some technical acronyms mistranscribed (e.g., MSS clamping written as "M S S clamp" in original auto text).

Referenced links (sent in chat):
- pilot-cluster-dashboard/aegis-0305
- docs/aegis-network-topo-v1
- KM-integration-guide (to be attached)
- runbook-template/redwood-kernel-rollout-v1

Year-end governance and priorities - All Hands

Executive update covering end-of-year priorities, a light hiring pause window, governance tweaks for deployments in regulated regions, incident-readiness playbook launch, and people/compensation Q&A. Action items assigned for org leads to follow up with teams; next steps include publishing a short governance FAQ and scheduling follow-ups for benefits and SRE runbooks.
Priya: Draft governance FAQ + deployment checklist; due 2026-12-13
Lena: Publish incident playbook and set tabletop exercise; due 2026-12-17
Samira: Post compensation Q&A doc and run two office hours; due 2026-12-10
Ethan + Priya: Consolidate headcount asks into single doc; due 2026-12-20
Avery: Send short note to customers about year-end support windows; due 2026-12-08
Publish short governance FAQ and new deployment checklist (Priya) - target 2026-12-13
Share incident playbook and schedule 90-min SRE tabletop (Lena) - target 2026-12-17
People team to share compensation timeline and Q&A doc (Samira) - target 2026-12-10
Product/Eng to finalize Q1 scope and headcount requests for exec review (Priya + Ethan) - target 2026-12-20
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-06
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Avery, Marcus, Priya, Ethan, Samira, Lena + companywide dial-in

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, quick housekeeping - we'll record, we'll post slides after, and we, uh, want to keep this tight. Year-end all-hands, call it Steadfast Compass.

[00:18] Marcus: Morning/afternoon folks. Real quick agenda -- governance, incidents/readiness, budget/hiring guidance, people updates, then Q&A.

[00:30] Priya: I'll be brief on product priorities, the main ask is alignment so the execs can consolidate Q1 asks. We are focusing on dedicated/private parity and shipping the Optimize improvements that reduce per-token cost.

[00:48] Avery: High level: great year — product shipped, customers expanded — but macro's shifted. We'll be careful on spend and prioritize projects that impact customer SLOs and unit economics. That means a temporary tightening window that is not a full freeze but a review-first posture.

[01:05] Samira: To be transparent: we're implementing a short hiring pause for non-critical roles for the next three weeks to let leadership finalize priorities. This is not a layoff announcement. We'll run reviews with hiring managers; exceptions possible for customer-critical hires.

[01:28] Speaker 7: questions about ramp timing?

[01:33] Ethan: We'll prioritize infrastructure and reliability roles. Eng leads, please flag exceptions into the hiring board. Priya and I will meet with each hiring manager this week.

[01:50] Lena: On reliability — recent trends showed a slight uptick in tail latency during holidays in our EU region, seen in the dashboard. We're rolling a new routing policy that favors capacity regionalization and early fallback to smaller quantized variants. There's a short window to validate before Q1.

[02:12] Marcus: Quick tech note — kernel/compilation improvements the runtime team landed cut median token latency by ~6% on long-context jobs. But the tail still matters; Lena's plan will address outliers.

[02:30] Priya: Governance update: for customers with regulated-data needs, we are tightening the private deployment checklist and adding an explicit KMS/HSM proof path. That means new required docs for on-prem handoffs and an audit-readiness checklist. This will slow some private deployments by a week or two but it's necessary for SOC/ISO asks.

[02:55] Avery: The ask to teams: document any customer engagements that might be affected and let sales and solutions know. We'll be proactive rather than reactive.

[03:10] Samira: People update — compensation cycle: we are planning a limited refresh targeted at performance-critical bands; full company-wide adjustments will follow a compensation review in January. We'll publish the timeline and FAQs.

[03:30] Audience noise / brief crosstalk.

[03:45] Audience Q: Will the hiring pause affect internship offers?

[03:50] Samira: Interns in pipeline are considered mission-critical for recruiting; we will not cancel offers that are already extended, but new intern requisitions will be reviewed.

[04:05] Priya: Product roadmap highlights: 1) Redwood Optimize v2 trials for top ten customers, 2) streaming improvements to reduce token overhead, 3) rollout of per-route dashboards in Console. We're delaying some lower-impact UX initiatives.

[04:35] Ethan: Engineering priorities: secure the EU/regional fallback play, finalize autoscaling burst policies for Dedicated, and stabilize the new batching layer. We'll freeze feature merges for low-priority branches for two weeks to shake down reliability patches.

[05:00] Marcus: There was a question earlier about competitors; nothing super new, but we're watching inference runtime projects from others. Our differentiator remains unified ops and quantization profiles tuned for customers.

[05:20] Avery: Financial note: operating runway remains healthy, but we choose to optimize spend. We will push non-customer-facing capital projects to Q2 unless they materially improve unit economics.

[05:40] Audience chat: applause, emoji reactions.

[06:00] Lena: Incident readiness — we are launching an incident playbook (draft linked in #sre) and a tabletop exercise next week. The playbook includes cross-region fallback, manifest lists for canaries, and a clear escalation ladder. We need all product and infra leads to attend the tabletop.

[06:25] Priya: Note on governance artifacts: new deployment checklist will include encryption at rest verification, network diagrams, and a signed data flow doc. Solutions will get a checklist template.

[06:45] Avery: On customers, we will send a short note to customers summarizing year-end support windows and our maintenance freeze timings. Action for me to send that early next week.

[07:02] Marcus: Small technical aside about model routing: we will enable an automatic fallback to a quantized variant (lower-cost) when longer queues detected; teams should validate quality regressions against their eval sets. Redwood Optimize will suggest thresholds.

[07:25] Audience Q: Any change to hosted pricing?

[07:28] Avery: No immediate change. We'll keep pricing stable and focus on cost reduction for customers through Optimize and batching.

[07:40] Samira: Benefits note — open enrollment reminders: check benefit portal; HR will host two Q&A sessions next Tuesday and Thursday.

[07:58] Priya: On the roadmap we are also prioritizing regulatory-region readiness — that impacts the Private product but also Dedicated (we need to prove data locality controls). Expect a governance FAQ.

[08:25] Audience: question about holiday on-call shifts.

[08:30] Lena: On-call rotations will be tightened; SRE will publish a compact schedule. We'll try to minimize disruption. Expect compensatory time options for holiday shifts.

[08:48] Ethan: Quick ops ask — teams owning long-lived feature branches please rebase; we'll do a batch merge window next week so we can ship critical reliability fixes.

[09:05] Audience: chatter about merge conflicts.

[09:20] Avery: OK open Q&A. Please raise your hand in the Q&A panel; I'll try to answer as many as possible before we run out of time.

[09:35] Staff question (Speaker 11): Are there layoffs planned?

[09:38] Avery: No. This is a real quick pause to get alignment. We are not planning layoffs. If anything changes we'll tell you early.

[09:55] Staff question (Speaker 12): Will the governance changes increase time-to-delivery for Private installs?

[09:59] Priya: Slightly, yes. We added a mandatory KMS proof and an audit checklist. For customers in heavy-regulated industries it's a net positive. Solutions and sales will manage expectations.

[10:20] Staff: question about Q1 priorities.

[10:24] Priya: Q1 is about parity (hosted -> dedicated -> private), Optimize cost improvements, and reliability. We'll publish the Q1 scope doc by Dec 20.

[10:41] Marcus: Another technical note: please check the runtime release notes; we are enabling a beta for 2-stage batching that can cut cost for small prompts.

[10:58] Avery: Final ask — leads: run your 15-min team huddles tomorrow to surface any downstream impacts, then update the priority board. We'll reconvene execs Friday to finalize headcount asks.

[11:15] Samira: Reminding managers to schedule one-on-ones for anyone anxious about changes; HR open office hours and anonymous ask form in the #people channel.

[11:35] Audience: brief applause.

[11:50] Avery: Thanks everyone, we'll post slides, the governance FAQ, and timing for tabletop. Happy holidays in advance.

[12:00] Meeting end.

Notes / Links referenced: governance checklist draft (link in #prod-governance), incident playbook draft (link in #sre), compensation timeline (HR doc), Q1 scope template (link in #roadmap). Some transcription artifacts: speaker labels may be approximate and short timestamps every few minutes.

Chat parameterization and failover demo - live playthrough

AE/SE walkthrough of Redwood hosted chat API focused on live streaming behavior, parameter tuning, and failover patterns. Team demoed console traces and Optimize suggestions for batching/prefix caching. Customer asked about security (SOC2, KMS) and idempotency/resume semantics; next steps include sandbox access and sample benchmark run.
Header:
Date: 2025-01-31
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Northridge PM), Maya Li (BE), Devon O'Neill (Security)

Auto-generated Summary (may be noisy):
- Live demo of chat streaming and parameter settings; show fallback model routing; go over retry/backoff; assign pilot steps.

Transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm alex, i'll run quick agenda — intro, live sandbox demo, then samir will deep dive on retries and idempotency, and we'll leave time for q's, sound good?
00:11 Jordan (Northridge PM): yep sounds good, appreciate it — we have about 45 minutes.
00:18 Maya (BE): quick note, we're mostly evaluating for in-app triage chat, low latency 200-400ms targets for 512 token responses.
00:26 Alex: perfect, that's helpful. samir, want to kick off the sandbox?
00:30 Samir (Redwood SE): sure — i'll share my screen, bear with me. so first a very quick callout: we'll demo streaming with partial tokens, how params affect latency/quality, and then a failover example where we route to a cheaper variant. you might see some ASR mis- labels in the transcript, ignore those — live demo stuff.
00:52 Speaker 1: (screen noise)
01:05 Samir: ok, calling the chat endpoint now — here's the payload: messages history, temperature 0.2, max_tokens 512, top_p default, stop sequences set to ["\n\n"]. watch the stream events — we send DELTA chunks and an END event.
01:30 Maya: can you explain why you set temp so low?
01:33 Samir: yeah — for triage/chat we recommend 0.0-0.3 to reduce hallucinations; if you need creative outputs bump to 0.7. lower temp tends to be more deterministic which helps heuristics.
01:50 Jordan: and what about max_tokens — we're concerned about truncation for longer tickets.
01:55 Samir: for long context we suggest two options: increase max_tokens on the call or use prefix caching so your KV cache keeps earlier context off the wire. prefix caching reduces token roundtrip cost and keeps tail latency down.
02:15 Alex: i'll pull up Optimize suggestions — this is the console view that surfaced batching and quantization recommendations based on your workload profile.
02:29 Samir: quick demo of a retry: we force a 503 on the primary pool, you'll see client backoff at 500ms, 1s, 2s exponential — Redwood supports configurable retry policies and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant (same architecture/quantization family) when capacity is low.
02:50 Devon (Security): if you fallback to another model where logs or outputs differ, how do we preserve auditability?
02:56 Samir: good q — fallbacks are logged in the trace with model id and reasoning; you can require a policy that disables automatic fallback for certain routes, or route into Dedicated capacity if you need hard isolation. we emit audit logs and per-token costs in the console.
03:26 Jordan: can we pin a model version and still use the hosted API?
03:29 Alex: yes you can pin model versions in the API or console, and rollouts are supported (canary + percentage routing).
03:38 Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
04:05 Samir: showing a resume/idempotency example now — we send an idempotency_token in the header. if a request partially streams and the client reconnects, the resume token can pick up from the last acked sequence. it's not perfect speech-to-text; in some cases the client must re-request the tail but we've seen good reliability.
04:34 Maya: are resume tokens sticky across model changes?
04:38 Samir: resume tokens reference session state stored with the serving runtime; if you switch across incompatible model families the resume won't match and we'll return a short circuit so client can re-run. that's why we recommend same-family fallbacks for seamless resume.
05:02 Jordan: ok timeline question — if we go to pilot, how long to get sandbox access?
05:06 Alex: we can provision a sandbox today — i will send an invite after this call.
05:10 Alex: samir, walk through partial-chunk sizes and how that impacts latency.
05:14 Samir: sure. chunk size is driven by internal buffer flushes. we tune to flush every ~40-60 tokens or 200ms whichever comes first for low-latency configs. smaller chunks mean more network overhead but faster first-byte. Optimize suggests a sweet spot per model/workload — the console shows token/latency heatmaps.
06:00 Jordan: what about retries — do you do client-side only or server-side guards?
06:05 Samir: both. Redwood provides server-side rate limiting and graceful congestion signals (early 429 with retry-after in headers). client libraries have built-in exponential backoff with jitter and idempotency_token support so you don't double-charge.
06:28 Maya: double charge — do you mean double tokens billed?
06:31 Samir: yes, retries that re-execute generation can incur extra tokens, unless the server deduplicates based on idempotency_token and returns cached result for duplicate requests. we recommend idempotency for operations that are not user-visible or that can be retried safely.
06:56 Alex: demoing console trace now — here is a sample trace for a failed request: timeline, first-byte latency, model switch, and a fall back to an m-chat-8q variant. you can click into the trace and see the exact model selection and the reason (capacity spike).
07:23 Devon: do you support customer-managed keys (KMS) for logs?
07:27 Alex: yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM; for hosted we integrate with cloud KMS and can enable envelope encryption for log exports.
07:40 Jordan: great. curious about cost tradeoffs — how much cheaper is fallback variant?
07:44 Samir: depends strongly on quantization and architecture — an 8-bit quantized variant can be 30-60% cheaper per token; Optimize shows historic cost deltas per model.
08:01 Jordan: could that affect quality for triage? even small differences in phrasing could change triage heuristics.
08:05 Samir: yep that's a known tradeoff — Optimize will run regression checks on your prompt/testset and flag quality regressions. you can configure automatic rollback if metric delta exceeds threshold.
08:24 Speaker 3: (typing noise)
08:40 Samir: moving to a live failure scenario — i'll simulate a partial network cut during a stream. watch the client reconnect and use the idempotency header to request resume.
09:02 Samir: (typing) ok simulating. client reconnects — server returns resume_token: seq45 — client asks for events after seq45 and continues stream. you can see a slight delay but no duplication.
09:32 Maya: neat. in our infra we typically have WebSocket multiplexers — is the event stream compatible?
09:37 Samir: yes, Redwood supports both server-sent events (SSE), WebSockets, and gRPC streaming. semantics are consistent: DELTA events then a FINAL event. some client libs will normalize these for you.
09:56 Jordan: in the console, can we see per-customer latency P95?
10:00 Alex: yep, per-route/per-customer metrics with token-level breakdowns and P50/P95/P99. you can set alerts on regressions.
10:10 Devon: how are logs retained? we're regulated so 7 years may be required for certain audit trails.
10:15 Alex: hosted retention defaults to 90 days but we offer enterprise retention add-ons and an on-prem/private deployment which you can configure for longer retention and transfer to your SIEM via secure export.
10:32 Maya: let's talk about tokenization differences — we preprocess and store as utf-8, but do you do any normalization that could change tokens?
10:40 Samir: the runtime uses consistent BPE vocab per model; if you retokenize with a different vocab you can see token count differences. Optimize will surface token budgeting suggestions per model.
11:05 Jordan: great, can you demo a real request pattern from our app? we sent over a sample convo earlier.
11:10 Samir: pulling it in now. sample has long context + attachments reference. i'll show how prefix caching can keep the heavy context server-side: when we hit the endpoint we attach a prefix_id instead of sending the full long prompt. subsequent calls reference prefix_id and the runtime merges context.
11:34 Maya: curious about eviction — if prefix cache evicts, do we get a signal?
11:38 Samir: yes you get a 409-like response indicating prefix not found; client can either re-upload or degrade gracefully. eviction policy is LRU and configurable. Optimize suggests cache size based on your traffic patterns.
12:02 Jordan: earlier you mentioned batching — what's safe for chat? our calls are user-driven so batching may add latency.
12:10 Samir: batching is more applicable for large throughput async jobs. for interactive chat we keep batch windows very small (10-50ms) or rely on continuous batching in the runtime to combine micro-batches without delaying user obs. Optimize will recommend batch targets that meet your latency SLO.
12:31 Alex: showing the Optimize recommendations again: this customer profile (sample data) gets a 22% cost reduction with prefix cache + small quantized model family for non-critical routes.
12:50 Devon: on security: do you provide RBAC controls for who can change routing/fallback policies?
12:55 Alex: yes, console has RBAC roles (Viewer, Operator, Admin) and API keys can be tied to scopes. audit trail records the change.
13:12 Maya: exercise: how to handle a stuck stream that never returns FINAL?
13:16 Samir: client should set a window timeout; if no FINAL after X seconds, client cancels and re-requests with idempotency_token. server side we also have TTLs and will close stalled sessions. logs show last acked seq so you can resume.
13:40 Jordan: any limitations with function/tool calling in streaming?
13:43 Samir: tool/function calls are streamed as structured DELTA chunks; we send tool_call start and end events. if a tool call fails mid-stream we include a tool_error event and you can retry or fallback. some SDKs will buffer structured events into a single obj for you.
14:03 Alex: ok quick break — any burning q's?
14:07 Devon: do you have a SOC2 report we can review?
14:09 Alex: yes i'll share the SOC2 PDF and our network diagram after this; i'll add to next steps.
14:18 Jordan: can you repeat binder details for the sandbox tokens? we have strict IP allowlist.
14:22 Alex: we'll provision sandbox in an isolated VPC range you give us; tokens are scoped and can be rotated. we'll include IP allowlist instructions in the invite.
14:35 Samir: moving to a short troubleshooting demo — i'll show a sample where a client made duplicate calls without idempotency and was double-billed; then i'll show behavior with idempotency_token where server returns cached result and billing is single-run.
15:05 Maya: good to see. do you expose per-request billable token counts in the trace?
15:09 Alex: yes per-request token counts and cost estimates are in the trace and cost dashboard.
15:20 Jordan: timeline for pilot infra — we need dedicated pool versus hosted? our SLA requires 99.9 for triage path.
15:28 Samir: for 99.9 and strict isolation, Dedicated is recommended. Hosted can hit high availability but don't guarantee isolation unless Dedicated. we can do hybrid: host critical routes in Dedicated and leave other routes on hosted with fallbacks.
15:50 Devon: is the Dedicated deployment a managed service or do we host the infra?
15:55 Alex: Dedicated is reserved capacity managed by Redwood; Private (VPC/on-prem) is an option if you need full control. Dedicated gives SLA and capacity reservation.
16:10 Jordan: ok, next steps?
16:13 Alex: i'll recap in a sec. samir, any final demo bits?
16:17 Samir: one last note — watch the console trace when a fallback happens: we log the reason code (CAPACITY_CONSTRAINT or POLICY_BLOCK) and you can set alerts. also, Optimize can proactively recommend increasing Dedicated capacity when your P95 latency crosses thresholds.
16:40 Alex: recap of next steps — send SOC2 and network diagram, provision sandbox with IP allowlist, share quickstart repo and code snippets, schedule a pilot kickoff the week of Feb 10, and a separate deep-dive on Dedicated sizing if they want.
17:00 Jordan: that works. any other q's?
17:05 Maya: none from me.
17:08 Devon: okay, thanks everyone.
17:12 Alex: thanks all — we'll follow up with materials.
17:20 (meeting ends)

Send SOC2 report and network diagram via secure link
Provision sandbox with IP allowlist and scoped tokens (Alex to send invite)
Share quickstart repo and sample prefix-cache code (Alex/Samir)
SE to run synthetic latency + throughput benchmark with customer sample data w/target week 2025-02-03: run by 2025-02-07
Alex Chen - send SOC2 + network diagram by 2025-02-03
Alex Chen - provision sandbox and invite Northridge by 2025-02-01
Samir Patel - run synthetic latency benchmark and share raw traces by 2025-02-07
Jordan Reyes - provide representative conversation logs and expected SLOs by 2025-02-03
Devon O'Neill - confirm required log retention policy and export targets by 2025-02-05

Ceres Diagnostics - Renewal & Staggered Burst Clauses / VPC Pathway

Monthly renewal/expansion check-in focused on contract window options, introducing a staggered burst clause for seasonal load, and clarifying VPC onboarding and KMS expectations. Customer requested a mix of reserved capacity plus a predictable burst buffer and a compliance checklist for SOC2/KMS integration. Redwood to provide redline options and an estimated cost delta for burst tiers plus VPC onboarding runbook.
Renewal term and timing
Staggered burst capacity proposal
VPC/on-prem pathway and timelines
KMS/encryption & audit logs
Pilot phasing and benchmarks
Samir - Send 2 redlined contract options (12mo vs 24mo) and three burst-tier addenda - due 2026-10-20
Lena - Share VPC onboarding checklist + estimated provisioning timeline (staging to prod) - due 2026-10-18
Maya - Provide historical usage export (last 90 days) and sample prompts for perf eval - due 2026-10-19
Tom - Confirm internal approval window for 24mo commit and procurement constraints - due 2026-10-22
Priya - Share KMS vendor and any additional encryption requirements for review - due 2026-10-20
Redwood to send redlines and burst pricing by Wed (10/20)
Customer to deliver usage data and KMS details for security review
Schedule technical pilot run for EU VPC staging week of 10/25
Follow-up call to review pricing and legal terms on 10/26
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samir from Redwood here, joining with Lena and Maya. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Dr. Elena: Hi, Elena Ruiz from Ceres.
[00:10] Tom: Tom Bowers, platform.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, security lead.
[00:15] Samir: Awesome. Goal today is to land on renewal cadence and talk through the burst clause idea you asked about plus VPC pathing. Roughly 45 minutes. Sound good?
[00:25] Dr. Elena: Yep, that's right. We're mainly trying to understand the cost delta for predictable bursts vs increasing base commit. Also need to confirm the KMS flow for private keys.
[00:34] Lena: Quick save, when you say predictable bursts, do you mean scheduled seasonal uplift or on-demand overflow?
[00:40] Dr. Elena: Both, actually. We have scheduled upticks for end-of-quarter processing and occasional ad-hoc spikes when partner plugins run reports.
[00:50] Tom: Our ops ask is we want a cap so we can forecast egress and cost, not surprise bills.
[00:55] Samir: Totally. So we've been experimenting with a staggered-burst addendum — it's basically a committed baseline plus a tiered burst pool with fixed rates per tier and an overage safety cap. Gives predictability.
[01:06] Priya: Important for us is how bursts are routed. If it goes through multi-tenant hosted, we need assurance on data residency and logs. SOC2 is a must.
[01:16] Maya: We'll make sure the burst instances honor the same data controls — audit logs, token redaction, retention policies.
[01:23] [00:30] Lena: Technical note: The burst instances can be spun from your dedicated pool or fall back to a lower-latency hosted variant; there's a kernel-selection path there, but for VPC usage we prefer dedicated farm in your VPC to maintain network egress boundaries.
[00:38] Tom: So the question — do we assign burst capacity to their VPC or do we let Redwood broker it?
[00:43] Samir: You can do either. If you own the dedicated capacity in your VPC (private deployment), you get full control and egress predictability. If you use Redwood-hosted burst, it's faster to activate but less isolated. There's a middle ground — dedicated reserved plus a Redwood-managed burst pool that routes via a private peering link.
[00:58] Priya: We need the private peering approach to pass our security review. It keeps a single egress path from our VPC.
[01:04] Dr. Elena: Risk question — what's the failover if our dedicated pool saturates? We can't have requests hang.
[01:10] Lena: We have automatic fallback policies: canary to a compatible quantized model or route to regionally adjacent cluster. You can configure SLOs — like maintain p95 under 400ms — or prefer cost minimal.
[01:22] Tom: Hmm, p95 400ms might be optimistic during peaks. What's realistic with the current model mix?
[01:27] Lena: For your workload (short prompts, 1-2k tokens typical) in dedicated 8x A100 class, p95 is around 180-220ms. With burst routing to a managed pool you'd see p95 in the 300-500ms window depending on batch width. These are ballpark numbers; we'll run a pilot.
[01:43] [01:30] Samir: On contract structure, two practical options: 12-month renewal with increased baseline + optional burst addendum, or 24-month commit with lower unit price and burst pool included at a discounted rate.
[01:49] Dr. Elena: Procurement would prefer 24mo if the burst pricing is predictable. But our legal needs a staggered clause so we can increase capacity mid-term without a full amendment.
[01:58] Maya: We can draft a staggered-capacity amendment that lists tranches — e.g., +20% at Q2, +50% at Q4 — with pre-defined pricing bands. That avoids renegotiating.
[02:07] Priya: For SOC2 and KMS — we need your KMS integration doc. Primary questions: key rotation policy, who controls keys (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed), and HSM attestation.
[02:19] Lena: Redwood supports both customer-managed KMS (we integrate via VPC endpoints) and Redwood-managed KMS. For Ceres, if you choose CMK (customer-managed keys), we never persist plaintext; we do envelope encryption and only store ciphertext. We can send the KMS architecture doc.
[02:35] Tom: About audit logs — we need token-level tracing and per-request headers logged for three months. Any egress costs for logs?
[02:43] Maya: Audit logs are provided; retention beyond the default window is an add-on. No additional egress for logs within the VPC peering, but long-term storage may incur costs. We'll itemize that.
[02:55] [02:50] Dr. Elena: Timeline wise — we want VPC staging in EU (frankfurt) by end of October, a short pilot the following week, and production by mid-November if approvals land. Is that feasible?
[03:05] Lena: It's tight but doable: provisioning VPC peering, key exchange, and baseline reserved capacity takes 2-3 weeks if procurement and security are responsive. If you can confirm baseline numbers this week, we can aim for staging 10/25.
[03:16] Tom: I'll try to lock down baseline numbers by Friday.
[03:19] Priya: One more on encryption — do you offer bring-your-own-HSM (BYOHSM) options? We need FIPS 140-2 attestations for some workloads.
[03:26] Lena: We don't host customer HSMs inside Redwood; on private deployments you can integrate your HSM via standard KMS bridges. We have customers with HSMs in their VPC that we've integrated. We'll include the integration pattern.
[03:36] [03:30] Samir: Pricing — ballpark numbers: 24mo commit roughly 18% lower unit cost vs 12mo, and burst tiers are priced as fixed increments: Tier A (burst cushion 20% usage) +8%; Tier B (50%) +17%; emergency overage cap kicks in at +40% marginal rate. We'll send a spreadsheet.
[03:53] Dr. Elena: Those increments look reasonable, but procurement needs the exact math. Also want a cancellation clause if we onboard a new partner and shift traffic.
[04:03] Maya: We can offer a limited break clause with 60-day notice tied to a migration event, subject to minimums. We'll flag it in the redlines.
[04:11] [04:00] Tom: On benchmarking — we want Redwood to run three target prompts (we'll share) against the staging cluster to validate p95 and cost per token. Can you run with our sample dataset?
[04:21] Lena: Yes, if you provide the prompts and a small representative dataset, we can run controlled runs and give a profiling report — latency, token cost, batching behavior, and KV cache hit rates.
[04:33] Priya: For the run, can we require that logs exclude PHI? Our prompts sometimes contain redacted patient IDs. Need clarity on redaction.
[04:40] Maya: We'll respect redaction flags; advise to pre-redact any PHI before handing prompts. We'll include guidance.
[04:48] [04:45] Samir: Okay, let's recap actions — I'll produce the two contract options and burst addenda sheet; Lena will send the VPC/KMS runbook and provisioning timeline; Maya will ask for the usage export format and retention options. Ceres to produce usage and KMS vendor details and confirm internal timeline.
[05:03] Dr. Elena: Sounds good. One last off-hand — any updates on regional model variants? We sometimes see different latency in eu-west vs eu-central.
[05:12] Lena: We maintain comparable model variants; differences are mostly infra locality and kernel tuning. We'll include region-specific perf notes in the report.
[05:20] [05:15] Priya: Also, please include a sample SOC2 addendum and a list of sub-processors. We need that for our legal pack.
[05:26] Maya: We'll attach the SOC2 report link and full sub-processor list in the follow-up email.
[05:32] Tom: Great. If we can get the cost spreadsheet and redlines by Wed, procurement will take a look and we'll reconvene.
[05:38] Samir: Perfect. Thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the 10/26 pricing review.
[05:44] Dr. Elena: Thanks everyone, bye.
[05:46] [End of recording]

document.content:
Bridgeway - Embeddings & Hosting Options Discovery

Discovery focused on embeddings/rerank architecture, vector DB integration choices, throughput projections, and hosting tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC). Customer emphasized strict PII controls, SOC2 + regional residency, and a Q4 pilot target. SE offered a benchmark plan and suggested quantized embeddings + hybrid rerank for cost/latency balance.
current stack and pain points
vector DB integration options
throughput and tail latency
embedding dimensionality and quantization
hybrid search + rerank architecture
hosting modes: hosted/dedicated/private (VPC)
security/compliance requirements
pilot success criteria and timeline
00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about 45 minutes. Quick intro, I'm Alex from Redwood, joined by Priya our solution engineer. 00:22 Markus Vogel: Yeah hi, Markus here, CTO at Bridgeway Analytics. We all good. 00:28 Aisha Khan: Aisha - Head of Search. We want to talk embed pipeline and where to run it. 00:35 Alex Chen: Cool. Could you start with current infra and volumes? 00:42 Devon Lee: Sure, we run a mixed infra. Primary search is Elastic for metadata, we use a self-hosted vector DB (open source) for embeddings right now; throughput spikes are common, like 2k-3k embedding requests per minute during biz hours, and rerank calls are bursty on search pages. 01:05 Priya Nair: Ok do you do embeddings online sync or batch? 01:09 Devon Lee: Hybrid - initial batch for backlog and then online upsert for user content. 01:15 Aisha Khan: Our latency SLO for search front-end is 300ms P95, and rerank can be slightly higher but we prefer sub-200ms for the second stage. 01:27 Alex Chen: Makes sense. When you say self-hosted vector DB, are you on Milvus/Pinecone-managed or custom? 01:35 Devon Lee: It's a custom fork of Milvus, running on k8s. We found some ops pain with sharding and rebalances. 01:41 Markus Vogel: The key drivers for us are: cost predictability, strict data controls (no raw vectors leaving our VPC for PII content), and reproducible quality — we measure NDCG for rerank. 01:56 Priya Nair: Understood. We usually evaluate three hosting options: Redwood Hosted API (fast to start), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), or Redwood Private which runs in your VPC / on-prem. Sounds like Private might be interesting because of the PII requirement. 02:15 Aisha Khan: Yes, private is attractive. But we also want to know performance delta — is Dedicated near-hosted in latency? 02:24 Alex Chen: In many cases dedicated is near-hosted; the difference comes down to networking and scale. Hosted has global infra, and Dedicated gives you reserved capacity co-located with predictable throughput. Private adds your network egress and KMS controls so slightly more tail latency depending on connectivity. 02:44 Devon Lee: What about KV cache and prefix caching? We rely on KV for session state but would like auto cache for repeated prefixes. 02:52 Priya Nair: Our runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching. For heavy rerank workloads we often recommend KV cache + short TTLs to keep tail latency low. 03:04 Markus Vogel: On embeddings: we're using 1536-d vectors today. We're debating lowering dims to 768 to save cost, but worried about recall drop. 03:16 Priya Nair: Tradeoffs there are workload dependent. For semantic retrieval 1536 can help, but quantization (int8/4) plus a smaller dimension can often preserve NDCG if you tune the reranker. We suggested running a dimension sweep in eval. 03:33 Aisha Khan: Would Redwood run that eval or do we run locally? 03:38 Alex Chen: We can run a joint eval — our Optimize toolkit will suggest quantization and dim profiles given a sample corpus and query set. We usually do a small A/B on reranker quality. 03:50 Devon Lee: Integration with our vector DB: we want to avoid wholesale migration. Can Redwood handle hybrid search where topk from our DB is combined with Redwood embeddings/rerank? 03:59 Priya Nair: Yes, hybrid setups are common — you can do vector fanout from your DB to Redwood's rerank model or call Redwood to generate embeddings and push to your DB; we support both. Also fallback routing to a cheaper quantized model for lower SLAs. 04:18 Markus Vogel: Any constraints on throughput per second? Our spike profile is 200 qps for rerank at peak. 04:25 Priya Nair: For rerank at 200 qps we'd look at Dedicated or Private with reserved GPUs. Hosted can handle it but cost unpredictability during sustained spikes is a concern. We recommend a dedicated pool with autoscale and burst capacity. 04:39 Aisha Khan: How do you shard embedding compute if our DB is sharded? 04:45 Priya Nair: We align shard topology with your DB fanout; Redwood's routing can route requests by shard key to the right serving pool, which reduces cross-shard copies and KV cache misses. 04:58 Devon Lee: Security questions: do you provide SOC2 docs, SSO, SAML, and KMS integration? 05:06 Alex Chen: Yes to all. We provide SOC2 Type II reports, SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning; in Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management. 05:18 Markus Vogel: For Private, is the control plane still Redwood-hosted? 05:22 Alex Chen: Usually yes — control plane can be in Redwood but with strict audit logs and RBAC; we also offer fully air-gapped options for certain regs but that is a contract-level discussion. 05:33 Aisha Khan: About benchmarks — can we run an on-prem perf test for our real queries? 05:37 Priya Nair: Absolutely. We usually run a smoke benchmark with your sample traffic, evaluating P50/P95/P99 and token cost. We'll need a small dataset and a few thousand queries to be representative. 05:50 Devon Lee: On cost, what levers do we have? 05:53 Priya Nair: Model size, quantization level, batching config, and routing policies. For embeddings cost we can push quantized float8/int4 and reduce dims; for rerank model we can use a smaller distilled model for the first-pass and full model for final ranking. 06:09 Markus Vogel: Our timeline is Q4 pilot, production in Q1. We need security review next week if possible. 06:16 Alex Chen: Noted. We'll send security pack and a pilot scope doc. 06:20 Aisha Khan: Actionable: we'd like a clear plan: integration steps with our vector DB, benchmark run, and pilot pricing. 06:27 Priya Nair: We'll propose a 4-week pilot: week 1 bootstrap + connectivity, week 2 perf/quality eval, week 3 config tuning (quant/dim), week 4 run pilot traffic and final report. 06:40 Devon Lee: For connectivity, our infra sits in AWS eu-west-2 and we use private VPC peering for critical data. Can Redwood support VPC peering? 06:49 Alex Chen: Yes for Private and Dedicated we can peer; Hosted supports TLS+private IP via partner connections in some regions. 06:58 Aisha Khan: Any gotchas on vector serialization/compatibility? 07:02 Priya Nair: We support common vector formats (float32 arrays, int8 packs) and have small adapters for Milvus/FAISS/Weaviate. Expect small conversions but nothing major. 07:14 Markus Vogel: Competitors we looked at: Pinecone, built-in vendor endpoints and some self-hosted toolchains. 07:21 Alex Chen: Right. Our differentiation: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, cost controls and routing policy, and first-class eval tooling. 07:30 Aisha Khan: Questions about SLA: what's your typical P95 uptime for Dedicated? 07:34 Alex Chen: We offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated (99.9+) and monitoring hooks; full SLA in contract. 07:41 Devon Lee: Can you demonstrate end-to-end latency numbers for a sample rerank flow? 07:44 Priya Nair: We'll share a benchmark sheet; rough numbers now: optimized rerank on 1-2 GPUs gives sub-100ms P95 for short context and cached KV; without caching expect higher. 07:59 Markus Vogel: Good. Next steps? 08:02 Alex Chen: We'll send security docs, pilot scope, pricing matrix, and a short list of data needed. Also schedule SE-led benchmark next Tue if that works. 08:14 Aisha Khan: Tue works. We'll prepare an eval set, 5k queries and sample docs, and an infra contact for peering. 08:22 Devon Lee: I'll be the infra contact, email devon@bridgeway.ai. 08:26 Alex Chen: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and links. 08:31 End of recording.

document.content:
Console lab: trace playback & request forensics - HelioPharm

Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 68 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Arjun Singh (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (HelioPharm SRE Lead), Noah Kim (Platform Eng), Priya Rao (CTO)
----
Auto-summary: Quick hands-on lab exploring Redwood Console trace playback and request forensics. Focus on reproducing a customer error path, KV cache/ prefix cache behavior, fallbacks between model variants, and retention/compliance controls (audit logs, KMS). Agreed next steps: run a 24h replay of sample traces and share the cost/latency profile.
Topics covered: 1) trace playback UI and filters; 2) request-level logs and correlated spans; 3) error analysis patterns; 4) routing/fallback behavior; 5) private deployment / VPC considerations.
Action items (auto): see action_items metadata.
----
Transcript:
[00:00:05] Maya Patel: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, quick intros? this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE and i'll run the agenda, arjun is our solutions engineer and he'll do the deep console walkthrough.
[00:00:18] Dr. Lena Ortiz: hi lena here, SRE lead at HelioPharm. we run models for dosing guidance in production, so latency and correctness both matter, uh, a lot.
[00:00:25] Noah Kim: Noah, platform. curious about request logs size & retention, and how we can replay a day of traffic without burning a ton of tokens.
[00:00:30] Priya Rao: Priya, CTO. i'll listen in for compliance bits.
[00:00:33] Arjun Singh: great thanks, let's jump in. i'll share my screen and start in the Console -> Trace Playback. if anyone can't see ping maya.
[00:00:45] [screen share begins]
[00:01:05] Arjun Singh: alright so this is the trace index, we've got 14k traces in this project, i'm filtering to the last 24 hours, and i'm going to show a failed path that lena sent over - it shows a model timeout then fallback to a smaller variant and later a KV cache miss.
[00:01:30] Dr. Lena Ortiz: yeah the error triggers when patients' notes hit about 4k tokens, we see a burst of timeouts around 9am PST on tuesday.
[00:01:40] Arjun Singh: okay i'm applying the token-length filter and the latency spike, you can see aggregated latency heatmap here, this is the request histogram.
[00:01:55] Maya Patel: quick note, our histogram buckets are adaptive; they change based on the distribution, so when you zoom on 4k+ tokens you get finer buckets.
[00:02:12] [00:02:12] Noah Kim: is that live or sampled? we can't pull everything for compliance reasons.
[00:02:18] Arjun Singh: good question, the index is a combination - traces are retained as metadata for the full 30 days by default, but full request payloads are sampled; you can configure deterministic sampling for specific routes so all e.g. /dose-eval requests are kept.
[00:02:35] [00:02:35] Dr. Lena Ortiz: so deterministic sampling ties to route name and model id?
[00:02:42] Arjun Singh: yep you can pin it to route+model+customer tag; that way we only store full payloads for anything matching the signature you give.
[00:02:55] [00:02:55] Maya Patel: and for SOC2/ISO, we offer an audit log export and KMS-backed encryption of request payloads - arjun will show encryption toggles in a sec.
[00:03:08] [00:03:08] Arjun Singh: jumping into a single trace now - top-level view shows timeline, spans, and any fallback events. here you can see the initial tokenization span, then inference span where the timeout occurs, followed by the fallback to a 7B variant.
[00:03:30] [00:03:30] Arjun Singh: the span annotations show exit codes, GPU utilization, and kernel warnings; sometimes transcription calls them "kernel warn" but it's basically a tensor-core oom or kernel launch stall.
[00:03:45] [00:03:45] Dr. Lena Ortiz: can you show the raw request body? we need to check prompt prefixes for pii leakage risk.
[00:03:51] Arjun Singh: sure, here's the payload inspector. note: if payload is redacted due to compliance settings you'll see a redaction banner. for this trace the payload is available - you can copy or download.
[00:04:08] [00:04:08] Noah Kim: how big are those payload blobs typically? i'm worried about egress and storage cost.
[00:04:14] Arjun Singh: we store compressed blobs, typical payloads are 2-20KB compressed; embeddings and attachments increase that. our suggestion is to enable route-level deterministic sampling only for the few routes you're actively debugging.
[00:04:30] [00:04:30] Priya Rao: what about KMS - who holds the keys if we do Private?
[00:04:36] Arjun Singh: for Private deployments you retain keys in your KMS/HSM. for Dedicated and Hosted we integrate with customer KMS via envelope encryption; we can give a diagram. maya i'll flag the network diagram for priya.
[00:04:49] Maya Patel: noted - will include network and kms integration diagram in the follow-up.
[00:04:55] [00:04:55] Arjun Singh: back to the trace timeline — here's where Redwood routed the request: primary model was rwd-large-v1, fallback policy triggered after 6s and routed to rwd-medium-q4, you can see the fallback event recorded with reason code and cost delta.
[00:05:14] [00:05:14] Dr. Lena Ortiz: that cost delta number is important, can you show the per-token breakdown for the fallback?
[00:05:21] Arjun Singh: yes, there's a token-cost panel that pops out; it shows tokens generated, tokens billed, and unit cost normalized by model. note that quantized variants like rwd-medium-q4 have lower per-token cost but sometimes higher latency for very long contexts.
[00:05:40] [00:05:40] Noah Kim: earlier you mentioned KV cache miss - can you show where that appears in the trace?
[00:05:47] Arjun Singh: sure, here — we annotate KV cache hits/misses as spans; in this trace the first chunk was a cache miss because the request used a new prompt prefix, so the runtime had to re-compute key values which cost us time.
[00:06:00] [00:06:00] Dr. Lena Ortiz: so is prefix caching automatic or do we need to configure it on the client?
[00:06:06] Arjun Singh: prefix caching is automatic for repeated prefixes, but you can also pin prefixes via the SDK to force caching server-side. there's also a TTL per-prefix setting.
[00:06:22] [00:06:22] Maya Patel: many customers see a big win from prefix pinning for conversational assistants that have a stable system prompt.
[00:06:30] [00:06:30] Noah Kim: can you simulate a cache warm-up on the Console? like run synthetic warm calls?
[00:06:36] Arjun Singh: yes in the Console there's a 'Warm' action on the route which will push a synthetic set of requests to warm KV caches across the pool; we usually suggest a small burst during deploy windows.
[00:06:48] [00:06:48] Dr. Lena Ortiz: if we warm, does that increase our billed tokens?
[00:06:52] Arjun Singh: warm calls are billed same as normal, but you can mark them as internal so they don't count against end-user quotas; cost still incurred.
[00:07:06] [00:07:06] Priya Rao: let's talk about replicating the incident - can we replay the exact sequence for the 9am spike?
[00:07:13] Arjun Singh: yes we can. Arjun continuing: in the playback mode you can select a time window and choose 'replay in staging' which will re-execute the requests against a pinned model in a sandbox. i'll demo: selecting 08:45-09:15, selecting the route, and clicking replay.
[00:07:32] [00:07:32] [clicks]
[00:07:40] [00:07:40] Arjun Singh: ok replay job created - note that replays are rate-limited and you can throttle to match production QPS; we also provide a dry-run where we only simulate without consuming quota if you don't need full inference.
[00:07:55] [00:07:55] Dr. Lena Ortiz: dry-run could be useful for initial triage, yes. but for root cause we'll probably want the full replay.
[00:08:03] [00:08:03] Noah Kim: what about routing policies - is it possible a node was overloaded and triggered fallbacks? how is that surfaced?
[00:08:10] Arjun Singh: routing telemetry includes per-node CPU/GPU saturation metrics and a routing decision trace. if a pool reports overload the routing tier logs an overloaded flag and you'll see increased fallback rates in the route analytics.
[00:08:24] [00:08:24] Maya Patel: also our autoscaling policies can be tuned - you can configure target latency, buffer queue length, and max burst nodes. we'll share sample configs that mirror HelioPharm's QPS.
[00:08:36] [00:08:36] [00:08:36] Dr. Lena Ortiz: what about private deployment though - network egress is restricted for our infra team, we might need an on-prem option.
[00:08:44] Arjun Singh: for Private we ship a control plane and you run inference in your VPC or on-prem; logs and traces stay within your network by default. we've done air-gapped installs for pharma customers; it requires a connector for updates and a staging sync process.
[00:09:03] [00:09:03] Priya Rao: compliance will want signed audit trails for who accessed traces. can we get a per-user audit export?
[00:09:10] Arjun Singh: yes the audit logs include user, action, timestamp, and resources accessed. you can export as JSON or append to your SIEM. for hosted setups we stream audit logs to customer S3 or BigQuery.
[00:09:24] [00:09:24] Maya Patel: i'm going to drop the SOC2 artifact link in chat now - it covers audit log retention and encryption flow.
[00:09:30] [chat link posted]
[00:09:36] [00:09:36] Arjun Singh: jumping into error analysis - here's a common pattern: long context -> tokenization spike -> kv miss -> model OOM -> fallback. the console flags this as an "inference chain" and suggests remediation steps like prefix pinning, chunking, or model aliasing.
[00:09:56] [00:09:56] Dr. Lena Ortiz: chunking might break some of our prompt semantics, have you got examples for safely chunking clinical notes?
[00:10:04] Arjun Singh: we have a chunking helper in the SDK that preserves question/answer pairs and folds metadata. it's not perfect for every use case but we've got a clinic-specific pattern pack we can share.
[00:10:16] [00:10:16] Noah Kim: Arjun, can you show the correlation between request logs and our external observability? we use Datadog.
[00:10:22] Arjun Singh: sure - there's a correlation pane where you can paste a trace id and it will link to any external link we have mapped, like Datadog or Splunk. we also include a trace id header in requests so you can join on that side.
[00:10:36] [00:10:36] [00:10:36] Priya Rao: who typically triggers a replay job - are there RBAC controls? we don't want engineers accidentally replaying production traffic.
[00:10:45] Arjun Singh: RBAC is granular - replay create requires 'ops:replay' permission which you can limit to a role. replay approvals are optional; you can enable an approval workflow that routes to a pager duty or Slack channel for sign-off.
[00:10:58] [00:10:58] Dr. Lena Ortiz: nice. can the approval include a scrub step for PII?
[00:11:04] Arjun Singh: yes we support pre-replay transformation hooks where you can run a lambda to scrub sensitive fields; if the hook fails the replay won't start.
[00:11:14] [00:11:14] Maya Patel: quick aside, a lot of customers confuse 'trace retention' with 'payload retention'. traces (metadata) are cheap and kept longer; full payloads are controlled by sampling.
[00:11:25] [00:11:25] Noah Kim: back to cost - do you have a sample cost report from a 24h replay?
[00:11:32] Arjun Singh: yes i'll pull an example. this one replays 60k requests, default throttled to 200 qps, cost was $1,200 and average latency increased about 15% due to serialization overhead in staging. i'll attach the CSV in follow-up.
[00:11:52] [00:11:52] Dr. Lena Ortiz: what about cold-starts on shards? during the spike we also saw a flurry of node restarts. can the trace show node restart correlations?
[00:12:00] Arjun Singh: node events are correlated; you'll see a node lifecycle span in the trace. if a restart overlapped the request the trace will show the restart and the routing layer will log an eviction event.
[00:12:12] [00:12:12] Priya Rao: how do you instrument that without too much noise? we don't want pages for every tiny restart.
[00:12:19] Arjun Singh: thresholds for alerting are configurable; we recommend a cluster-level SLO and to only alert on sustained error budgets or repeated evictions.
[00:12:31] [00:12:31] Maya Patel: quick poll - is priority one for you to figure out the 9am spike root cause, or to validate whether Private deployment is feasible?
[00:12:40] Dr. Lena Ortiz: root cause first, Private next.
[00:12:43] Noah Kim: agree.
[00:12:45] Arjun Singh: okay i'll run a replay on your sample traces and generate the trace map. can you share the sample again to the secure upload link?
[00:12:52] Dr. Lena Ortiz: uploading now, link in chat.
[00:12:58] [chat link posted]
[00:13:05] [00:13:05] Arjun Singh: got it. starting the job in replay-sandbox mode with full payloads, throttled to 150 qps. I'll attach the job id in chat.
[00:13:16] [00:13:16] [job created]
[00:13:25] [00:13:25] Maya Patel: i'll put the follow-up items in calendar—proposed 30min check-in the week after the replay completes.
[00:13:33] [00:13:33] Dr. Lena Ortiz: sounds good. couple more quick console features: can we annotate traces internally for handoffs?
[00:13:39] Arjun Singh: yes, there's an annotations layer that supports @mentions and pinned notes; those show up in the audit trail too.
[00:13:50] [00:13:50] Noah Kim: curious about retention costs - if we keep 30 days of full payloads at 50GB/day how is that priced?
[00:13:57] Arjun Singh: there's an object storage charge plus a retrieval cost depending on your retention tier; we generally provide a cost calculator. I'll run a calc for 50GB/day and include it.
[00:14:10] [00:14:10] Dr. Lena Ortiz: for the failed requests, do you surface the exact exception from the model runtime? sometimes our SEs see ambiguous error codes.
[00:14:18] Arjun Singh: yes we surface runtime exceptions and map them to normalized reasons; sometimes transcriptions will show odd names like 'tensor stall' or 'kernel crash' but we include the underlying errno and stack snippet if available.
[00:14:33] [00:14:33] Priya Rao: are there examples of remediation playbooks? we need an ops runbook for a production incident.
[00:14:40] Arjun Singh: we have pre-built runbooks in the Console->Playbooks section; you can clone and customize them. they include steps for triage, warming, rollback, and escalation.
[00:14:50] [00:14:50] Dr. Lena Ortiz: excellent.
[00:14:55] [00:14:55] Maya Patel: i'll share a sample runbook tailored for long-context clinical notes.
[00:15:01] [00:15:01] [pause - brief questions about small UI items]
[00:16:12] [00:16:12] Arjun Singh: moving on, i want to highlight the cross-correlation map - it visualizes which downstream services were called per request. here you can see a call to our reranker; when the reranker failed we got a compounding slowdown.
[00:16:30] [00:16:30] Dr. Lena Ortiz: we actually run a custom reranker in house, can you call external services during replay?
[00:16:37] Arjun Singh: in replay you can toggle external call replay - by default it's disabled for safety; you can enable it and set a stub endpoint to mirror production behavior.
[00:16:50] [00:16:50] Noah Kim: does the console show per-model memory footprint during inference? that could help with OOM triage.
[00:16:57] Arjun Singh: yes the span metadata includes GPU memory before/after and peak usage. sometimes the names are abbreviated in the transcript export like 'mem peak' or 'vram high' but it's there.
[00:17:12] [00:17:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: one last thing - log stitching. we use correlation ids from our app logs; can we auto-stitch them?
[00:17:20] Arjun Singh: absolutely, if you pass X-Request-Id in headers we will stitch app logs that match. we support regex patterns to extract IDs from logs too.
[00:17:33] [00:17:33] Maya Patel: okay we're at the 30 minute mark, this is going well — any blockers?
[00:17:39] [00:17:39] Dr. Lena Ortiz: no blockers, just the usual: need to confirm SSO and the secure upload for traces.
[00:17:45] Maya Patel: noted.
[00:17:48] [00:17:48] Arjun Singh: i'll fast-forward through a few more advanced panels: the request timeline can be exported to CSV with annotations, and the trace graph can be opened in raw JSON; we do encourage customers to use the SDK for bulk analysis.
[00:18:03] [00:18:03] [fast demo - 6 minutes of clicks and short explanations omitted for brevity]
[00:24:10] [00:24:10] Arjun Singh: showing the anomaly detector now - it surfaces unusual fallback spikes and can auto-create a ticket in Jira. it's ML-based and learns your normal distribution.
[00:24:30] [00:24:30] Noah Kim: can we tune sensitivity so we don't get noisy alerts?
[00:24:34] Arjun Singh: yes you can set seasonality windows and minimum sample counts.
[00:24:40] [00:24:40] Dr. Lena Ortiz: what's the false positive rate generally?
[00:24:44] Arjun Singh: varies, but typically we tune to under 5% noise after a couple weeks of training.
[00:24:53] [00:24:53] Maya Patel: jumping back to the replay job - arjun did you set it to full payloads?
[00:24:58] Arjun Singh: yes full payloads for the first pass, throttled at 150 qps. i'll watch for any failover patterns and report.
[00:25:05] [00:25:05] Dr. Lena Ortiz: if it reproduces, can you narrow to exact spans so we can instrument additional metrics?
[00:25:11] Arjun Singh: yep we'll tag the exact spans with additional debug metrics and re-run.
[00:25:20] [00:25:20] [client-side question about API keys and token rotation]
[00:25:35] Arjun Singh: for API keys we support rotation and scoped keys per route; keys can be short lived and integrated with your secrets manager.
[00:25:44] [00:25:44] Priya Rao: do we get a bill preview for the replay? we need to approve budget before you run a big job.
[00:25:51] Maya Patel: i'll include a replay cost estimate in the follow-up and cc finance.
[00:25:59] [00:25:59] [00:26:00] Arjun Singh: ...and just to call out, if you run the replay in a Dedicated pool you can cap cost by limiting concurrency on the pool.
[00:26:10] [00:26:10] Dr. Lena Ortiz: curious about the model aliasing you mentioned - can we pin a failing route to an experimental quantized model?
[00:26:18] Arjun Singh: yes model aliases let you switch traffic or pin a single replay target without changing client code. useful for canaries.
[00:26:28] [00:26:28] Noah Kim: any gotchas with quantized variants and long contexts?
[00:26:32] Arjun Singh: quantized variants can sometimes have slightly different tokenization or higher latency in decode heavy workloads; we recommend an eval set. Redwood Optima - sorry, Redwood Optimize (console slip) can run an automated comparison across the variants.
[00:26:48] [00:26:48] Dr. Lena Ortiz: ha, yeah that Optimize tool is critical for us.
[00:26:52] [00:26:52] [00:26:52] Maya Patel: we're at the 40 minute mark, let's start to wrap and confirm next steps.
[00:27:00] [00:27:00] Arjun Singh: quick recap: Arjun will run the 24h replay (job id attached) and produce latency/cost CSV + highlighted spans; Maya will send SOC2 + network diagram + runbook; HelioPharm will schedule SSO window and share staging creds.
[00:27:18] [00:27:18] Dr. Lena Ortiz: perfect. one last question - are there limits on how many concurrent replays you accept per customer?
[00:27:25] Arjun Singh: we limit by account to avoid noisy neighbors; usually one large replay or up to three small ones concurrently. we can raise limits for Dedicated customers.
[00:27:36] [00:27:36] Noah Kim: ok thanks, that answers it.
[00:27:40] [00:27:40] Priya Rao: thanks everyone.
[00:27:43] [00:27:43] Maya Patel: thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and the job results.
[00:27:48] [00:27:48] [wrap-up niceties]
[00:28:00] [END OF MAIN DEMO - session moved to technical deep-dive Q&A for 40 more minutes]
[00:28:12] [00:28:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: quick technical question - in the event of a model downgrade fallback we saw a mismatched embedding flavor; is there a mapping table?
[00:28:23] Arjun Singh: yes we include compatibility mappings between model families; during fallback we can auto-run a convert step or emit a compatibility warning. sometimes transcripts will show 'embedding mismatch' which maps to a dtype/shape change.
[00:28:38] [00:28:38] Noah Kim: can we assert compatibility checks at ingress? like fail-fast if an incoming payload won't be compatible across variants.
[00:28:46] Arjun Singh: there's a validation hook in the router that can enforce compatibility or mutate the request automatically. you control that policy per-route.
[00:28:58] [00:28:58] Dr. Lena Ortiz: about the routing logs - do they include affinity info, so we can see if specific customers always land on the same shard?
[00:29:07] Arjun Singh: affinity is logged; you can query by customer tag and see node affinity heatmaps.
[00:29:15] [00:29:15] Maya Patel: we're at about 55 minutes now, any outstanding blockers?
[00:29:20] Dr. Lena Ortiz: just the SOC2 confirmation and the upload link, which you have.
[00:29:26] Maya Patel: ok i'll send checklist in email.
[00:29:30] [00:29:30] [misc small talk and contact exchange]
[00:31:00] [00:31:00] [session resumes with Arjun running a targeted replay and narrating findings: several small pauses where he inspects spans and annotates root cause candidates]
[00:38:10] [00:38:10] Arjun Singh: finding: a node restarted at 08:52:11 which correlated with three concurrent long-context requests; routing tried to rehome flows but one request hit a cold shard and had a KV miss causing a cascade. attaching span ids.
[00:38:32] [00:38:32] Dr. Lena Ortiz: that matches our logs - we see node restart logs around that time.
[00:38:36] [00:38:36] Arjun Singh: proposed mitigation: increase warm pool size during morning window and pin prefixes for multi-turn sessions.
[00:38:46] [00:38:46] Noah Kim: acceptable tradeoff, will try that config.
[00:38:52] [00:38:52] [00:38:52] Priya Rao: can you include the exact CLI commands to pin prefixes? our infra team prefers infra-as-code.
[00:38:59] Arjun Singh: yes i'll add those to the follow-up. example: rwdctl prefix pin --route /dose-eval --prefix "system:clinic:v1" --ttl 7d.
[00:39:10] [00:39:10] Dr. Lena Ortiz: great.
[00:39:14] [00:39:14] Maya Patel: ok final check: who will own the pilot?
[00:39:18] [00:39:18] Priya Rao: HelioPharm will own the pilot, with Maya as Redwood lead.
[00:39:24] Maya Patel: perfect, we'll send the pilot SOW and timeline.
[00:39:30] [00:39:30] [closing remarks and thanks]
[00:39:40] [00:39:40] Maya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Thursday with docs and the replay results.
[00:39:47] [00:39:47] Dr. Lena Ortiz: thanks.
[00:39:50] [END 60 MIN MARKER - remaining 8 minutes were short clarifying Q&A and chat link exchanges]
[00:48:00] [00:48:00] [minor crosstalk about upcoming holidays]
[00:50:12] [00:50:12] Maya Patel: okay signing off now.
[00:50:18] [00:50:18] [call ended]
