document.content:
POC Weekly Sync: Pin Matrix & Emergency Swap Playbook

Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-02
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (NexaBank), Evan Brooks (NexaBank), Sonal Iyer (NexaBank)
Links shared: pin-matrix template: https://redwood.app/sheets/pin-matrix-nexa, perf spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/sheets/nexa-perf

Summary (auto): quick review of week 2 POC metrics, discuss model pin matrix, define emergency swap playbook and next steps. Agreed to run extended throughput sweeps and rehearse swap.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay folks welcome back, thanks for joining. quick checkin for week two of the POC. we've got a few items on the agenda, latency trends, pin matrix, and the emergency swap playbook.
[00:28] Priya: thanks Maya, quick context — we're mostly concerned about tail latency at >2k tokens for our summarization pipeline and also want a clear rollback path if output quality regresses.
[00:40] Diego: got it, we'll walk through the numbers Diego (SE) here — uh, sorry, Diego — includes the ded pool runs and the host fallback behavior.
[00:54] Evan: one ask up front, can we avoid full on-prem for now, we'd prefer VPC private deployment but still under our KMS.
[01:08] Sonal: and security will need encryption at rest details plus audit log retention, that's non-negotiable.
[01:20] Maya: absolutely — we shared the SOC2 + ISO notes in the drive, and for KMS we have an integration doc, we'll post the specific KMS flow diagram after the call.
[01:35] Priya: great, thanks. can you also explain the difference between pinning a model and soft-fallbacks? we had a brief convo with platform about the catalog variants.
[01:48] Diego: yeah so quick definition: pinning means routing route X to a specific model version — it's sticky. soft-fallbacks are policy-based, e.g. if latency > x or capacity exhausted, route to a compatible variant (smaller/quantized) — there's also a shadow mode for validation.
[02:10] Maya: and we'll show the pin-matrix template — columns are route, model_id, version, percent_traffic (canary), fallback_model, fallback_condition.
[02:28] Evan: ping, what's the expected impact on throughput when you pin to an fp16 vs 4-bit quant? we've seen token cost variance up to 40%.
[02:40] Diego: in our bench, quant 4-bit gives 2.5x tokens/sec improvement on Ampere gen cards but you'd want to run quality evals — there's a tradeoff. our Optimize recommendations give a cost/lquality delta per workload.
[03:02] Priya: ok can you surface that delta specifically for our summarization test set?
[03:10] Diego: yes — action: I'll run a focused quality run comparing fp16, q4 and q2 on the same prompt set and attach results.
[03:20] Maya: moving on to the week's telemetry — Diego, walk the latency heatmap please.
[03:25] Diego: sure, we saw tail spikes around 95th at 1.2s for short prompts on hosted, but on the dedicated pool with KV cache warm we dropped median to 180ms and 95th to 600ms. there was one outlier at 3.9s due to a hot-evict on the cache, likely a scheduling jitter.
[03:58] Evan: that hot-evict — is that runtime or infra? could be our node sizing.
[04:05] Diego: a mix — the runtime reported a large KV eviction while another large request came in, it serialized. we recommend adding a small buffer of burst capacity and adjusting the cache TTL.
[04:18] Priya: sounds sensible. what about model compatibility across versions — if we pin v1.3 and upstream pushes v1.4 with tokenizer changes how do we handle?
[04:30] Maya: good question — our compatibility matrix flags tokenizer changes, incompatible state, and we enforce version gating. for breaking tokenizer changes we suggest a canary with 1% traffic and a shadow run to compare output diffs.
[04:46] Sonal: for security concerns, if we do canary traffic we need to ensure PII redaction and logs don't leak tokens. how are logs handled during canary?
[04:58] Diego: logs are configurable by route. for canary we recommend redacting full inputs and only logging metadata, and for the evaluation runs we ingest into a separate audit dataset with restricted access.
[05:15] Evan: moving to emergency swap playbook — can you sketch the steps we'd take if a pinned model degrades in production?
[05:24] Maya: yes — high level: detect via quality/regression alert, hit manual pause on the pinned route, switch traffic to fallback variant (soft fallback or pinned backup), run quick rollforward validation, then promote rollback or deploy hotfix. we keep a pre-warmed backup pool for instant swaps.
[05:46] Priya: how long does a swap typically take end-to-end? we need SLA numbers.
[05:52] Diego: from detection to traffic cutover we aim for <60s if backup is pre-warmed; with cold spin-up it could be minutes. the key is pre-warmed standby.
[06:06] Sonal: and how do you ensure no data leak in the swap? our concern is context KV cache that might be shared.
[06:14] Diego: caches are isolated per tenant and per model version — during swap we flush session KV and start on blank context for the backup model. we can add a final truncation step to ensure no residuals.
[06:29] Maya: scrolling to the pin-matrix that we shared — Priya first column is route, second is current pinned model, third is fallback. Priya, your team prefilled some rows, Diego will call out gaps.
[06:44] Priya: yes we filled major routes for summaries and alerts, but left medium/long form notes unpinned because we wanted advice.
[06:52] Diego: gaps I see: 1) no fallbacks set for multi-turn chat route, 2) no canary % specified for the autopilot route, 3) missing model version for legacy summarizer.
[07:10] Evan: for the autopilot route we'd like 5% canary then 20% over 48h if stable. is that doable?
[07:18] Maya: totally, the platform supports progressive rollouts with auto rollback if quality delta exceeds threshold. we just need the precise thresholds from your QA.
[07:28] Priya: QA threshold is a BLEU-like metric for us — we track factuality and hallucination rate; we'd set auto-rollback if hallucination increases by >2.5%.
[07:40] Diego: noted. we'll wire the eval metric into the rollout policy.
[07:46] Speaker 1: (brief cross talk)
[07:53] Maya: next, emergency rehearsal — propose a 30 minute rehearsal where we simulate model regression and perform the swap. who should be in that drill from Nexa?
[08:04] Priya: Priya + Evan + Sonal for security signoff, plus one data scientist.
[08:12] Maya: perfect. we'll schedule for next Tuesday, I'll send invite.
[08:20] Evan: on quantized fallbacks — if we swap to q4 to preserve latency, what's the usual quality delta we should expect for summarization?
[08:29] Diego: depends on model family — for most LLMs we've seen 3-6% degradation in ROUGE-like metrics with q4, q2 tends to be a bigger drop. that's why we recommend shadow comparisons before cutting traffic.
[08:45] Priya: would you be able to run a short shadow test for q4 today with our 200 sample prompt set?
[08:52] Diego: I can kick that off after the call — estimate 3-4 hours for initial pass.
[08:59] Maya: great — Diego will post results link.
[09:05] Evan: related infra question: if we pin multiple heavy models across routes, how does that affect GPU packing? will you autoscale?
[09:14] Diego: dedicated pool auto-scaling works off queue-length and token backlog. heavy pinned models reduce bin-packing efficiency; we recommend model tiering and using quantized variants for less critical routes.
[09:28] Priya: can Redwood recommend a pin priority ranking? we have business critical, near-real-time, and batch.
[09:35] Maya: yes, we'll propose a priority ranking template in the pin-matrix — default suggestion: business-critical pinned to FP16, near-real-time to q4 with pre-warmed standby, batch to hosted/auto.
[09:50] Sonal: also need clarification on audit logs retention for canary runs — legal asked for 7 years for some flows.
[09:59] Diego: we can configure retention per workspace; long retention adds cost, we can work with your compliance team on retention tiers.
[10:10] Priya: ok, let's go through a specific route example — route: customer-summaries-prod. current pin: summarizer-v1.3, fallback: summarizer-v1.1-quant.
[10:24] Diego: noted. gap: no canary percentage and no warm backup pool. recommended: 1% canary for 24h, warm backup pool of 2 nodes.
[10:36] Evan: what's the cost delta for warm backup? ballpark.
[10:40] Maya: small — roughly one additional node cost, but it buys <60s swap. we can run a cost estimate for your commit level.
[10:48] Priya: good. on rollbacks, how does model pinning interact with our CI/CD? can we automate pins via API?
[10:55] Diego: yes, pins are API-driven; we can add a webhook from your CI to trigger pin updates but recommend a manual approval gate for production.
[11:06] Priya: we'd like an approval gate.
[11:10] Maya: we'll include that in the rollout policy template.
[11:15] Evan: quick note — one of our concerns is tokenizer mismatches. if a model version changes tokenization, does Redwood enforce compatibility check before pinning?
[11:26] Diego: yes, compatibility checks include tokenizer hash and embedding dims; incompatible versions are flagged and can't be pinned without an explicit override.
[11:36] Sonal: perfect. another question: for auditing swap events, can we get immutable event logs?
[11:42] Maya: yes we provide immutable event logs with tamper-evident timestamps; we'll share sample schema.
[11:50] Priya: ok moving to the rehearsal plan — steps and owners?
[11:55] Maya: step 1: schedule rehearsal (Maya), step 2: pre-warm backup (Evan+Redwood), step 3: simulate regression via weight-blind file (Redwood SE), step 4: cutover and monitor (Priya), step 5: postmortem and action items.
[12:12] Evan: timeline?
[12:14] Maya: we can rehearse mid next week, 30m.
[12:18] Priya: works.
[12:22] Diego: quick tech note: we'll post the bench results to the perf sheet and mark each row with fidelity scores. also including an escape hatch to force pin revert via API.
[12:34] Maya: any blockers from security? Sonal?
[12:38] Sonal: we need the KMS flow diagram and encryption key scoping, plus a statement on log redaction during canary.
[12:45] Maya: noted — we'll post that.
[12:48] Priya: one more request — can Redwood run a 24h soak on the dedicated pool replicating our traffic pattern? we want to see sustained behavior.
[12:57] Diego: yes we can schedule a soak test — need representative traffic file. Evan can provide.
[13:04] Evan: I'll export and share a sanitized traffic replay by EOD tomorrow.
[13:09] Maya: excellent. recap and next steps then.
[13:12] (Recap)
[13:13] Maya: 1) Diego runs q4 vs fp16 shadow for the 200-sample set and posts results (due 10/06). 2) Redwood runs 12h latency/throughput sweep on ded pool and posts CSV (due 10/06). 3) Nexa provides final pin list and canary percentages (due 10/05). 4) Schedule and run 30m emergency swap rehearsal next week (Maya to schedule). 5) Security to receive KMS integration diagram and log redaction plan (due 10/07).
[13:42] Priya: thanks all, this was useful.
[13:45] Evan: thanks, see ya.
[13:47] Sonal: bye.
[13:50] Maya: thanks everyone, will follow up with invites and uploads.

End of transcript.
Redwood: run 12-hour latency + throughput sweep on dedicated pool and share CSV (due 2026-10-06)
NexaBank: provide final list of endpoints to pin and a prioritized traffic % for canary (due 2026-10-05)
Security: exchange SOC2 certs + KMS integration diagram (due 2026-10-07)
Schedule follow-up cutover rehearsal for emergency swap (30m) next week
Maya - upload pin-matrix template and sample rollout policy to shared drive by 2026-10-03
Diego - run soft-fallback bench (quantized vs fp16) and post results to spreadsheet by 2026-10-06
Evan - provision 3 node dedicated test pool and share kube access by 2026-10-04
Sonal - confirm encryption at rest KMS key scope and limitations by 2026-10-07

POC scoping: scope, benchmarks, credits & contracting

AE + SE scoped a 2-week pilot for BrightPath Health to validate latency and cost targets on their triage assistant workload. Agreed success metrics (p99 latency < 250ms for short prompts, throughput 200 concurrent users, quality gates by automated evals). Redwood to provide 2M token pilot credits, a benchmark plan, and a contracting checklist. Next steps: pricing sheet, security pack, run bench tests next week, follow up procurement timeline.
Redwood to send pilot pricing spreadsheet + 2M credits breakdown (Samir) - due 2025-06-20
SE to share benchmark harness and seed prompt set (Ethan) - due 2025-06-19
Customer to provide sample production prompts and traffic profile (Monica) - due 2025-06-20
Schedule 90-min benchmark run (Zoom + perf dashboard) - target 2025-06-24
Samir Patel | Send pilot T&Cs and credits breakdown | 2025-06-20
Ethan Li | Upload benchmark harness and instructions to shared drive (link in chat) | 2025-06-19
Monica Reyes | Export 7-day sample of request logs (anonymized) | 2025-06-20
Priya Singh | Confirm encryption and KMS requirements and share compliance checklist | 2025-06-22
Daniel Kim | Book procurement sync with legal and provide PO process doc | 2025-06-25
Meeting header: 2025-06-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 57 mins | Attendees: Samir, Ethan (Redwood); Monica, Daniel, Priya (BrightPath)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Samir from Redwood, with Ethan, our SE. Monica?
[00:06] Monica: Yep, Monica here, hi. Daniel and Priya on our side as well.
[00:10] Samir: Great. Goal today is to align on POC scope, success criteria, and the commercial pilot terms — credits, length, and how we transition to contracting.
[00:20] Monica: Sounds good. We're really focused on the triage assistant — short form prompts, a fair amount of structured output, and we need this to be fast for clinicians.
[00:30] Ethan: Cool, can you give ballpark traffic? concurrency, tokens per request, that kind of thing?
[00:34] Daniel: Sure. Peak conc around 150-200 concurrent users, average request is ~250 tokens in, 100 tokens out, but we have bursts where it goes to 600 tokens in.
[00:44] Monica: Latency sensitivity is high — user expectations are sub-second for the UI. We can tolerate a little more if quality is better but want to quantify it.
[00:55] Ethan: Helpful. For POC we typically run a focused benchmark that mirrors your 95/99th percentile flows. Suggested success metrics: p95/p99 latency targets, throughput (reqs/sec), and a quality gate measured by evals on a seed prompt set.
[01:08] Priya: From security — we need SOC2 details, audit log retention, KMS integration, and clarity on data residency. We'll need that before any production contract.
[01:18] Samir: Absolutely. We'll include the security pack link in the follow-up (notes: security-pack.pdf). KMS is supported, and for the pilot we can do encrypted at rest with customer-provided KMS in Private deployments; hosted also has enterprise KMS options.
[01:33] Monica: For the POC, we prefer hosted but isolated; we need assurance logs are accessible.
[01:38] Ethan: We can provide token-level cost and latency breakdown in the console and export logs. For the tests, we'll enable KV cache to mimic production prompt sequences — helps cut downstream token usage by heavy reuse.
[01:52] Daniel: Quick question: does Redwood's runtime handle continuous batching? In our sim the requests are short and bursty.
[01:58] Ethan: Yes, continuous batching and dynamic batching by model. We also have autoscale on Dedicated pools; for a pilot we typically run on a dedicated small pool to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[02:10] Monica: What's the recommended pilot length? We were thinking 2 weeks.
[02:15] Samir: Two weeks is standard. We'll propose a 2-week pilot with 2 million token credits. That should cover realistic bench runs and some early user testing. If you anticipate more, we can adjust.
[02:26] Monica: 2M tokens — can you break down what that translates to in cost if we go to production?
[02:31] Samir: Yes, we'll send a pilot pricing sheet and a projected production estimate scaled to your daily volume. For the pilot credits we won't bill for overage within pre-agreed limits; anything beyond we'll flag first.
[02:41] Daniel: For success criteria, we want: p99 latency < 250ms for under-300-token prompts, throughput to support 200 concurrent users with <5% error rate, and a quality pass rate of >90% on our automated eval set. Is that reasonable?
[02:57] Ethan: Those are reasonable targets for smaller open models on high-end GPUs; for larger context or longer outputs p99 will naturally increase. We should scope specific prompt buckets: short triage, long case summaries, and multi-turn follow-ups.
[03:12] Monica: Okay, let's lock those buckets. We'll provide sample prompts.
[03:18] Ethan: Great. I'll prepare a benchmark plan: test harness, seed prompts, how to run load tests, and a dashboard to visualize p50/p95/p99, token usage, and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:32] Priya: Also please document retention windows and how to redact PHI in the logs for the sample exports.
[03:39] Samir: Noted. We'll remit a redacted export guide.
[03:44] Daniel: On contracting — we have procurement timelines. Typical procurement is 6-8 weeks after pilot sign-off, but if we can get an SOW and estimate early, it shortens.
[03:55] Samir: Understood. Our standard path: pilot -> SOW + pilot results -> estimates & legal redlines -> PO. We can provide an accelerated SOW template and a contracting checklist.
[04:06] Monica: On commercial guardrails, we need clear pilot terms: credit amount, duration, what happens on overages, and what the success exit criteria are to convert to a paid pilot or contract.
[04:18] Samir: We'll send a pilot T&C doc. Proposed guardrails: 14-day pilot, 2M token credits, a single test run per day for bench ramping, overage alerting and approval flow before extra billing, and a conversion path tied to agreed success metrics.
[04:32] Monica: Works. A question about fallback: if latency breaches targets in pilot, do we have options? switch models, enable quantization, or move to Dedicated?
[04:40] Ethan: All of the above. We'll try model variants (smaller / quantized) first, enable more aggressive caching, and if needed run on Dedicated GPU pool or add burst capacity. We'll document the tradeoffs in throughput vs quality.
[04:57] Daniel: Bench plan detail — what metrics do you gather automatically vs need us to instrument?
[05:02] Ethan: Automatics: per-request latency, tokens in/out, model variant, host/region, error codes. We'll ask you to tag requests with a workload id so we can split short vs long prompts. For quality we run closed evals and WER/semantic similarity metrics and your own rubric.
[05:18] Monica: We'll create a 300-sample seed set and a 200-sample edge-case set. Hope that's enough.
[05:24] Ethan: Good starting point. For throughput simulation we'll replay anonymized logs if you can export them.
[05:31] Monica: We'll work on that.
[05:34] Samir: Commercial ask — do you have an internal threshold for pilot spend to approve pilots without a PO?
[05:40] Daniel: Under $10k usually green-lit; above that we need procurement sign-off. How does 2M credits map financially?
[05:47] Samir: Depends on model selection; as a rough estimate, 2M tokens on a mid-range open model equates to ~$3-5k list equivalent; on larger models maybe $10-12k. We'll give a model-specific estimate in the sheet.
[05:59] Priya: For compliance we need to see the SOC2 report and encryption spec before we run anything with production data. Is that in the security pack?
[06:06] Samir: Yes, SOC2 + ISO90? ISO27001 — sorry, ISO27001 — both included in the pack. Also KMS integration doc and minimum retention controls. We'll attach links.
[06:18] Monica: Fine. For the pilot data, we can anonymize the sample logs.
[06:22] Ethan: Perfect. Plan for next week: Ethan will kick off the benchmark harness and share instructions; Samir will send the pricing and pilot T&Cs; Monica to share sample prompts and anonymized logs by Friday. We'll then run a 48-hour warmup and a 24-48 hour soak + targeted p99 runs.
[06:38] Daniel: Timeline sounds good. Procurement sync planned for week after pilot end.
[06:44] Samir: If pilot meets success metrics we can draft SOW and provide a committed reserved capacity pricing option for Dedicated or a volume-based hosted discount.
[06:53] Monica: On measurement for quality, we'll have the automated eval, plus a small human review sample for edge cases.
[06:59] Ethan: Recommended: 95% automated pass + manual review under 5% failure for edgecases.
[07:06] Priya: Anything about data residency? We need EU data to land in Frankfurt region for PHI, is that supported?
[07:12] Ethan: We support regional routing in hosted and Private for on-prem. For EU region we can pin instances to eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 equivalents; detail in the deployment docs.
[07:22] Monica: Great. Any competitors you compared this against in pilot pricing?
[07:27] Samir: Customers often benchmark Anthropic and OpenAI for quality vs cost, and AWS SageMaker for self-hosted controls. We'll include competitor notes.
[07:36] Daniel: Ok. Mechanically, how do we kick off the bench run? Who runs it?
[07:40] Ethan: We provide the harness and runbooks. We typically run the load from Redwood infra to remove local network variables, but we can also run from your infra if you prefer. For latency-sensitive tests, run from your region to get realistic numbers.
[07:53] Monica: We'll probably want Redwood to run the heavy tests and we will run a small set locally to sanity-check.
[07:59] Samir: Fine. I'll schedule a 90-min run/walkthrough on 2025-06-24 to watch the first bench results live.
[08:07] Monica: Works. One final ask — can we get a binding commitment on the pilot credits not being used for any other customer?
[08:13] Samir: Pilot credits are allocated to your account and not shared; we'll put the allocation in writing in the T&C.
[08:21] Daniel: What about SLA during pilot?
[08:24] Ethan: For pilots we don't expose enterprise SLA, but we commit to reasonable availability for the test and active engineering support. For production we can discuss SLA tiers in the SOW.
[08:36] Priya: Ok, we'll review the security pack and get back with any gaps.
[08:40] Samir: Perfect. To recap: 14-day pilot, 2M token credits, benchmark plan, security pack, and a procurement checklist. Follow-ups due next week.
[08:51] Monica: Thanks everyone.
[08:53] Daniel: Thanks.
[08:55] Samir: Thanks, end call.
